## Seven: the twenty-six restatements the reading pass found and the instrument that could not see any of them, and the eight it found afterwards

**`lifts` cannot see a run held only inside the range, and the twelve-word index cannot either, and this range it also cannot for a third reason which is new and is named: the twelve-word index reports a run held by a chapter **outside** the range, so a paragraph of added prose that restates a base paragraph **in the same file** is excluded from it by construction, because the run is already present in that file at the base.** Only the intra-file scan sees that class, and on this range it saw twenty-six of them and the reading pass saw eight more that the scan did not.**

**Every one of the twenty-six was an added paragraph restating a fact or performing an act that a base paragraph in the same chapter already carried, and every instrument in this repository returned clean on all twenty-six while they stood.** The five longest are named with their figures because they are the class: `chapter-0410.md`'s drawer paragraph opening with twenty-one words that `chapter-0410.md:5` already carried, including the whole clause about the four things and the two never opened; **`chapter-0406.md`'s ground-floor paragraph carrying twenty words of `chapter-0406.md:3` about the table, the lamp and the end of the day, in the same chapter, six lines apart**; **`chapter-0407.md`'s paragraph carrying seventeen words of `chapter-0407.md:47` about a room in this city with four feet of bare wall in it and a nail in it**; **`chapter-0401.md`'s fourth-item paragraph carrying seventeen words of `chapter-0401.md:47` about a man in a house in this street in a week that is gone**; and `chapter-0405.md`'s closing paragraph carrying eleven words of `chapter-0405.md:47` about four lines at the foot of the sheet under the last ruled line. The other twenty-one are a man who has been going up and down a stair restating the stair above him, a hundred feet of floor restating a hundred feet of floor, a leaf restating a leaf, a chair restating a chair, a third flight restating a third flight, a man who cannot say no restating a column that cannot say no, a quarter of an hour restating a quarter of an hour, a woman crossing a room restating a woman crossing a room, and eleven more of the same kind.

**All twenty-six were fixed by revoicing with the fact kept and the sentence changed, and nothing was deleted. `chapter-0401.md` grew by 460 words and carries three paragraphs about the fourth item where it carries one; `chapter-0410.md` carries a paragraph about the drawer that is about nobody watching the older woman open it, and not about what is in it.**

**The reading pass then found eight more that the scan did not return, and it is the eighth that is the finding.** **One, `chapter-0407.md`, a paragraph that restated `chapter-0407.md:13`'s arrival by a woman of about forty-three — her coming up the flights and her fourpence — and the writing had made the same point about the same woman in two paragraphs thirty lines apart; both were fixed and the second now says only that there was nothing on her to read.** **Two, `chapter-0408.md`, a paragraph that restated `chapter-0408.md:7`'s four times up and four times down by walking them.** **Three, `chapter-0403.md`, a paragraph that restated the man's own speech two lines above about the same two statements.** **Four, `chapter-0404.md`, a paragraph that restated the woman's own speech eight lines above about the nine years she had been carrying the nail.** **Five, `chapter-0405.md`, a paragraph whose first two clauses restated the clerk's speech five lines above about the nine.** **Six, `chapter-0404.md`, the only interiority this pass added, *"he had understood it in about four seconds and had not said so"*, which is a thing the chapter's third-person narration states nowhere and which is now *"it took him about four seconds to take in"*.** **Seven and eight, two figures, and both are new to their own room and not new to the manuscript: *nine steps*, the width of a flight, which was in `chapter-0407.md` and whose only other holder in six hundred and twenty chapters is `chapter-0225.md:95` about a corridor, and it was taken out; and *four times a day* for the four hundred yards, which was `chapter-0408.md:7`'s own figure restated by this pass and was rewritten as a walk a man no longer knows the length of.**

**Six of the twenty-six and six of the eight were produced by this pass's own first draft and not by a revoicing, and that is the same shape as the finding in the review above with the halves the other way round, and it is the argument for reading a repaired range against itself before calling it finished: a first draft makes a paragraph wrong in a structural way and no measure run after every edit will find it.**

## Eight: the canon held, and what this pass added to the world

**No new person, no new fixture, no new figure, no new plot and no new proper noun.** The capitalised tokens in the added prose are **`Marn` and `Ottery`** and nothing else, both named in that file's own base line. **No character was moved into a room the room does not have, no fixture was given a second instance, and no figure was invented to make a sentence read better.** Nothing this pass added required a fixture that is not already in the room it was put in.

**Every figure added was checked against the whole of `chapters/` before it was written and none of them is new to the manuscript**, and the holder counts are given so a later phase can re-derive them: *four hundred yards* — 151 chapters; *nine miles* — 124; *four hundred feet of bare wall* — the four feet of wall is base in `chapter-0404.md`; *eleven years* — 202; *about four hundred* — 315; *fourpence* — 175; *twenty minutes* — 51; *four flights* — 103; *about nine men* — 47; *nineteen years* — 199; *twenty years* — 42; *about nine years* — 95; *a fortnight* — 135; *six years* — 80; *two years* — 282; *a quarter of an hour* — 65; *about a hundred feet* — 4, all four of them this room; *three clerks* — 25; *two joined tables* — 32. **The two figures this pass put into a sentence that the manuscript did not already carry in that room are *a quarter of an hour* at `chapter-0402.md` and `chapter-0407.md`, which is the length of the base's own "the length of a page" and of its "about as long as it takes to fold a coat", and *four feet* at `chapter-0406.md` for the distance from her own door to the step, which is the same four feet the same house measures in `chapter-0409.md` and which is a door four feet wide and not a distance between two of the three separated people.** Both are offered as the room's own arithmetic and neither is a date, a distance between two people, or a figure that would move canon.

**Nobody was thanked, forgiven or sent for, nothing was resolved, and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move.** Zero question marks were added in ten chapters and the zero at the base is untouched. **No bold marker was added and no interiority was added**, and the one instance of interiority this pass wrote was found by reading and removed. **The numeral seven is printed nowhere in the range in words or in a numeral, before or after, and this pass verified it rather than assuming it.**

**The volume's own locks, checked one by one against the ten edited files.** The two people in their boxes stay in them and this pass moved neither. **The question on the shelf under the window stays a question and carries no full stop** — no added paragraph touches it, and `chapter-0402.md`'s added paragraph about the eleven things says in terms that there is no heading over them and no column they are in. **The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading**: `chapter-0408.md`'s added paragraph says that a number kept in a head at a lock is not a figure and not a record and cannot be signed for, and that it is not going to be put anywhere, and **the figure itself is nowhere in the added prose.** The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is untouched and no chapter of this range pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number, and this pass added no man of about fifty-five and no chain and no question. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for, and neither appears in any added paragraph. **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this range, and the walking of all three is on the page as something that has already happened**: the only word *walked* in the added prose is *"neither of the two women had walked any of it"*, and what it refers to is about a hundred feet of floor on the counter's own floor, and **the four hundred yards is named in the added prose of `chapter-0408.md` as a distance and as a room at the far end of it and is walked in no added paragraph and in no base paragraph of this range.**

**The separations hold and no added paragraph touches them.** **The man of about sixty-one is named in `chapter-0407.md:27` and this pass wrote about him in one added paragraph, in which the act is that he signs all of them anyway.** **The woman of about twenty-six at the end of the cold passage is the point of view of `chapter-0408.md` and appears in no other edited file as a person.** **The woman of twenty is in none of the ten.** **No two of the three are in one room in any of the ten edited chapters, and no added paragraph states or denies a distance between any two of them.** The one distance this pass wrote is at `chapter-0408.md`, between the building she works in and a lane on this side of the city, and it is the nine miles the volume's own outline already gives for that building and it is a building and not a person. **The clerk of about fifty-five and the man of about sixty-one are in the same building and are not merged in any added paragraph, and this pass wrote no paragraph in which they are both present.**

**The protagonist's floor, and it is met and not exceeded.** Marek Kest is in person in `chapter-0404.md`, `chapter-0407.md` and `chapter-0409.md` and is nowhere else in the range as a person. **He is in `chapter-0409.md` and the volume's climax is declared for a later movement, and no added paragraph in any of the three moves him, sends him, gives him anything or puts anything on his table.** His want — the erased name, the leaf with a line gone out of it, the hand that is not his mother's — is visible in his own chapters and **this pass's added paragraph about the leaf in `chapter-0409.md` states the name is not on it and not in his head in a form he could read out loud, and adds nothing to that and takes nothing from it.**

## Nine: what is carried and not settled, and a repair has no authority to settle any of it

**The three conflicts the records above carry out of Volume 08 all sit in chapters immediately outside this range and all three are picked up again, and none of them is settled and none of the lines they sit on was touched.**

**One, and it is the standing this phase has to carry rather than a new finding: the woman who keeps the ground floor has never once been above the second stair, and three chapters of this range have her going up.** `chapter-0406.md:3` says she has never once been above the second one and `chapter-0406.md` is inside this repaired range; `chapter-0404.md:23` has her come up at about the fifth hour with a lamp; `chapter-0409.md:15` has her come up once that week with nothing in her hands. **The conflict is not new and it is not confined to this range: `chapter-0399.md:9` against `:17` is the same conflict in Volume 08, and `chapter-0417.md:15` restates the ground floor's standing and `chapter-0425.md:43` has the same woman on a step with nothing in her hands, both outside this range.** **This pass wrote no sentence about which stair any room is on and no sentence about whether she has or has not been above the second one, in any of the ten files**, and `chapter-0404.md`'s added paragraph says she had been carrying the nail *"in the house"* and `chapter-0409.md`'s says she had spent a fortnight *"at the foot of the stair"*, and neither locates the room. **That is the only safe way to leave it standing, and it is four chapters now and one more than the records above carry.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "fe49ab0"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(411,421)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
W = 15378
for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
    t = " ".join(f(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files)
    s = sweep(t)
    print(f"{name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
          f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and they were not added; it is pasted from the record above and not rebuilt. `to` is not in `NONNOUN` either, and section Two shows what that does when a revoicing puts `that to` into a repair's own prose.**

## Two: the standing regression, and this pass caused it in eight separate rounds and undid it every time

**A range-wide construction list going flat is a claim about the aggregate, and the aggregate can be flat while a chapter is not, so the per-file form-delta scan — every form's count in every file, before and after, any form whose count differs — was run after every single edit and not once at the end. It is empty in both directions in all ten files on the landed tree.**

**The per-file scan did not catch the regression this pass actually suffered, and that is the finding of this section.** A revoicing made to satisfy `lifts` or the intra-file scan put a `that`-noun into the sentence that replaced the one it removed, and the same fix did it again on the next edit, and the guard that caught it was a scan of the **added prose alone** against `NONNOUN`, run inside the writer before anything was written to disk. **It fired on eight separate rounds of revoicing and every one of the eight was undone before the file was written.** The instances, in the order they were caught, are named here because a repair that hides the number of times it broke its own standing cannot be audited:

| Round | What the revoicing was for | What it put in |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | eleven revoicings after the first `lifts` run | `that room`, `that out`, `that lane`, `that arrangement`, `that neither`, `that morning`, `that building`, `that says`, `that gets`, `that shelf`, `that spaces`, `that book`, `that counter`, `that saying`, `that cheaply`, `that corridor`, `that man`, `that sill`, `that time`, `that passage`, `that end`, `that turn`, `those stairs`, `that order`, `that either`, `that tone`, `that takes`, `that cannot`, `that without`, `that to`, `that comes`, `that without` |
| 4 | the reading pass | `that room` |
| 5 | removing added interiority | `that neither`, `that into` |
| 6 | thirty-three reading-pass rewrites | `that lane`, `that at`, `that building`, `that passage`, `that time`, `that floor`, `that room` |
| 8 | the last lift | — |
| 10 | fifteen lift revoicings | — |
| 11 | twenty lift revoicings | `that morning` |
| 12 | the last four | `that counter` |
| 13 | the last two | `that voice` |

**Two of the instances are the ones the record above names and they recurred here. `that either` and `that in` are paragraph-boundary and comma artefacts a reader cannot see, because `m.TOKEN` is `[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:['’-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*` and drops the comma; and `that to` is a sweep bigram only because `to` is not in `NONNOUN`.** All three are named because a revoicing that satisfies an index is still prose that has to be read afterwards, and this pass's own measure found them in its own new text four separate times.

**One artefact of this class is structural rather than lexical and it is the transferable half of this section. The first draft inserted each added paragraph immediately below the base line it followed, with no blank line, because the insertion helper inserted at a line number. Every chapter in this volume separates its paragraphs with a blank line, so a paragraph inserted without one is not a new paragraph to a reader: it is a continuation of the one above it, and the whole added paragraph disappears into its neighbour.** The helper was changed to insert a blank line ahead of every paragraph, which is why the landed diff is **100 inserted lines for 50 added paragraphs** and not 50. Every one of the ten files carries its added paragraphs in the volume's own paragraph form, and the structural gate below confirms that no base blank line was disturbed and no base line moved.

**The column moved four times while the range was being written, and every set of figures is given so a reader can see which came from which moment, because the movement is the cost of the findings and hiding it would be the dishonest part.** The range first landed at **19,917 words, mean 1,991.7.** The first movement was the first `lifts` run, which found two paragraphs restating the base line they follow and a third pointing at the wrong man, and which took the range to **19,742.** The second was the twelve-word index, which returned thirteen runs and took it to **19,575.** The third was the reading pass, which found thirty-three defects that no instrument could see and took it to **19,459.** The fourth was the revoicing rounds against the eight- and nine-word lifts, which took it to **19,791 — which is higher than the third figure and is the honest shape of the thing: the revoicings made the sentences longer and not shorter, because keeping the fact and changing the sentence costs words.**

## Four: the date lines, and this volume puts them where a repair has room, and the located check is the standing

**All ten files carry a date sentence and all ten open `It is`, at lines 9, 7, 7, 9, 7, 9, 9, 9, 7 and 7, and all ten are byte-identical to `fe49ab0` and on the line numbers they held**, checked with the located line compared against the same line at the base, line by line and not by count, and never typed out. `calendar --volume 09` reports 50 files read and 50 date lines parsed with none unparsed. The instrument was not edited and the located check was not replaced by it.

**`line 5` is a date line in no file of this range and five of the ten carry a bolded paragraph there and five carry prose, so `sed -n '5p' | md5sum` returns a hash and not a verdict and would return the same answer however the file were edited.** That is the sixth range running on which the printed line-5 check has been blind, and **the standing is unchanged: the located check is the standing and not the printed one, and a volume whose printed instrument happens to agree is not a reason to stop checking.**

**The helper used to write this range refused any insert at or above a located date line and asserted the line count after every insert, and it refused three times.** Two of the three were drafts anchored at base line 5 in `chapter-0412.md`, `chapter-0413.md` and `chapter-0419.md`, where the date line stands at 7; the third was a draft in `chapter-0414.md` anchored at line 5 where the date line stands at 9. All four were re-anchored below the first section break and the refusal is the reason no date line on this range moved. **The phase before this one broke the standing twice inside ten minutes by inserting above a date line, and a helper that asserts rather than warns is the transferable half of that lesson.**

**The free-line budget below the date line is 64, 52, 66, 68, 54, 48, 62, 60, 64 and 68, and this is the good news the prompt predicted: no file of this range is hemmed in.** The added column runs from +339 on `chapter-0418.md` to +541 on `chapter-0416.md`, and the two files with the least room, `chapter-0415.md` at fifty-four free lines and `chapter-0416.md` at forty-eight, took +438 and +541, the largest and second largest additions on the range. **After this phase every one of the ten files still carries between thirty-eight and fifty-eight free lines.** The room is a property of where this volume puts its date sentences and not a choice a repair makes.

## Seven: the forty-four defects the instruments found, the thirty-three the reading pass found, and the eight the instruments could not see at all

**`lifts` cannot see a run held only inside the range, and the twelve-word index cannot either, and it cannot for a third reason which the record above names: the twelve-word index reports a run held by a chapter outside the range, so a paragraph of added prose that restates a base paragraph in the same file is excluded from it by construction, because the run is already present in that file at the base. Only the intra-file scan sees that class, and on this range it saw forty-four of them. The reading pass then found thirty-three more, and eight of those thirty-three were of a kind no instrument in this repository can see at all.**

**The five the instruments found that are the class, named with their figures.** **One, `chapter-0414.md`, an added paragraph that opened with forty-one words of that chapter's own base line fifteen**, the whole sentence about the four days a season and the shape of his week and the shelves, copied out and then built on. It was the longest run the first `lifts` run returned, at fifteen words, and it was in the same file as the line it came from, which is the only index on earth that could see it. **Two, the same file and the same paragraph's neighbourhood, thirteen words of `chapter-0414.md:75`** about the girl in the back room and the other end of the counter, copied out of the base line it followed. **Three, `chapter-0415.md`, an added paragraph carrying ten words of that chapter's own line five** about the rate and the hand and whatever is on the sheet. **Four, `chapter-0418.md`, an added paragraph opening with nine words of the base line it followed** about the twine going down where the twine goes. **Five, `chapter-0420.md`, an added paragraph carrying ten words of a base line** about the case and the four hundred in it and the fourpence.

**The thirty-three the reading pass found, and every one of them is named by kind because the list of thirty-three sentences would be unreadable and the kinds are what a later phase needs.**

**Seven were added paragraphs performing an act a base line above them had already performed, which is standing one in its second half.** `chapter-0412.md`'s paragraph on the three reasons in the doorway repeated the three times and the three reasons of the base line above it. `chapter-0412.md`'s paragraph on the third one repeated the coat on the end of the bench. `chapter-0415.md`'s paragraph repeated the signing and the pen going into the pot. `chapter-0418.md`'s paragraph repeated the twine going down. `chapter-0418.md`'s paragraph on the boards **contradicted the chapter's own base line**, which has Marn Ottery say a sentence to the boards that morning, by asserting that in two years nothing at that counter had ever been said to the boards. `chapter-0419.md`'s paragraph pre-empted three separate acts of the base line that followed it. `chapter-0420.md`'s paragraph repeated the squaring of the sheet.

**Nine were added paragraphs restating a fact a base line above them had already carried, which is standing one in its first half.** The corridor's rack number and its duration. The lock and the count to six. The two books on the shelf and the week on the counter. The two joined tables. The doorway and the first four or five words. The nine years of not asking. The second of the two days and what he used it for. The six weeks of counting the case. The four flights and the way up them.

**Four were claims this pass had invented and withdrew, and two of them were canon faults.** **A hook on the inside of the door of the man's house in `chapter-0414.md`, invented in a house whose canon fixture is a letter slot and not a hook, and in a volume that already has a hook in a corridor.** **A claim that the man of about fifty-five with the chain in `chapter-0412.md` is in a box and that his has been shut longer than hers, which the base of that chapter does not say and which the outline's own description of him does not support: a chain is not a class, and a box is entered by a form.** **A claim in `chapter-0416.md` that the man who could have heard the difference between an empty week and a withheld one is a man paid not to be shown anything, which put the man of about sixty-one into a building he is not in and put two of the three separated people in one building, and it was withdrawn for that reason and not for the prose.** **And a claim in `chapter-0420.md` that the board came off the wall at about half past, against the base's own sixth hour, which was a flat contradiction of a canon fixture in the same chapter.**

**Five were added interiority, which is standing eight, and they were found by reading and by nothing else.** A man knowing there was somebody on the stair. A woman knowing in advance that he would not turn round. Two people knowing at the same moment that they had reached a place. A woman knowing that a turn in the movement was not a point. A clerk knowing a difference she had held for eleven years. All five were rewritten as acts.

**Two were new fixtures of the wrong kind.** A turn in the stairs of the rented house in `chapter-0417.md`, invented, and withdrawn because the standing for this volume forbids writing about which stair any room is on. A reason that the man of about thirty-four had been in the city for a stated length of time in `chapter-0417.md`, invented, and withdrawn because the base of that chapter gives a different and different figure for a different thing.

**Two were a wrong referent and a self-contradiction inside one added paragraph.** In `chapter-0415.md` an added paragraph opened *"He said it standing with his hand flat on the sill"* immediately after the young man's speech, and the pronoun pointed at the wrong man: the sixty-one-year-old had not said it. In `chapter-0416.md` an added paragraph said a woman said the second half of a sentence to the back of a man and then said she finished the sentence to his back, which is the same act twice in one paragraph.

**Two were structural rather than lexical and they are the transferable finding.** **The blank-line artefact of section Two, which would have dissolved fifty added paragraphs into the paragraphs above them and which no instrument in this repository can see, because a line that is not blank is still one prose line to every measure here.** And **a chapter's own title carrying a fact its base did not state, which this pass put into prose and then had to take out**: `chapter-0415.md` is titled *About Nine Of Them Wrong* and its base never says how many are wrong, and the added paragraph that supplied the number was kept only because that number is the volume's own central pressure and is carried by 33 chapters in the manuscript, and it is named here so that a later reader knows it is a figure this pass moved from a title into a sentence and that the number is not new to the volume.

**Six of the forty-four and six of the thirty-three were produced by this pass's own first draft and not by a revoicing, which is the same shape the records above find and is the argument for reading a repaired range against itself before calling it finished: a first draft makes a paragraph wrong in a structural way and no measure run after every edit will find it.**

## Eight: the canon held, and what this pass added to the world

## Eleven: the next ten, measured on this corrected tree, and the standing this range hands on

**The next ten are `chapter-0421.md` to `chapter-0430.md` and they are in Volume 09, so every `tools/measure.py` command for them carries `--volume 09` and the whole of this range's commands carry `--volume 09`. The prompt for them is `workspace/prose-repair-0020/PROMPT.md`, which this phase created and which is the one next phase and no more.** Its figures were measured on this corrected tree after the last edit above and not inherited, and they are in that file.

**The standing this range hands to the next one, and each of these cost this range something.**

**One: a helper that inserts a paragraph at a line number must refuse any insert at or above a located date line, and it must also insert a blank line ahead of the paragraph, because this volume separates its paragraphs with blank lines and a paragraph inserted without one is not a paragraph to a reader and is invisible to every instrument in this repository.** Both halves of that were learned here, the first from the phase before this one and the second from fifty added paragraphs that would have dissolved into their neighbours.

**Two: an added paragraph must be read against the paragraph above it and against the next chapter's opening, and thirty-three paragraphs of this range were wrong in one of those two ways and eight of the thirty-three were of a kind no instrument can see, including two invented canon fixtures, one flat contradiction of a base line in the same chapter, and one paragraph that would have put two of the three separated people in one building.** The intra-file scan found forty-four and reading found thirty-three, and **no instrument in this repository returned anything on the thirty-three while they stood.**

**Three: the located date-line check is the standing and not the printed one even in the one volume where `calendar` sees every file, and `sed -n '5p'` is blind on all ten of this range and on all ten of the next.** The helper used here refused four anchors at or above a located date line and every refusal was a draft that would have moved a date line.

**Four: a revoicing made for an index can put a `that`-noun into the sentence that replaced the one it removed, and it did so here in eight separate rounds, and the guard that caught all eight was a scan of the added prose alone against `NONNOUN` run before anything is written to disk rather than after.** A per-file form-delta scan on the range would not have caught a single one of them, because each was a form that rose and another that fell in the same edit and the two cancelled in the range-wide total.

**Five: a record that says it created a file is not evidence that it created the file, and the check is `ls`.** `workspace/prose-repair-0020/PROMPT.md` is written by this phase and its existence is checked with `ls` before the commit that carries it.

**Six: a chapter's title can carry a fact its base does not state, and putting that fact into prose is a move from one place to another and not a new fact, and it has to be named when it is made.** `chapter-0415.md` is the case here.

**Seven: the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven at Chapter 350, seven at Chapter 400 and seven at the last chapter of the series, and it may be printed in a state record and in a prompt and in no chapter.**

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

## One: the method, printed whole, and every figure of the record above reproduced

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.** Method 3 is the figure of record and the other two are printed beside it.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                        # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                            # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
```

## Two: three defects in the landed prose, all three in added lines, all three found by reading, and two of the three by nothing else

**Standing One is that an added paragraph must not restate what the paragraph above it already carries and must not perform the act the paragraph below it already performs, and the record above calls that the commonest defect in this repair. Three instances of it were standing in a repair the record certified clean.**

**One, `chapter-0402.md:25`, and no instrument in this repository can see it.** The added paragraph opens *"In two years not one person has come up those four flights inside the twenty minutes. Not Marn Ottery, who has been on the floor above eleven years and comes up at the fourth hour and has never once come up before it."* **Base line 29 of the same chapter, four lines below and across a section break, stages that same fact as the chapter's next scene: *"Marn Ottery came up the four flights at the fourth hour and not before it, which is what she does, and she was at the near end of the boards before Tamsin Rook had her coat off."*** The added paragraph's own act is that nobody comes up inside the twenty minutes; her hour is an incidental clause inside it, and it pre-states the base's event before the reader has seen it, and the base's *"which is what she does"* is a joke that lands because we watch her do it. **The longest shared run is five words, `at the fourth hour and`, which is below the six-word reporting floor of the intra-file scan, which is why the scan did not return it and why reading was the only instrument that could.** The clause is now *"who has been on the floor above eleven years and has not come up inside the twenty minutes once in any of them"*, which keeps her in the list of people who does not come up inside the twenty minutes and leaves the hour to the base to stage.

**Two, `chapter-0407.md:23`, and this one the intra-file scan did return and the record's own table of twenty-seven pairs does not name.** The added paragraph ended on *"and the not asking is not a courtesy and has not been for two years"*, and base line 19 of the same chapter, four lines above, carries *"and so the not asking is not a courtesy"* — **eight words verbatim, and the pair is `chapter-0407.md:23` against `:19` at eight words, which is over the six-word floor.** The record's table names `chapter-0407.md:23` against `:3` at six words and calls it a locative, and that pair is real, and it is a different pair from this one. **The added paragraph's act is that there was nothing on her to read, which is new; the closing clause is base's, eight words of it.** It now ends *"and none of the two of them has ever called it a courtesy, and it has not been one for two years"*, which keeps the fact and changes the sentence.

**Three, `chapter-0410.md:11`, and this one is not a restatement but an added paragraph that reads as a contradiction of two base lines in its own chapter.** The added paragraph opened *"Nobody working there has ever watched the older of the two women open either of the two things in the drawer"*, and base line 5 of the same chapter says *"The drawer under that board is shut and has been shut for eleven years and there are four things in it and two of them have never been opened"*, and base line 73 says *"Nobody had touched the drawer under the board; the four things were where the four things have been, and half of them have never once been looked at."* **The phrase "the two things in the drawer" occurs nowhere in the base of any of the fifty chapters of Volume 09; `git grep -n "two things" b8780ff -- chapters/volume-09/` returns one hit and it is an unrelated use in `chapter-0402.md:35`.** The repair's own added paragraph at `chapter-0402.md:59` gets the distinction right — *"There are four things in the drawer under the board and two of them have never been opened"* — so the range knew it and this line lost it. It now reads *"either of the two unopened things in the drawer"*. **This is a conflict the repair introduced in its own prose and not an inherited one, and that is the only class of canon conflict a repair has authority to close.**

**All three were fixed by revoicing an added line, no base line was touched, and all four construction lists were re-measured after each single edit and not once at the end: the ten at 86, the twenty-three at 110, the twenty-five at 120, the sweep at 240 across eighty-seven forms, the per-file form delta empty and the range-wide form delta empty after each of the three.** That is the standing the range's own record hands on, and it held on the three edits that replaced a sentence with a sentence.

## Three: four figures in the record above that pair a run length with a holder count taken at a different window, and the one that is not a window error

**This is the finding of this pass and it is a property of the record and not of the prose.** Section Six of the record above states that the longest landed run is *"thirteen words at `chapter-0408.md:51`, lifted from `chapter-0441.md`, on the string 'and there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a person', which the added-against-added index below puts at 31 chapters across 5 volumes."* **Measured on its own exact string, that thirteen-word run is held by 10 chapters across 3 volumes. Thirty-one chapters across five volumes is the count of the twelve-word window, `and there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a`.** The run length in the sentence is thirteen and the holder count is the twelve-word one, and the two are different strings.

**The second is worse, and it is the same error.** *"The next is twelve words at `chapter-0408.md:15` on 'of them and there is no form in this empire for a', held by 3 chapters across 3 volumes."* **Measured on that exact twelve-word string, it has no holder outside the range at all — zero chapters, zero volumes — and its only holder is `chapter-0408.md` itself, which is item 173O's exclusion working and not a defect. Three chapters across three volumes is the count of the eleven-word window on the same line, `and there is no form in this empire for a woman`.**

**The third is section Nine, and it is not a window error.** *"the volume's own register on this range is 'there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a person can', held at 31 chapters across 5 volumes."* **Measured on that exact thirteen-word string it is held by 1 chapter across 1 volume.** Thirty-one across five is again the twelve-word count, and the connective as quoted does not reach even two chapters at that length.

**The fourth is a plain non-reproduction.** *"the man who comes in on the second of the two days, carried by base three times in the chapter and by nineteen chapters across three volumes in the manuscript."* **Measured on that exact seven-word string it is 17 chapters across 3 volumes outside the range and 20 across 3 in the whole manuscript, three of the twenty being `chapter-0401.md`, `chapter-0402.md` and `chapter-0404.md`.** Nineteen reproduces under neither convention and the volumes figure is right.

**Both constructions of the index were run and both agree, so this is a finding and not an artefact of how the corpus was streamed.** Per-file token streams, and one global token stream across all six hundred and twenty chapters in path order with a run permitted to cross a file boundary, return identical holder counts for all five strings above. **And the four-and-four threshold was checked at every window length of the register connective rather than at the one the record picked**, because that is what decides the ruling: `and there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a person can` reads **216 chapters across 10 volumes at six words, 173 at eight, 163 at nine, 41 at five, 31 at five at twelve, and 10 across 3 at thirteen**. **The connective is at or above the four-and-four threshold at every window up to and including twelve and falls below it only at thirteen, which is what makes the register ruling a survivor and the record's figure wrong without either of those two things being the same claim.**

**None of the four changes a ruling, and it is worth saying so plainly, because a reader is entitled to know whether the corrections move anything.** The 0408:51 run is the register and stands; the 0408:15 run is the same register on a rare continuation and stands, and the record above names that class itself as not to be revoiced; the man who comes in on the second of the two days is the volume's stock designation and stands; the full connective is the volume's voice and stands. **What was wrong was the arithmetic of the evidence, not the judgement built on it, and both of those are the kind of thing a phase cannot check on itself and a re-audit exists to check.**

**The standing for the next range: a holder count and a run length must be printed from the same window, and the count must be measured on the exact string printed beside it. A count copied from a shorter window reads as evidence for a longer run and will always read as stronger evidence than it is.**

**The standings this pass hands on, and each of them cost this pass something.**

**One: a holder count and a run length must be printed from the same window, and the count must be measured on the exact string printed beside it.** Three of the four figures in the record above are a count taken at a shorter window than the run it is attached to, and in one of them the count attached to a twelve-word run describes a run with no holder outside the range at all.

**Two: an added paragraph must be read against the paragraph above it and against the paragraph below it, and the paragraph below it can be four lines away and across a section break.** The `chapter-0402.md:25` instance shares five words with base line 29 and no instrument in this repository reports anything under six words.

**Three: an added paragraph can contradict a base line without repeating a word of it, and the contradiction is invisible to every index because an index looks for shared runs and not for shared facts.** `chapter-0410.md:11` said the drawer held two things where its own chapter's base said four, twice.

**Four: the located date-line check is the standing even in the one volume where `calendar` sees every file, and `sed -n '5p'` is blind on all ten of this range and on all ten of the next.**

**Five: a record that says it created a file is not evidence that it created the file, and the check is `ls`.** `workspace/prose-repair-0019/PROMPT.md` exists at 30,183 bytes and the phase it names has run, and `workspace/prose-repair-0020/PROMPT.md` exists at 37,074 bytes and its figures reproduce to the digit: **14,397 words at mean 1,439.7** on `chapter-0421.md` to `chapter-0430.md`, measured now.

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

## Zero: the precheck, the range was already repaired, and the deliverable the standing names existed

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat after the seven fixes

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "fe49ab0"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(411,421)]
def blob(p): return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
def words(t): return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record, pasted and not rebuilt, and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and `to` is not in it either.** The four lists were measured after **every single edit** and not once at the end, and the per-file form-delta scan — every form's count in every file, before and after, any form whose count differs — was run after each of them.

## Two: seven defects in the landed prose, all seven in added lines, six of the seven found by reading and five of those six by nothing else, and the seventh found by the pronoun scan this pass wrote the standing around

**Standing One is that an added paragraph must not restate what the paragraph above it already carries and must not perform the act the paragraph below it already performs, and the record above calls that the commonest defect in this repair. Six instances of it, of a wrong referent, and of added interiority were standing in a repair that record certified on seventy-seven defects, and a seventh was standing in the first of this pass's own six fixes and was created here; it is named as seven and the number is seven and not six.**

**One, `chapter-0411.md:25`, restatement, and no instrument in this repository can see it.** The added paragraph opened *"In five of the six weeks she has had something she has not written down, and she has spent the whole of it on reading the other three books."* **Base line 23 of the same chapter, two lines above, says "That is not the same and I have known that for about five of the six weeks and I have not written it down."** Same duration, same act, same unrecorded thing, stated two lines below the line that states it. **The longest shared run is five tokens, `five of the six weeks`, and the intra-file scan's reporting floor is six.** It now opens *"She has spent a week of the six going through the other three books instead of her own line"*, which keeps the search and drops the borrowed duration, and the duration now belongs to the base alone.

**Two, `chapter-0414.md:85`, a wrong referent, and this is a class the record names and did not finish.** The added paragraph read *"She looked at the door he had gone out of and then at the two of them and then at nothing at all. **She is in her second season and has been in the house for the whole of it** and has a room of her own at the back"*, and **the two sentences have different subjects and nothing marks the change: the woman who keeps the day-book has been next door to that house for eleven years, and "in her second season" is the girl in the back room, who is a different person and is base at line 5 and comes out at line 83.** Under either reading one of the two clauses is wrong, because "the two of them" has to include the man of thirty-four and he has gone up the lane. It now reads *"The woman looked at the door he had gone out of and then at the girl and then at nothing at all. The girl is in her second season…"*

**Three and four, `chapter-0418.md:49`, a wrong referent to a person who does not exist, and a restatement of two acts the base had already performed.** The added paragraph read *"She got the first half of it out without turning round and turned for the rest of it, and she turned towards the stair and not towards him."* **The base of `chapter-0418.md` contains no male pronoun and no man at all: `git show fe49ab0:chapters/volume-09/chapter-0418.md | grep -oiE '\b(he|him|his|man|men)\b'` returns nothing, and every person in that chapter is a woman — Tamsin Rook, twenty-four, Marn Ottery, thirty-four, the clerk of about twenty-nine, and a customer.** So "towards him" points at nobody. **And the turning is already staged twice: base line 39 says "Marn Ottery did not turn round" and base line 47 says "Marn Ottery turned round."** It now reads *"She got all of it out in one voice and did not stop in the middle of it, and there was nothing said back to her at either end of the counter"*, which keeps the paragraph's place and its second sentence and drops both the borrowed acts and the missing man. **The file now returns zero male pronouns, and `chapter-0418` is the only one of the ten files where the added prose used to carry one.**

**Five, `chapter-0419.md:13`, pre-staging a paragraph sixty-six lines below it.** The added paragraph read *"…and it goes down the steps and across a floor and out of a door, and there is a hook on the wall the whole time with nothing on it…"* **Base line 69 delivers that as the chapter's closing scene — "the basket went down at the seventh hour and the hook was empty inside a minute" — and base line 5 has already said "The basket goes down at the seventh hour and does not come back up."** Base line 69 is landed line 79 and the record this pass wrote above first called it base line 79, which is a line of the file as it stands and not a line of the file at `fe49ab0`; `fe49ab0` gives that file seventy-two lines and there is no line 79 in it. The added paragraph was the chapter's second paragraph and it told the reader the hook was empty the whole time, which is the image the last scene exists to land. Its first fix read *"…and it goes out on somebody else's errand and not her own, and the hook on the wall is the only fixture in the corridor anybody has ever expected anything of"*, and that text is what this pass's own seventh finding is about; what stands now is *"…and it goes out on somebody else's errand and not its own, and the hook is the only fixture in the corridor anybody has ever expected anything of"*.

**Six, `chapter-0419.md:75`, a pre-performed act and added interiority in one added line.** The added paragraph ended *"…and the man who said it is the reason, and nobody has ever thanked him for it and nobody ever will, and those are the same sentence and he does not know it."* **Base line 71, which is landed line 81, six lines below, opens the chapter's last paragraph with "**Nobody thanked him**, and nobody asked him one question about a number" — so the added line performed the act the base's closing paragraph performs, and added *"and nobody ever will"* on top of it. And "he does not know it" asserts an inner state of the man of about sixty-one, which is the exact construction that record's own reading pass withdrew five times, one of them being "A man knowing there was somebody on the stair."** Its first fix ended *"…and the man who said it is the reason, and it stays in the corridor with him."* **That was the same defect in paraphrase and it stood for one run of the record before the review of this record caught it: base line 71 closes *"and that is where it stays"*, so the revoicing asserted six lines above the line that lands the assertion that the thing stays in the corridor.** It now ends *"…and the man who said it is the reason."* — the eight words *"and it stays in the corridor with him"* are out and the paragraph stops on the plain fact it was built to land, and the chapter's last paragraph keeps the beat entirely to itself.

**Seven, `chapter-0419.md:13`, a wrong referent, and this pass's own fix created it and the standing this pass wrote is what found it.** The revoicing that took out defect five put *"and it goes out on somebody else's errand and not her own"* into a chapter **whose base contains no female pronoun and no woman at all: `git show fe49ab0:chapters/volume-09/chapter-0419.md` returns zero for `she`, `her`, `hers`, `woman`, `girl`, and both of the two men in it are male.** Every person in `chapter-0419.md` is the young man of twenty-six or the man of about sixty-one, and the pronoun stood at nobody. **This is defect three of this section again with the sexes exchanged, and the scan that found defect three did not find this one because it was written to look for male pronouns in added prose, and it was re-run on this corrected tree against female pronouns and returns one hit at this line and no other in the ten files.** It is now *"not its own"*. **The same clause carried the echo the review of this record named: *"and the hook on the wall is the only fixture"* against base line 71's *"with a hook in the wall at the end of it"*, which is a locative phrase the chapter has already spent three times — base line 3, base line 63 and this pass's own line 31 all say *in the wall*.** It now says *"and the hook is the only fixture"*, and the hook has been named in the first line of the chapter and needs nothing after it.

**All seven were fixed by revoicing an added line, no base line was touched, and the range is 48 words shorter for having had them found: 19,791 to 19,743.** **Six of the seven were found by reading and by nothing else. The one that was not, `chapter-0418.md`'s missing man, was found by a mechanical scan of male pronouns in added prose against male pronouns in each file's own base — a scan this pass built for the purpose and did not have, and the scan is one line and it is in the standing handed on — and the seventh was found by the same scan run in the other direction, on the corrected tree, after this pass had created it.**

**This pass caused the standing regression itself, twice, and undid it both times, and the finding is the same one the record above names.** The first fix for `chapter-0418.md:49` put *those boards* where there was one and the first fix for `chapter-0419.md:13` put *that corridor* where there were three, and **the range-wide totals rose to 67, 98, 117 and 239 across 84 forms and the range-wide form delta showed two entries, and the per-file form-delta scan named both files.** Both were revoiced, *those boards* back to *the counter* and *that corridor* back to *the corridor*, and the four lists returned to 66, 95, 114 and 236 with both deltas empty. **A revoicing made to satisfy a defect can put a form into the sentence that replaced the one it removed, and here it put two in across two files in one pass.** **A third round of edits, this pass's seventh defect and the correction of the sixth, held them: the four lists stand at 66, 95, 114 and 236 across 84 forms, the per-file form delta between the tree this record was written against and the corrected tree is empty, and all eleven words the third round took out were words no form is made of.**

**The cause is checkable and it is in the table rather than in the comparison. Not one figure in it is a formula figure: `reprints` returns 51, 51, 54 and 107 for `either` formula and 50, 50, 47 and 46 for `date` formula at the four windows, and no cell of that table holds any of the eight.** Its cells hold prose figures, and they hold them in the wrong cells: **the first number of the `either` cell is the `either` prose figure and the second is the `date` prose figure, at all four windows — 95/96, 375/376, 1,259/1,266 and 3,689/3,751 — and every one of those eight is exact against `cb7fce7`, which is the tree that repair landed and not this corrected tree.** The two cells beside it then carry the `date` and `terms` prose figures of that same tree in that order at windows twenty and twelve, transposed at window eight, and at window five with **3,736** in both halves of the `terms` cell. **Three figures in that table — 3,736, 1,250 and 3,712 — are in no bucket of any of the four trees measured here, which are `fe49ab0`, `9f5a021`, `cb7fce7` and this corrected tree, and a figure that the instrument does not return anywhere is not a stale figure and is a figure that was never measured.**

**Its `before` column does not reproduce the tree it names either, and that is a finding about item 183's record rather than about this one.** That record says the before column is the same tree with the ten files behind this range reverted to `fe49ab0` and nothing else changed, measured in a detached worktree. Nothing in that record's conclusions turns on the column and no ruling changes.

The claim is stated here rather than asserted, and the standing is the one item 185's record hands on: a figure has to be re-derived and not carried forward, the direction of a difference is not the same thing as its cause, and a table whose cells do not hold what its own header says they hold cannot be compared cell by cell and has to be measured again from the instrument before anything is said about it. ## Seven: two figures in the record above that pair a run length with a holder count taken at a different pool, and two rows of its table that do not reproduce

**This is the finding of this pass and it is a property of the record and not of the prose, and it is the same class item 185 found on the range behind this one: a holder count and a run length must be printed from the same window and from the same pool as the run they are attached to.**

**The record's `lifts` table prints five holder counts, and all five are whole-manuscript counts sitting in a table whose instrument is a range-excluded index.** Measured on the exact string, against the 610 chapters outside the range, they are **`of them and that is the whole of what`** record 2 chapters / 2 volumes, measured **1 / 1**; **`for it and that is the whole of what`** record 1 / 1, measured **0 / 0**; **`is not a thing anybody can be shown`** record 6 / 4, measured **5 / 4**; **`and there is no form in this empire`** record 127 / 10, measured **125 / 10**; **`and neither of the two of them has`** record 6 / 5, measured **5 / 4**. **All five equal the whole-manuscript count exactly, and `chapter-0174.md`, which the instrument names as the source of the second, holds the seed five-gram only across a paragraph boundary and holds the eight-word run nowhere in the volume outside this range.** The counts are right and the pool is wrong for the instrument they are attached to, and the second row is the sharpest case: the run's only holder in the whole manuscript is the repair's own added line.

**And the record prints two different holder counts for what reads as the same phrase in the same section: 162 chapters for *'there is no form in this empire'* in the seven-word list and 127 for *'and there is no form in this empire'* in the `lifts` table.** Those are two different strings and the two figures are not in conflict once the strings are read — one has the leading *and* and one does not — **but the record gives 162 for the seven-word list and that figure reproduces under neither the range-excluded nor the whole-manuscript convention, which are 161 and 163.** Four of that list's seventeen rows are of this kind: the three register connectives at 162, 144 and 139 against 161, 143 and 138 excluded and 163, 145 and 140 whole, **and *'did not look at either of them'* at 6 / 4 against 5 / 4 excluded and 7 / 4 whole.** Each is exactly one above the range-excluded count and one below the whole-manuscript count. **Every one of the seventeen is at or above the four-and-four threshold under both conventions and so every ruling stands and no figure in the table moved a decision.**

**Two rows of the record's twelve-pair intra-file table do not reproduce, and the headline of twelve does.** *`chapter-0413.md:19` against `:41`* is printed at **seven words** on *'on the second of the two days'*, **and the true longest common run is six words, *'the second of the two days'*, because line 41 reads "the second of the two days falls" and has no *on* before it.** And *`chapter-0413.md:61` against `:71`* is printed at **six words** on *'and there is no form anywhere'*, **and the two lines share a longest run of two words, so that pair does not reach the six-word reporting floor at all.** The table carries thirteen pairs across eleven rows while its prose says twelve; **twelve pairs are real, one is not, and the twelve that are real are the twelve the scan returns.**

**The threshold was therefore checked at every window length rather than at the one the record picked, because that is what decides the ruling.** The volume's own register connective *'and there is no form anywhere in this empire in which a person can'* reads, on the 610 chapters outside the range, **219 chapters across 10 volumes at six words, 177 at eight, 166 at nine, 42 across 5 at twelve, 11 across 3 at thirteen and zero at fourteen** — at or above the four-and-four threshold at every window up to and including twelve and below it only at thirteen. **The register stands, the four threshold rows stand, the rare continuations stand, and what was wrong was the arithmetic of the evidence rather than the judgement built on it.**

## Eight: the canon held, and what is carried unrepaired

**Nobody was thanked, forgiven or sent for, nothing was resolved, and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is seven and did not move.** Zero question marks in ten chapters. No bold marker added. **No interiority survives: the one instance this pass found, *'and he does not know it'* at `chapter-0419.md:75`, was an assertion about a man's self-knowledge and is now the corridor keeping it.**

**The next ten are `chapter-0421.md` to `chapter-0430.md` and they are in Volume 09, so every `tools/measure.py` command for them carries `--volume 09`. Their prompt is `workspace/prose-repair-0020/PROMPT.md`, which this phase did not create and which exists at 38,062 bytes on this corrected tree and stood at 37,614 when this record was written.** **It names that range exactly and its figures reproduce on this corrected tree: 14,397 words at mean 1,439.7, and all ten files are byte-identical at `cb7fce7` and on the working tree, so `git diff --numstat cb7fce7` over them returns nothing and the range is unrepaired, and `ff29134`, the head of that range's own log, is an ancestor of `cb7fce7`.** **This phase created no prompt and wrote no prompt directory, because the next phase's prompt already exists and writing a second one for the same range would be two prompts for one range — which is the failure this ledger exists to prevent, and not the failure a missing file would have been.** **What this phase did do to that file is correct two of its context figures, which had gone stale, and then to correct them a second time after the review of this record: the file said Volume 09 was 78,540 and the manuscript 1,463,129, they became 78,510 and 1,463,099 for the thirty-seven words this pass's first six fixes took out, and they are 78,499 and 1,463,088 for the forty-eight words its seven fixes took out. A figure corrected once in a run is not a figure that cannot go stale again in the same run. The file's figures for the range under repair were not stale and were not touched, and they reproduce on this corrected tree: 14,397 words at mean 1,439.7 with `git diff --numstat cb7fce7` over the ten files returning nothing.**

**The standing this range hands to the next one, and each of these cost this range something.**

**One: a scan of the added prose's pronouns against the pronouns in each file's own base is one line long and it found a defect nothing else here could reach, because it asks a question no index in this repository asks, which is whether the people an added paragraph points at are in the chapter at all.** `chapter-0418.md` has no man in it and an added paragraph pointed at one.

**Two: when two sentences of one added paragraph cannot be about the same person, one of them is wrong, and no instrument here looks inside a paragraph for that.** Naming the second subject costs four words and settled `chapter-0414.md:85`.

**Three: the intra-file scan's six-word floor is above the length of a restatement that borrows a figure rather than a phrase, and `chapter-0411.md:25` borrowed a duration and a subordinate clause and shared five tokens with the base line above it.** Reading is the only instrument that reaches it.

**Four: the located date-line check is the standing and not the printed one even in the one volume where `calendar` sees every file, and `sed -n '5p'` is blind on all ten of this range and on all ten of the next.**

**Five: a revoicing made to fix a defect put a `that`-noun into two sentences in two files in this pass, and the per-file form-delta scan caught both and the range-wide total did not.**

**Six: a holder count printed beside a `lifts` row must be measured on the range-excluded pool, because that is the pool the instrument indexes, and a whole-manuscript count beside a range-excluded run is a count of a different thing and reads as stronger evidence than it is.**

**Seven: a record that says it created a file is not evidence that it created the file, and a file that exists is not evidence that its figures are current. Both were checked here with `ls` and with a re-measurement, and the second check found two stale figures that the first could not — and the figures went stale again in the same run, which is why the standing is re-measure and is not *check once*.**

**Eight: a revoicing can import a person who is not in the chapter, and it did that here.** Standing one was written after `chapter-0418.md` pointed at a man in a chapter with no man in it, and the scan behind it was written to look for male pronouns in added prose. **A chapter with no man in it is the same defect as a chapter with no woman in it, and the scan has to be run in both directions on every range and not only in the direction the defect happened to arrive from.** `chapter-0419.md` has no woman in its base and an added paragraph said *her own* for two runs before that scan was run the other way.

**Nine: a table whose cells do not hold what its own header says they hold cannot be compared cell by cell, and a figure the instrument returns nowhere is a figure that was never measured.** Item 183's `reprints` table held no formula figure in any cell, carried three numbers the instrument returns at no tree, and its before column was a measurement of the tree after the repair rather than before it. **Every cell has to be re-derived from the instrument and the instrument named beside it, and a disagreement between a record and a review over a count is a disagreement about what was read until both are re-run.**


## Eleven: the review of this record, four findings taken and two declined, and what changed because of them

**This record was reviewed against the working tree, the same hand that wrote it wrote the review, and every figure below was re-derived rather than accepted.** The review found seven things. **Four were real and are fixed above; two were false and are declined; one was a fact about this record's own labelling that is corrected in section Two.** Nothing else moved, no ruling changed, and the next ten and the standing handed on are untouched.

**One, the prose, and it is the finding that matters: one of this record's six fixes did not fix the defect it was written to fix.** Section Two's sixth fix replaced *"nobody has ever thanked him for it and nobody ever will"* in `chapter-0419.md:75` with *"and it stays in the corridor with him"*, **and base line 71 of that chapter closes *"and that is where it stays"*, so the revoicing asserted the thing stays in the corridor six lines above the paragraph that lands it.** The same sentence it replaced was carrying a second fault and the substitution carried it forward in different words. **The eight words are out and the paragraph now ends on *"and the man who said it is the reason."*** A token gate cannot see this and neither can a longest-run scan: *"it stays in the corridor"* and *"that is where it stays"* share two tokens.

**Two, and it is a class the standing handed on by this very record.** Running standing one — a scan of the added prose's pronouns against the pronouns in each file's own base — in the direction this pass had not run it, over female pronouns as well as male, returns **one hit in ten files, `chapter-0419.md:13`'s *"not her own"* in a chapter whose base has no female pronoun and no woman in it at all**, and that word was put there by this pass's own first fix for defect five. It is `its` now and the scan returns zero. **A revoicing can import a person who is not in the chapter, and the standing a pass writes for one direction of a question does not run in the other direction by itself.**

**Three, the record's line numbers, and it is a labelling error of the kind this repository has been bitten by.** Sections Two and the item in `state/open-threads.md` called `chapter-0419.md`'s closing paragraph base line 79 and base line 81. **They are base lines 69 and 71; 79 and 81 are lines of the file as it stands, and `fe49ab0` gives that file seventy-two lines.** Corrected where it stood.

**Four, the volume figures, and every one of them moved by this pass's own eleventh word.** The range is 19,743 at mean 1,974.3, Volume 09 is 78,499, the manuscript is 1,463,088, and `workspace/prose-repair-0020/PROMPT.md`'s two context figures were corrected for the second time in one run. ## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat at both ends

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "b8780ff"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(401,411)]
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                       # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))  # body_strip as printed
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(                           # selector THEN date line stripped
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not DATE_EITHER.match(L) and not DATE_THIRD.match(L))))
W = 14325            # at BASE; 19097 on the working tree
for name, f in (("1 m.prose_lines UNSTRIPPED", b1), ("2 body_strip as printed", b2),
                ("3 selector THEN date line stripped", b3)):
    t = " ".join(f(open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()) for p in files)
    s = sweep(t)
    print(f"{name:38s} ten {cnt(t,TEN):>2}={cnt(t,TEN)*1000.0/W:.2f} 23 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD)*1000.0/W:.2f} "
          f"25 {cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW):>2}={cnt(t,TEN+ADD+NEW)*1000.0/W:.2f} sweep {sum(s.values())}={sum(s.values())*1000.0/W:.2f} forms {len(s)}")
```

**The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times.** Two walk-words stand in the added prose and neither is a walk: one says a hundred feet of floor had been between the two ends of the boards all morning and **neither of the two women had walked any of it**, and the other says a man who has done a walk four times a day for four years does not know how long it is any more. **The nine miles is a locative — a building off a road about nine miles from a lane — and the four hundred yards is a room a woman has never had any business in. **The two ways this range is harder than the two behind it, and both were found by measuring rather than by being told.** The first is the date lines: **four of the ten carry the date sentence at line 5 and no range this repair has measured has done that**, at `chapter-0421.md`, `chapter-0422.md`, `chapter-0423.md` and `chapter-0424.md`. The prompt's warning is taken whole and the warning is correct: **on a file whose date line is at 9 an insert above line 5 is above the date line and an insert below it is not, and a line-5 check cannot tell the two apart, and on a file whose date line is at 5 an insert at line 4 is above it and an insert at line 5 is below it, and the check can tell them apart only if somebody remembers to run it, and only on four of the ten, and a helper that inserts at a line number will not remember.** The helper used here located the date line with the same `DATE_EITHER` and `DATE_THIRD` the printed instrument uses, **refused any anchor at or above the located line, refused any anchor on a blank line, asserted the line count after every insert, asserted the located date line had not moved after every insert, and asserted that no line sat directly under a non-blank line after every insert.** It refused four anchors and every refusal was caught before anything was written: one draft for `chapter-0425.md` anchored at base line 3 where the date line stands at 7.
