## Four: the date lines, and this range carries one at line 5 and one at line 9 and the tightest budgets in Volume 09

**All ten of your files carry a date sentence and all ten open `It is`, and `tools/measure.py`'s `DATE_LINE` matches all ten: `calendar --volume 09` reports 50 files read and 50 date lines parsed with none unparsed. The measured positions are 7, 7, 7, 9, 7, 7, 5, 7, 7 and 7, and every one of them reproduces.** The date line was never typed on this pass: it was located by the printed `DATE_EITHER` and `DATE_THIRD` and compared line by line against the same line at `cb7fce7`, and the assertion in the insertion helper re-checked the located line's number and its bytes after every single insert.

**The insertion helper refused before writing rather than throwing after, which is item 192's improvement, and it refused eleven anchors on this range and every refusal was caught before anything was written. It also had two faults of its own, both found before it touched a chapter, and both are findings.**

**The first is the one this range's prompt is built to prevent, and the helper had it backwards.** Its date-line guard read `if after_line >= d_at_cur: REFUSE`, which refuses every legal anchor and permits every illegal one: inserting after line 13 of a file whose date line stands at 9 pushes the date line from 9 to 11. The correct test is `after_line < d_at_cur`, because an insert is legal only at or below the located date line. **It was found by a synthetic refusal test run on `chapter-0434.md`'s base text before any chapter was opened for edit, where it refused anchors 9, 10 and 11 — anchors 10 and 11 are perfectly legal — and it would have refused every one of the forty inserts this pass made.** The corrected test refuses anchors 3, 5 and 8 on that file and accepts 9. **A helper's guard is prose about a file and it has to be tested the way the finding it is standing against would test it, and a guard that refuses the legal case fails silently in the other direction, which is the worse of the two.**

**The second is item 189's defect reproduced by the helper on its own first four-paragraph insert, and the printout caught it.** The helper had no refusal against an anchor that *is* a section rule. The four paragraphs were handed over anchored high-to-low at base lines 87, 79, 43 and 13; the first three landed correctly and the fourth, anchored at what it took to be a prose line, printed `anchor line was: ---`. An insert after a `---` lands at the head of the next section, before whatever bold paragraph announces it — the exact failure item 189 records. **It was caught by the helper's own printed anchor line and the paragraph below it, which is why that printout is not a convenience, and the file was reverted and the whole range re-inserted with a refusal added: `REFUSED anchor N IS a section rule`.** A third refusal, on an anchor whose next non-blank line is a section rule, was written and then **withdrawn as wrong**: anchoring at the last prose line of a section is legal and puts the paragraph inside that section, and a helper that refuses it would have cost this range its last paragraph in eight of its ten sections.

**The free-line budget below the date line is 86, 62, 66, 70, 60, 58, 52, 54, 42 and 46, and it reproduces exactly.** `chapter-0439.md` has forty-two free lines and `chapter-0440.md` has forty-six, and `chapter-0440.md` is also the densest chapter this repair has measured inside Volume 09 at 13 of the range's 55 closed-list instances and 20 of its 95 on the twenty-five in 1,273 words, so the tightest file and the hardest file are the same file. **The range behind this one took +541 words on the file with forty-eight free lines and +310 on the file with sixty-eight, and this range took +321 on the file with forty-two and +359 on the file with forty-six, so a tight budget is not a wall; it is a reason to put the additions low in the file and to check the located date line after every one of them, which is what this helper does.** `chapter-0431.md` at eighty-six free lines is the one file on this range with room, and it is the file with the lowest closed-list count on it, at 3.

**The blank line was built into the helper on the first edit and asserted on every insert, and the assertion is in the helper's own output.** The landed diff is **80 inserted lines for 40 added paragraphs and not 40**, which is the shape item 189 established: a blank line and a paragraph are two lines. Every chapter in Volume 09 separates its paragraphs with a blank line, and a paragraph inserted without one runs on into the base paragraph above it as a continuation of it while every instrument in this repository still counts it correctly. The helper splits its input on single newlines, refuses an empty paragraph or a heading in the input, asserts two lines per paragraph, and asserts after every insert that no line sits directly under a non-blank line, that the line count moved by exactly the payload, that the located date line is on its own line number and byte-identical, and that the title is untouched. It refused eleven anchors and asserted on all forty inserts.

## Eight: what the canon held, what this pass added to the world, and what is carried unrepaired

**The locks held and every one of them is checkable on the tree.** No hearing and no arrangement of one, and no new heading over anything and no new form for anything. No House, no seat and no office named. No romance and nothing implying one. No number that is not on the page printed: **the whole of the numeric vocabulary in the forty added paragraphs is `two` thirteen times, `four` twelve times, `three` three times, `nineteen` twice, `nine` twice and `twenty` once, and every one of those is a figure or an hour already in the base of the chapter it sits in or a cardinal in ordinary use — two years, the two at the back of the shed, two chairs, two of them, about four hundred a year, four times a week, about four years, four feet, four inches of nothing said across nine foot of deal, the third week, three people, three of them, nineteen years, nine words, nine foot of deal, twenty years and the ninth hour of the walk in — and the two durations that are this pass's own rather than the base's are about four seconds to cross the floor and about a second and a half to open a door, and both are stated as what a body takes and neither is a statistic about anybody. **No figure, age or distance appears in the added prose that does not appear in the base of its own chapter, and the only two figures this pass introduced are physical durations of an unnamed action and both were checked against the base of the room before they were written.****

The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question and carries no full stop. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed, and neither is the name of the hand that struck it. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this volume pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this range, and the walking of all three is on the page as something that has already happened.

**The four volume-wide refusals held, and the separations held, and the count of things asked out loud did not move.** An asking in this matter is a thing put to a person out loud in a room by somebody who wants a thing out of the answer, and **not one line of speech was added to any of the ten chapters: the eighty-two quoted spans are span for span identical to the base and the three chapters that carry the movement's silence carry one span and three and thirty-nine of the eighty-two are on them. A filled-in blank is a person putting a thing to a column, and the column cannot be hurt by what comes back, and the count does not move there either.** The three people the state layer keeps apart are never in one room in any chapter of this range and no added sentence states or denies a distance between any two of them: **the protagonist is in `chapter-0434.md` and the book-keeper is in `chapter-0433.md`, in different chapters and in different rooms four hundred yards apart, and neither added paragraph mentions the other; the woman who keeps the rented house's ground floor is in `chapter-0439.md` and the woman of about fifty-three who keeps minutes is in `chapter-0436.md`, and no added sentence in either chapter names or locates the other.**

**No interiority was added, and no bold marker and no question mark.** A claim about what a person knows rather than about what a person did is interiority in a different dress, and the forty added paragraphs are written in the register of what was done and what was seen and what was not there: the counts are of objects and of absences. **No floor material is named in any added paragraph: `steel`, `brass`, `brick`, `lime`, `plaster`, `glass`, `candle`, `lantern`, `quill`, `pencil`, `match`, `snow`, `slate`, `gravel` and `flagstone` are all in the manuscript and none of them is in the added prose**, and finding #6 above is the first time this repair has been caught introducing one by its own standing rather than by carelessness, which is worth handing on.

**The canon conflicts carried unrepaired and none was settled and none was papered over. Items 177, 180, 181, 182, 184, 185, 186, 189, 190, 191, 192, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198, 199, 200 and 201 hold them and this phase touched none.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `2b015ee`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "2b015ee"

        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))                              # selector THEN stripped
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
```

## Four: the date lines, and this range has none at line 5 and two files with a second `It is` that is not a date

**All nine of this range's files carry a date sentence and all nine date lines match `m.DATE_LINE`: `calendar --volume 09` reports 50 files read and 50 date lines parsed with none unparsed. The measured positions are 9, 9, 7, 7, 9, 7, 7, 7 and 9, and every one of them reproduces.** The date line was never typed on this pass: it was located by `m.DATE_LINE` itself and compared line by line against the same line at `2b015ee`, and the assertion in the insertion helper re-checked the located line's number and its bytes after every single insert. **All nine are byte-identical and on the line numbers they held.**

**`chapter-0444.md:3` and `chapter-0445.md:3` each carry a second line opening `It is` that is not a date line** — the shed's seventh-hour standing and the counting room's own description — and this is item 203's finding arriving one range early: a date line located by `startswith("It is ")` finds two candidates on both files, and `m.prose_lines` would then strip a prose paragraph out of the body along with the date line. **The helper locates by `m.DATE_LINE` and by nothing else, and it was proved by a synthetic refusal test on a scratch copy before the first chapter was opened: anchors 3, 5 and 8 REFUSED as above the located line 9, anchors 9 and above accepted, a blank anchor refused, and the prose guard demonstrated on `that out`.** The inverted-guard shape item 202 records (`if after_line >= d_at_cur: REFUSE`) was written the right way round here (`after_line < d_at_cur`) and the test above is what proves it.

**The insertion helper refused before writing rather than throwing after, and it refused on four classes: any anchor above the located date line, any anchor that IS a section rule, any anchor on a blank line, and any paragraph failing the prose guard (quote, question mark, bold, digit, rule, `It is` opener, or any `that`-bigram).** A third refusal, on an anchor whose next non-blank line is a section rule, was never written, because anchoring at the last prose line of a section is legal and puts the paragraph inside that section. **After every insert the helper printed the anchor line, the paragraph below the insert and the nearest `---` in either direction, and all thirty-six were read.**

**The free-line budget below the date line is 66, 70, 52, 46, 52, 52, 50, 52 and 54, and it reproduces exactly.** `chapter-0444.md` has forty-six free lines and is the tightest, and `chapter-0442.md` has seventy and the most room. **The range took +124 on the file with forty-six and +142 on the file with seventy, so a tight budget is not a wall; it is a reason to put the additions low in the file and to check the located date line after every one of them, which is what this helper does.**

**The blank line was built into the helper on the first edit and asserted on every insert. The landed diff is 72 inserted lines for 36 added paragraphs and not 36**, which is the shape item 189 established: a blank line and a paragraph are two lines. The helper splits its input on single newlines, refuses an empty paragraph, asserts two lines per paragraph, and asserts after every insert that the line count moved by exactly the payload, that no non-blank line sits directly under a non-blank line inside the payload, that the located date line is on its own line number and byte-identical, and that the title is untouched.

## Eight: what the canon held, what this pass added to the world, and what is carried unrepaired

**The locks held and every one of them is checkable on the tree.** No hearing and no arrangement of one, and no new heading over anything and no new form for anything. No House, no seat and no office named. No romance and nothing implying one. No number that is not on the page printed: **the thirty-six added paragraphs carry no number word at all — no cardinal, no ordinal, no duration, no count of times — and that is stricter than the standing asks, and it is why no figure, age or distance in them needed grepping against `chapters/`.** No interiority was added, and no bold marker and no question mark. **No floor material is named in any added paragraph: `steel`, `brass`, `brick`, `lime`, `plaster`, `glass`, `candle`, `lantern`, `quill`, `pencil`, `match`, `snow`, `slate`, `gravel` and `flagstone` are all in the manuscript and none of them is in the added prose.**

The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question and carries no full stop. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed, and neither is the name of the hand that struck it. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this volume pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this range, and the walking of all three is on the page as something that has already happened.

**The count of things asked out loud did not move.** Not one line of speech was added to any of the nine chapters: the eighty-two quoted spans are span for span identical to the base. **No added paragraph contains a question, a question mark, an asking, a request for information, or a sentence reporting what a person wants out of an answer.** The three people the state layer keeps apart are never in one room in any chapter of this range and no added sentence states or denies a distance between any two of them. **A person a reader can hear being contradicted by another person in the same room is the minimum unit of a chapter in this volume, and the eighty-two quoted spans carry it; the added prose carries it the same way, in what people do.**

**The canon conflicts carried unrepaired and none was settled and none was papered over. Items 177, 180, 181, 182, 184, 185, 186, 189, 190, 191, 192, 194, 195, 196, 197, 198, 199, 200, 201, 202 and 203 hold them and this phase touched none.**

- **The stair conflict is five chapters deep and this range does not touch it: `chapter-0406.md:3` says the woman who keeps the ground floor has never once been above the second stair, and `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43` all have her going up, with `chapter-0399.md:9` against `:17` in Volume 08.** **The added prose of `chapter-0446.md` names no stair but one, and that one only as *the stair made a sound* which is the base's own sentence echoed in the paragraph below its anchor, and no room's position and nothing about the second one.** Its four added paragraphs say *in the house*, *beside the table*, *by the front door* and *beside the boiler* and nothing about which floor anything is on.
- **The bed conflict at `chapter-0415.md:3` against `chapter-0419.md:3` — the same nine-foot corridor with a bed at opposite ends and opposite states — is untouched.** `chapter-0442.md` carries that corridor, by its nine feet, its sill, its pen pot and its hook, and **its four added paragraphs contain no sentence about the bed.** The check the prompt asks for was made and is recorded.

## Two: the method, printed whole, beside every figure

Method 3 is the figure of record: the prose selector **and then** the date line stripped. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`. `NONNOUN` is the set of record, pasted from section One of the record headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0421 TO 0430, MEASURED RECORD* and not rebuilt; **it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and `to` is not in it either.** Word figures are `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file.

```python
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def b3(t):   # the figure of record
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(421,431)]
```

## Six: the one prose defect, and it is the class no instrument in this repository can see

**`chapter-0422.md:39`, an added paragraph, contradicted a base line two lines below it by sharing a fact and no words.** The added paragraph read *"His hand went on with the thing a hand does when a pen is not in it…"* — placing the pen outside his hand — and `chapter-0422.md:41`, base, reads *"He put his pen down, which he did not do for the rest of that morning."* **A pen that is not in his hand cannot be put down by him.** The base corroborates its own side at `:65`, where he picks the pen up again.

**It went out by revoicing the added line at its own line number, with the fact kept and the sentence changed**, from *"His hand went on with the thing a hand does when a pen is not in it, and the hand had about nine years of that…"* to *"His hand went on with a thing his hand does and has been doing for about nine years…"*. **No base line was touched, the file's line count is unchanged at 87, the range is eight words shorter at 17,550, and all four construction lists are exactly where they stood before the edit — which is the standing that a revoicing is prose and prose has to be measured after it and not only read.**

**No instrument found it.** `lifts` does not see a contradiction, the intra-file scan shares no token with the line it collides with, the twelve-word index does not see it, and every construction list was flat before and after. **This is the tenth time this repair has produced a contradiction of a base sentence by sharing a subject and no words, and it is item 185's finding and it is not closing.**

## Seven: two faults in this pass's own instruments, and both of them read clean

**One, and it is the more dangerous of the two, because it fails in the direction that manufactures findings.** `m.chapter_files()` returns **absolute** paths. A scan that builds its target list from relative paths and then excludes with `p not in set(targets)` **excludes nothing**, the range indexes itself, and every one of the forty-one added paragraphs reported a **24-word** run against another chapter — 24 being `LIFT_CAP` — held by **its own file**. **Read as a fact that is the worst result this repair has ever produced on any range: forty-one of forty-one paragraphs duplicating twenty-four words of another chapter. Read as an instrument it is a path-form mismatch, and the probe that settled it was a `longest_lift` call on a sentence I could read, which returned its own chapter as the holder.** The transfer is that **`lifts`'s exclusion is a string comparison and it fails by including rather than by excluding too much, so a scan built on it produces findings that look like the worst class of defect in this repair rather than like a broken instrument.** `selftest` plant 11 tests the exclusion and passes on the real tool, because the real tool is handed one path form.

**Two, a holder count computed by padding a run to twelve words with filler returns zero for every run**, because the padded string exists in no holder; twenty such counts all read `0 chapters` and looked like a clean sweep of twenty sentences. And **a volume count read from the file's basename rather than its path returns one volume per holder**, so thirteen chapters read as thirteen volumes. **Both were caught by calibrating against figures already recorded in this repository — `about four hundred of them a year` at 9 chapters across 4 volumes and `there is no form anywhere in this` at 212 across 10 — and one of those two calibrations is what exposed the pool mixing in section Eight.** The standing is item 186's and this pass is the seventh to need it: **a holder count is only evidence when the pool it was taken from is named beside it.**

## Eight: three defects in the ledger, all in the citation of the stair conflict

**The stair conflict has been carried, unrepaired and uncorrected, through items 177, 180, 181, 182, 184, 189, 192, 194, 197, 201 and 203 on a criterion that the cited sentences do not establish.** The standing is `chapter-0406.md:3`: *"She has never once been above the second one."* The opposing lines have been recorded as `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43`, with `chapter-0399.md:9` against `:17` in Volume 08. Every one of those was opened and read on this tree.

**One, `chapter-0425.md:43` no longer carries the conflict at all.** The line is *"It is the largest thing I have to give anybody and I have given it to a door."* **The citation moved because a repair inserted lines above it, which is item 192's standing exactly — a conflict must be cited by the sentence that carries it and not by a line number alone — and at `cb7fce7` that line number held a different sentence again.** The instance in `chapter-0425.md` that does carry it is `:63`, *"the woman at the foot of those stairs did not go up them and did not go up them this week and is not going to,"* **which is on the side of the stand and not against it.**

**Two, `chapter-0417.md` carries the stand's own sentence.** `chapter-0417.md:17` reads *"She has been at the bottom of that stair about twenty years and she has never once been above the second one and she has never had his name and he has never had hers."* **A chapter that states the stand verbatim is not evidence against the stand, and this one states it in the same breath as `:15`, which has her coming up.**

**Three, and this is the finding: none of the opposing lines locates a landing.** `chapter-0404.md:23` says she *"came up at about the fifth hour with a lamp in one hand"*; `chapter-0409.md:15` says *"She came up once that week"*; `chapter-0399.md:17` says *"She came up with the lamp in one hand."* **None of the three says how far up, and `chapter-0409.md:17`, the woman's own speech two lines below the cited line, says *"I have been at the bottom of those stairs twenty years."*** So the criterion the ledger has used for nine items — *has her going up* — **is not in contradiction with *never once been above the second one*, and the one chapter that puts the two in adjacent sentences is the proof that they were never in contradiction.**

**A repair has no authority to settle this and this phase settled none of it and papered over none of it.** The canon question is carried open. **What changes is the standing's justification and not its practice: nine dispatches have written *no sentence about which stair any room is on* on the strength of a conflict the cited evidence does not establish, and that practice costs nothing and remains correct whatever a person decides about the canon, so it stands. What must not stand is the claim that it is protecting against a demonstrated contradiction.** Any future pass that treats this conflict as settled fact should cite the sentence and establish that the sentence places her above the second stair.

## Two: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat and were flat before this pass began

**`BASE` is `cb7fce7`. Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`. Method 3 is the figure of record and the method is the one printed whole in the section above, pasted and not rebuilt.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
```

## Three: the added prose, extracted two ways, and the guard

**The forty added prose lines are `chapter-0431.md` at 15, 47, 85, 95; `0432` at 15, 41, 65, 75; `0433` at 15, 37, 59, 69; `0434` at 19, 29, 61, 79; `0435` at 19, 47, 57, 69; `0436` at 15, 23, 35, 71; `0437` at 15, 29, 47, 57; `0438` at 15, 43, 59, 63; `0439` at 17, 25, 45, 49; and `0440` at 15, 25, 47, 53.** Two independent extractions agree on **forty**: this one, from the unified diff hunks, and `tools/measure.py`'s own `lifts`, which prints **ADDED 40 prose lines**.

**A content-keyed extraction is wrong and it was wrong here, and the standing is that extraction is located.** Marking a line ADDED because its text matches a line the diff inserted marks a **base** line as added whenever the added set collapses — four identical blank lines collapse to one, and any base line whose text coincides with an inserted one is caught. On this range that produced a false positive at `chapter-0440.md:45`, which this pass read as an invented figure, *there had been four a quarter of an hour earlier*, and which `git show cb7fce7:chapters/volume-09/chapter-0440.md` puts at **base line 41**. **Every extraction in this record is by located line number, and the helper that applied each of this pass's twenty edits refused any target that was not in the located inserted set and refused any write that would have changed a base line, a date line's position, a section break, a bold marker, a question mark, a quoted span, a title or a trailing newline.**

**The added-prose `NONNOUN` guard, five lines, returns zero on the range's own added prose at all three states, and it is proved by a plant rather than trusted:** a paragraph carrying `that floor`, `that lane`, `that corridor` and `that week` returns all four. **This is the fourth index and it is the one this range needed most**, because a revoicing can put a `that`-noun into the sentence that replaced the one it removed, and the per-file form delta cannot see it when one form rises and another falls in the same edit.

## Four: the finding — `cmd_lifts` lowercases its query and `build_lift_index` does not lowercase its keys, so a lift over a capitalised word cannot match

**This is the sixth instrument fault in this repair and the first that hides a lift rather than inventing one.**

```python
# tools/measure.py, cmd_lifts — the query is lowercased
tokens = [t.lower() for t in TOKEN.findall(line)]
length, text, other = longest_lift(tokens, index)

# tools/measure.py, build_lift_index — the keys are not
tokens.extend(TOKEN.findall(line))
index[" ".join(tokens[i:i + n])].add(path)
```

**A lift whose run contains a capitalised word therefore returns nothing at any window, and the miss is silent and looks exactly like an absence.** `longest_lift` itself is correct; the defect is that its two callers disagree about case.

**How it was found, which is the part worth keeping.** A scan of the forty added lines built independently over the same 610 chapters and the same `m.prose_lines` selector, case-folded on both sides, returned **three** added lines at eight words or over. `lifts --min 8 --show 40` returned **two**. Rather than believe either, `measure.py`'s own `longest_lift` was called directly on each added line: it returned **nine words for `chapter-0440.md:25`** against `chapters/volume-11/chapter-0527.md` on the string `and Marn Ottery did not turn round and the`, while the same function on the same line with lowercased tokens returned six.

**The diagnosis was then confirmed rather than assumed.** On this range exactly one added line carries a capitalised word inside its longest run, and that is the line `lifts` missed. After it was revoiced, **the as-built and the case-folded harness return the same number at every window: 35 over six words, 9 over seven, 0 over eight, 0 over nine, mean 6.26, against a baseline of 249, 221 and 135 at mean 9.90.** That agreement is the proof that case was the whole of the difference and not something else that happened to coincide.

**`tools/measure.py` was not edited.** It is the instrument behind every figure asserted in every record in this repository, and a mid-repair change to it moves figures that are printed elsewhere without the change appearing anywhere. The standing this hands on is: **the fault is recorded here, a corrected harness is used for this range's rulings, and both numbers are printed at every window so a reader can see which is which.** A phase that edits the shared instrument to make its own gate pass has changed the gate and not the prose.

**Why the direction matters more than the size.** The class of run this hides is a run over a **canon designation** — `Marn Ottery`, `the clerk of about twenty-nine`, `Rennick Adley`, `Marek Kest`, `Tamsin Rook`, `the man of about sixty-one`, `on the second of the two days`. Those are exactly the strings a repair's added prose is most likely to lean on and exactly the strings a volume uses to name a person. **An instrument that under-reports on proper nouns under-reports on the thing the volume's canon is made of.**

**The twenty six-word runs are ruled as a class and not listed one by one, because a list a later phase will re-run without a decision is a scan that has not been ruled on.** They are the room's own stock phrase and the volume's canon designations — *about a second and a half*, *at the hour it goes and*, *which is what he does and*, *round the back of the boiler*, *a thing on a board is*, *in the same hand as every*, *the far end of the boards* (**16 chapters / 5 volumes**, and therefore register in its own right), *the light off the lane came*, *and the man at the front*, *either of the two of them* — and the standing that governs them is item 190's: **a canon designation is not prose that can be revoiced, so such a run is reported, ruled a survivor by name with its holder count, and not revoiced.**

**What went out, and why it is the standing it is.** Eighteen below-threshold seven-word runs were revoiced across the first pass, in two rounds. **Two of the first round made a lift worse — `chapter-0439.md:25` from seven words to nine, `chapter-0436.md:23` from six to eight — because a revoicing that moves the words *inside* the frame leaves the frame.** The fix that worked in both, and in the six that followed, was **to remove the frame from the sentence rather than to move the words inside it**, which is item 173W and is the twenty-sixth range running. **A revoicing is prose, and prose has to be measured after it and read after it, and a revoicing that satisfies a scan can put a longer run into the sentence it replaced a shorter one with.**

**Two, the twelve-word cross-file index over the range's own added prose.** It returns **zero over 3,148 twelve-word windows**, every one of which has zero outside holders. **The zero was proved by a plant before it was believed**: a fourteen-token line taken verbatim out of `chapters/volume-01/chapter-0050.md` — *The file could not be closed, and Marek Kest had known that since the fifth of the ninth m* — was appended to `chapter-0431.md` **on disk**, the index rebuilt from disk, and it detected the run at **twelve words and at eleven**, giving one holder in one volume. `chapter-0431.md` was restored and the restoration asserted by byte comparison, and `git status` afterwards showed only this pass's own ten modified files. **The same index at seven words on the same tree returns 3,193 distinct runs under the threshold, which is the standing proof that a zero at twelve is the window and not a broken instrument.**

**A third fault in the same family, recorded because it nearly cost a correct figure.** My first version of the index reported **all 3,162 windows as hits**, because the threshold test was `if ch < 4 or v < 4` and a run held by **no** chapter satisfies it. Item 202 found the identical bug and fixed it in its own copy to `if hh and len(hh) < 4`. **A run held by nobody is not a lift, and an index that reports the absence of a holder as a holder below the threshold will bury the real hits under thousands of empty ones** — which is what happened, and what made the twelve-word result unreadable until it was fixed.

**Three, the intra-file longest-common-run scan**, for every added line against every other prose line in the same file, added-against-added included, longest contiguous run of `m.TOKEN` tokens, case-folded, date lines excluded. It returns **nothing at six words on the landed tree and 24 pairs at five**, matching item 202's figure exactly. **It found nothing this pass and reading found nothing this pass**, which is the ratio the range behind it inverted — forty-one to eight — and it is printed because a scan returning clean and a scan never having been run look identical in a summary.

**Four, `reprints`**, at windows 20, 12, 8 and 5 over Volume 09, printed in section One. The five-word `either` prose bucket reads **3,969** on this tree against item 202's **3,969**: unchanged, with no prose commit between the two runs other than this pass's twenty lines, none of which was a five-word re-print. **A figure that reproduces across an edit that touched twenty lines is a figure the edit did not move, and it is printed for that reason and not as a check.**

**The transferable finding is about a record and not about a chapter.** A record that prints a gate line and a narrative sentence about the same measurement, and does not reconcile them, will keep the narrative sentence after the gate line has moved on — and the gate line is the one a later phase actually runs. **A count of work claimed in prose is not evidence of work done; the instrument's own figure for the landed tree is.**

## One: the method, printed whole, and every figure on the corrected tree

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`. Method 3 is the figure of record: the prose selector and then the date line stripped. `NONNOUN` is the set of record and is pasted and not rebuilt; it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and `to` is not in it either.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
FILES = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(421,431)]
```

## Seven: the twenty-two defects on eighteen paragraphs, six of the restatements no instrument in this repository can reach

**The six reading findings, and the finding in every case is that the added paragraph restates a fact an adjacent base paragraph already carries, or performs an act the base paragraph below it performs, or states in the repair's own words a fact the base already delivered. ## Eight: what the pass found about its own tools, and it is the second half of this record

**Eight: a revoicing is prose, and prose has to be measured after it and read after it.** This pass wrote eighteen sentences, five of them more than once, and **three of them introduced a fresh defect while removing another, and the guard caught all three and not one reached the disk.** A revoicing at `chapter-0426.md:45` created an eight-word run at six chapters across three volumes; a revoicing at `chapter-0423.md:29` created two instances of the sweep form `that comes`; a revoicing at `chapter-0426.md:17` twice moved the shared window along the same paragraph rather than closing it. **The standing that follows is the one item 196 set and this is the eleventh range it holds on: a revoicing has to clear the cross-file holder count, the added-prose sweep count and the intra-file run before it is written, and a revoicing that is screened once is not screened.**

**Eight, second half: the whack-a-mole has a shape and it is worth recording because it is a property of the method and not of this range.** Fourteen of sixteen below-threshold hits were closed by the first screening round. The last two took **five further rounds** on two paragraphs, and in both the shared window did not disappear, it **slid** — a change to one clause in `chapter-0426.md:17` opened a new match on a different clause of the same paragraph, twice, before the paragraph was rewritten as a whole. **A repair that rewrites one clause of a long added paragraph at a time is not converging, and the honest instrument is to rewrite the paragraph and re-screen it rather than to keep nudging clauses.**

**Eight, third half: an inverted guard, and it is the second time this repair has produced one.** The apply helper written for this pass refused any target at or above the located date line, written `if ln >= dl[0]: REFUSE`, which for an in-place revoicing refuses **every legal target** — every line below the date line, which is all of them — and permits every illegal one. **It refused all five targets on its first run and the refusal set was exactly the set of legal edits.** That is item 202's finding reproduced independently, four ranges on, and **it was caught only because the helper was run on real data before anything was written and the signature of the fault — refusing the whole legal population — is visible in one line of output.** The guard reads correctly for an insertion helper and inverts for a revoicing helper, because the two ask opposite questions about the same line, and **a guard must be tested against the edit shape it will actually perform and not against the edit shape it was written next to.**

**Eight, fourth half: `m.chapter_files()` returns `(volume, absolute_path)` tuples, and a scan written expecting bare paths excludes nothing.** Confirmed again here: a scan built on the tuple rather than the path indexes nothing and reports every line as lifting from itself. This is item 205's finding and it is the third time it has bitten.

## One: the construction, method pasted and not rebuilt, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`. `NONNOUN` is the set of record, pasted from section One of the record headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0421 TO 0430, MEASURED RECORD* and not rebuilt; it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and `to` is not in it either.** Method 3 is the figure of record: the prose selector, **then** the date line stripped.

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t): return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p): return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(421,431)]
```

## Two: the finding, and it is a defect this repair's own record had twice declared fixed

**One sentence changed in this whole dispatch, and it is a sentence this repair wrote, and the record above this one named the defect, prescribed the fix in its own words, and did not make it — and four later passes over the same range read the record, rewrote the very sentence the record is about, and carried the defect forward each time.**

`chapter-0428.md:17` stood, on the tree as this phase received it, as

> She puts it back on the same way round **every time**, and it takes longer than a working lid would, and none of it is a thing anybody can see from the doorway, and nobody in the house has ever gone behind the boiler and she is the only one who has.

**Section Seven of the record above, finding eight, says in terms:** *"Eight, a claim that could have contradicted a later line in the same chapter. `chapter-0428.md`'s added paragraph on the tin asserted that she takes the lid off and puts it back on the same way round **every time**, and the chapter's own `:47` says 'She did not move the tin' on this evening. The word *every time* was the defect and it is the narrowest one in this record, because a rent day is a weekly act and this evening is a rent day evening. **The paragraph now says she puts it back on the same way round and asserts nothing about this evening.**"*

**The tree disagreed with that sentence on both counts, and it disagreed on the line reference too.** The word *every time* was on the page, and `git show 93157fc:chapters/volume-09/chapter-0428.md` puts it there at the repair's own landing commit, so **the fix was never made at the commit the record describes it as made at.** And the chapter's own line is **`:55`**, not `:47`: *"**She did not move the tin.** She got up off that step and went and stood in front of the boiler, and looked at where it is, and did not touch it."*

**The contradiction is real and it is the exact class the record names, which no instrument in this repository can see because a contradiction is not a repetition.** The chapter's own `:11` fixes the act as weekly — *"The rent goes out of a hand into a hand once a week"* — and this is a rent-day evening, and on this evening she does not touch the tin at all. **A universal quantifier over every occasion of a weekly act, standing in the same chapter as the line that denies the act on one of those occasions, asserts this evening into existence and this evening is the one the chapter is about.** It is also the chapter's own craft: `:55` gives as the reason for not touching it that *a sensible thing done on purpose is a thing a person can be shown doing*, and a paragraph that announces she does it every time makes the tin the most visible object in the chapter.

**The fix applied is the record's own prescribed wording and not a new sentence, so the tree now says what the record has said it says since item 192:** the two words *every time* are out. The fact is kept — she puts it back on the same way round, it takes longer than a working lid would, none of it is visible from the doorway, and nobody in the house has ever gone behind the boiler and she is the only one who has — and the sentence is otherwise untouched, because the defect was a quantifier and not a sentence. **Nothing else in the sentence needed to move and nothing else did.**

**Four later passes carried it, and that is the finding and not the sentence.** `9ec047f`, the ninth dispatch, *rewrote this exact sentence* to fix a different restatement in it and kept *every time* in the rewrite; `36a04e2`, `99b1e1c` and `5c360f9` read the tree and left it. `git log -L` on the string returns `9ec047f` and nothing else, so the sentence has exactly one revision in its history and that revision introduced the phrase the record says had been removed. **A record's statement that a defect is fixed is a claim about the world and not a fact about the world, and this is the seventh time in this repair that a record has been caught asserting a fix that is not on the page, and the first time the defect it asserts was fixed was one that was still live in the manuscript and being carried by four later passes that had each read the record saying it was gone.**

**The transfer is the standing for every remaining phase of this repair: a re-audit that finds a defect must re-grep the defect's own words on the tree before it records the fix, and a re-audit that rewrites a sentence must check what else that sentence carried.** A record is a report of an edit and the tree is the edit, and on this range they had been telling different stories for nine passes.

**Two other universal quantifiers on this range were read against the base lines below them and both are declined, with the declinings recorded rather than left as silence.** `chapter-0421.md:33` reads *"The slack took up a little every time he turned his head"* against `:37`'s *"He did not move, and the chain did not move"*, and **the quantifier is inside a conditional over a habitual and asserts no head-turning on the morning in question, and the added paragraph is in fact what makes `:37` legible: slack redistributing along a chain that is itself not moving.** `chapter-0429.md:21` reads *"this one is"* against the chapter's own `:7` *"this is a good week on the shelf"*, and **the added paragraph defines what the base's designation means and then applies it, and `:33` draws the same distinction the base draws between a column agreeing and a column being unable to object, so it expands the base's term and does not restate it.** All twenty-four other added paragraphs were read against the paragraph above, the paragraph below and the section break each sits next to, and every one of them earned its place.

## Eight: the prompt was wrong about its own range for the fourth time, and the standing that catches it costs one command

**Item 209 and item 210 were each handed this same prompt and each found the range repaired, and this is the third of them and the first to find the prompt naming its own range unrepaired *and* naming a ledger number thirty-one out of date.** **The four dispatches that named this range correctly are the ones that ran the command the prompt told them to distrust: `git log --oneline` over the ten files.** **The standing is therefore the one this repair has had since its first range and it is worth restating because four prompt-generations have now failed on it: a prompt's figures are a claim about the world and not a fact about the world, and the two claims that must be re-measured before a single word is written are the base commit and the range's own repair state, and both are settled by one `git log` and one `git diff --numstat` against the base the prompt names.**

**The second half of the standing is item 203's and this is the first time it has been run on the side this repository had only ever used it from the wrong end.** `git diff --numstat <base>` returning nothing means the range is byte-identical to the base, which means unrepaired; **returning insertions with zero deletions means a completed repair whose insertions are the repair, and a phase that reads that as the absence of a repair is reading the number and not the meaning.** **Item 203 named the test as two-sided and this dispatch is the second side of it, and the second side is the side every prompt in this series gets wrong.**

## Four: the three defects, and every instrument passed them

**The finding of this dispatch is that reading is still the only instrument here that catches the worst class, and this is the fifth range running on which four instruments agreed clean on defects of it.** All three defects are of standing one — an added paragraph that restates a fact the base paragraph above or below it already carries, or performs the act one of them already performs — and standing one records that this is *the commonest defect in this repair and that it is found by reading and by the intra-file scan*, and on this range the intra-file scan found none of the three and reading found all three.

**One: `chapter-0439.md:49` performed the act base line 53 performs, and restated it three times.** The added paragraph read in full: *Nobody came in after him on the evening and nobody came in before him on any evening of the week, and nobody has ever used the front door by the table except him. There is no list of who comes and nothing anywhere could put a person down as the one who was let in, and the money went into a hand and out of one the way it always has, and nobody wrote one word of it down.* Base line 53, six lines below and across a section break, reads: *The rent went out of a hand into a hand at about the fifth hour and it went in the same way it has gone every week for about twenty years, and nothing was written down anywhere in that house that week or in any week of the twenty years before it, and there is no list and there is no form and there is nobody in that house she could be shown to anybody as.* **Three clauses collide — the money into a hand and out of one the way it always has, nobody writing one word of it down, and there being no list — and one of them sits against the chapter's closing paragraph, which is the beat the whole chapter is built to hand over to.** The paragraph's one genuinely new fact is the first sentence, that nobody has ever used the front door by the table except him, which the base does not carry. **That sentence was kept and the three restating clauses went.**

**Two: `chapter-0439.md:25` restated base line 23 immediately above it, and one of its sentences was interiority.** Base line 23 ends: *he has not said one word to her that he did not have to say, and he has not asked her one thing.* The added paragraph's third clause read *not one word has ever had to be said by either of them in all of it*, which is that sentence with the scope widened from a week to twenty years and nothing else changed. **The clause was removed and not revoiced, because the standing is that a revoicing of a restatement produces a second one and only reading catches both.** The paragraph's second sentence, *There is nothing in twenty years of that which either of them would want set down anywhere*, was also **an unhedged narration-layer claim about what two people would want, which is standing eight: a claim about what a person knows or would want rather than about what a person did, and no instrument here can see it.** It is replaced with a claim about the world, that a day of the week cannot be entered as anything but itself.

**Three: `chapter-0432.md:41` asserted, in the same construction as an added line in the chapter before, that nobody came up behind the young man while he stood there.** `chapter-0431.md:47`, an added line, already reads *nobody came up behind him and nobody sent him up*. **This one is invisible to two instruments by construction rather than by setting: the intra-file longest-common-run scan scans within one file and the two lines are in two files, and the run is four tokens, which is under the twelve-word cross-file index's window.** A cross-file scan of the range's added lines against each other was built to look for the class, and it returned a longest run of **six tokens** between any two added lines in different files, with the six being *nothing was carried out of the* between `chapter-0437.md` and `chapter-0440.md` and every other cross-file pair at four or five tokens and all of them the manuscript's stock connectives — *and nobody in the room*, *and nobody has ever*, *in the room and*, *the far end of*. **So the class is rare, it is real, and four tokens is where it lives; a twelve-word window cannot see it and a five-word scan of the manuscript's stock connectives would drown in it.** The duplicate went out of `chapter-0432.md` and `chapter-0431.md` keeps it, because 0431 is the chapter the young man is standing in and 0432 is the chapter after.

**Why every instrument passed all three.** `lifts` looks for a shared twelve-to-twenty-four-token run against another chapter and none of the three paragraphs shares one. The intra-file scan reports the longest shared run between an added line and any other prose line in the same file, and the two restatements on `chapter-0439.md` share four tokens with the paragraphs they collide with — *not one word*, *a hand and out of*, *there is no* — all under the six-word floor. The twelve-word cross-file index cannot see a restatement inside one file at all. The added-prose construction guard counts `that`-nouns and is blind to all three. **A restatement is a shared fact and not a shared string, and every index in this repository looks for shared strings; item 185 named that in a different dress, when it found a paragraph that contradicted a base line by sharing a fact and no words, and this is the same instrument-shaped blind spot reached from the other end.**

**Round two.** The revoicing that fixed it left an eight-word run, *one and nobody has ever been asked to*, held by **one chapter in two volumes** with this range excluded on the prose selector, which is below the four-and-four threshold and therefore this dispatch's sentence and not the register. **The frame came out of the sentence rather than the words moving inside it, which is item 173W on the twenty-seventh range running, and that is the fourth time in this repair that the fix has worked.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter

NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(431,441)]
```

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `2b015ee`. `chapter-0450.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure in this section because it carries the last line of Volume 09 and is not this repair's to move.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "2b015ee"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))                              # selector THEN stripped
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
```

### The ninth file, and it is a base defect this repair cannot touch

**`chapter-0447.md` is the one file of the nine whose quoted spans are not byte-identical at base and now, and the cause is in the base and not in this repair.** The base of `chapter-0447.md` carries an **odd** number of quotation marks — **17** — because the paragraph at base line 29 opens with a mark and closes with `**` and has no closing mark: it ends `...the one who decided.**`. The regex therefore pairs that opening mark with the opening mark of base line 31 as though it were a closing one, and every mark after that point is paired wrongly. **The quote-character count is 17 at the base and 17 now, the span count is 8 at the base and 8 now, spans one to seven are byte-identical, and the only delta is that the trailing malformed span grew from 167 to 305 characters because quoteless narration was inserted into the region the broken pairing had swallowed.**

**This repair cannot fix it: the fix is the addition of one character to a base line, and the gate is zero `replace` and zero `delete` against `2b015ee`. It is therefore carried, per standing seven, and it is named here so that no later pass treats the 0447 span delta as damage this pass did.** It is the second time in this repair that a base-text defect has made a gate unevaluable on one file of a range, and the transferable finding is that **the span-for-span gate has to be checked on the quote-character count as well as on the span list, and a file whose base has an odd mark count cannot be gated on the span list at all.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)

        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]

NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(421,431)]
```

## Three: the two defects, both found by reading, and one of them is a flat contradiction of base text

**Every instrument in this repository returned clean on both. The intra-file scan returns zero at six tokens on both, the twelve-word cross-file index returns zero on both, `lifts` reports one of them at six words, and the added-prose `NONNOUN` guard returns zero on both. All four are blind to the class both belong to, and standing one and item 192's reading finding are the whole of the method here.**

### The first: `chapter-0425.md:39`, a flat contradiction of eight base lines

The added paragraph said a person standing at a shut door in that street "can be heard by every window on both sides of it **and by nobody inside either building**." **The chapter is the one in which the man inside that building hears her twice and says so.** Base `:23` puts the voice in the street below; base `:31` is his `"I heard you."`; base `:33` is `"I know you did. I said it to the door and the door is not anybody."`; base `:37` has him speaking back "to the door and not to the street"; base `:47` has him "hear it move across about nine foot of pavement and stop where the step was"; base `:51` has the second of the two true things "said to a woman who was on the step". **An added clause asserting that nobody inside either building can hear her is contradicted by the scene it sits inside, and a contradiction is not a repetition, so no index in this repository can reach it by construction.**

It now reads that a person standing on a step in that street "can be heard by every window on both sides of it and by anybody inside a shut door, and nothing gets back out through one", which is what the base says and what the chapter's own argument is — the shut door stops nothing coming in and everything going out, which is base `:33` and base `:43` in the page's own words. **The paragraph's work is kept entire, no base line was touched, and the fact kept is the fact the base carries.**

### The second: `chapter-0430.md:15`, a restatement of base line 3 in four of its five clauses

Base `:3` is the chapter's opening frame and is set in bold: "**The fourth of the four on that wall board is the one none of the three of them can account for … The board behind that counter has carried four items for eleven years and not one of the four is time, and the three of them have between them looked at the fourth of those items and have never once agreed on what it is for.**" The added paragraph twelve lines below re-anchored four of those five facts — four items, looked at every morning for eleven years, the three of them, never once agreed about the fourth of the four — and its longest shared run with base `:3` is **three tokens**, `the fourth of`, which is under the five-token floor item 192 lowered the intra-file scan to. **A restatement with its words changed shares no run with anything, so the intra-file scan is silent by construction and not by setting.**

It now reads: "**Four items is a small amount of paper to look at twice a day for eleven years, and agreeing about the fourth of them is a thing three people can do in about a minute, and nobody has ever said out loud that the case and the board could be moved.**" **The three beats the added paragraph carried and the base did not — the smallness of the attention, the minute it would take three people to agree, and the case and the board nobody has ever proposed moving — are all kept, the re-anchoring is gone, and the opening frame is the only statement of itself in the chapter.**

## Zero: what the review put, and that all four of it were confirmed before any of them was touched

The review of this phase put four defects and one observation about the pipeline, and it was right on all four and wrong on the observation. **Its own central claim is a negative one — that a numerator in `state/current.md` was invented — and a negative claim about a measurement is the hardest kind to make and the easiest to accept by reflex, so it was re-derived here from the method rather than taken.** Every figure below was produced by running the method `state/batch-summary.md` prints whole under the heading *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0411 TO 0420, MEASURED RECORD*, against the live tree and against each of two historical revisions of it.

## One: the method, printed whole, because the defect was a figure and not a sentence

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, glob, importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
FORMS = ["those boards", "that lane", "that floor", "that table", "that door",
         "that stair", "that room", "that passage", "that tin", "that sheet"]
files = sorted(glob.glob("chapters/volume-09/*.md"))
words = hits = w49 = h49 = 0
for p in files:
    words += m.words_in_file(p)
    body = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", open(p).read(), flags=re.M)))
    hits += sum(len(re.findall(r"\b" + re.escape(f) + r"\b", body, flags=re.I)) for f in FORMS)
    if not p.endswith("chapter-0450.md"):
        w49 += m.words_in_file(p)
        h49 += sum(len(re.findall(r"\b" + re.escape(f) + r"\b", body, flags=re.I)) for f in FORMS)
print(f"all fifty  {words:>9,} words  {hits:>4} hits  {hits*1000.0/words:>6.2f} per 1,000")
print(f"forty-nine {w49:>9,} words  {h49:>4} hits  {h49*1000.0/w49:>6.2f} per 1,000")
EOF
```

**Historical revisions are measured by materialising all fifty files of the volume out of the commit and running the same method over them, never over a diff and never over a paragraph.** A count taken over a diff is a count of the lines the diff inserted, and it is a different quantity from a count over a volume.

```python
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]

NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def m3(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(431,441)]
```
