## Four: the six defects, and every one of them of a class no instrument in this repository can see

**Six came out of this range's own added prose, and the six were found by reading and by nothing else. `lifts`, the twelve-word cross-file index, the intra-file longest-common-run scan, the added-prose `NONNOUN` guard, the per-file form delta, `reprints`, `calendar`, `words` and `selftest` were all clean on every one of them.**

**One, `chapter-0431.md:15`, a claim that the base contradicts four paragraphs later.** The added paragraph opened by ending *Nobody spoke in the corridor at any hour of it*, and its own first sentence had set the frame *Before it came up the morning had gone the way it goes*, so the nearest noun to *it* was the morning. **Base `:75` says he *had just said out loud, in a corridor nine feet long*, and the chapter carries nine quoted spans of speech in that corridor, so a reader who takes *it* as the morning reads a flat contradiction of both.** The fact was true of the run-up and false of the morning, and the fix binds the window instead of denying the fact: the two sentences are now one, *Before it came up the morning had gone the way it goes and not one word had been said in the corridor.* **Word-neutral, 22 words for 22.**

**Two, `chapter-0433.md:37`, an act performed that the base then un-performs.** The added paragraph said she *waited about as long as she had waited and then she went, and she went the way she goes, which is down the stairs and out*. **She cannot have gone: the chapter carries six quoted spans below that line, at `:43`, `:45`, `:61`, `:63`, `:65` and `:67`, and the range's own added paragraph at `:59` says he *did not pick the pen up again before she left*, which is the same contradiction from the other end.** Standing one, and this is its second form on this range: not a restatement and not a re-performance of an adjacent paragraph, but a performed act that the chapter then goes on without. The fix keeps the fact — the length of the waiting, and the habitual way she goes — and stops claiming the departure: *and then she stopped, and she goes the way she goes*.

**Three, `chapter-0433.md:59`, a claim about the hour that the paragraph above it fixes.** The base line directly above says he *put his pen down about a quarter of an hour before the six*, and the added sentence said *the high window was giving the same light it gives at the fourth hour*, which puts the same room at two hours of an afternoon at once. **This is the class item 176's re-audit called a claim that could have contradicted a later line in the same chapter, and here it contradicted the line above.** The clause is out and the rest of the sentence stands; fifteen words gone.

**Four, `chapter-0434.md:19`, a restatement of the paragraph above it, in the file with the second-tightest free-line budget.** The added paragraph opened *The counter where she said it does not sell anything he uses and he has not bought anything at it since, and he was not going to be this week either*, and the base paragraph above ends *he did not buy a copy of anything that week and he is not going to buy one this week either*. **Same fact, same terms, same refusal, in the same breath — standing one in its plainest form, and this repair has been told twice on this range that it is the commonest defect here.** The whole first sentence is out and what remains is the wall: *Four feet of wall on one side of him and a window on the other, and nothing on the wall at any hour of any day of the two years, and nothing has ever been driven into it but the nail.* **The removal also took a seven-word lift with it**, `and he was not going to be` at seven words against `chapter-0021.md`, **and the ambiguous pronoun went with the rest: the old sentence ended *the only thing in the room that was ever put into it*, and the nearest antecedent to *it* was the room and the only thing ever put into a room is a man.**

**Five, `chapter-0435.md:47`, a claim about silence that the base breaks four lines later.** The added paragraph said *nothing was said across the nine foot of deal between the near end and the far end* and held it *for the rest of the morning*. **Base `:49` is Marn Ottery at the near end saying *"You are all going to be very quiet now," "The two of you"*, which crosses that nine foot to the far end, and `:59`, `:65` and `:67` are three more exchanges across the same floor.** The clause is now *and the far end of the boards did not take it up*, which is what base `:45` already says of the clerk and which nothing below contradicts.

**Six, `chapter-0436.md:35`, an invented observation sitting against a base line that marks the same thing.** The added paragraph said *the second line was in the same hand as every other line in the book*, and base `:31` says the second line *was in her own hand*. **The base's phrase marks the line as the nineteen-year-old's; the added clause asserts that it is indistinguishable from the fifty-three-year-old's writing throughout a book that has been hers for about eighteen years, which is a fact about the world that is nowhere on the page and that a reader has no way to check.** The clause is out and the paragraph's point — nobody asked how long it had been on the page — is untouched.

**Two findings were read, considered and left standing, and the reason is written down so that a later pass does not take them for oversights.** `chapter-0436.md:23` opens *What the rota says and what the list of clerks says are two different documents* and then says *she is on neither of them*, which base `:19` has already said; **the paragraph is not a restatement, because its second half is new — *she came in on neither* — and that half is the only place in the paragraph where the fact is load-bearing, so removing the hinge would remove the fact's only carrier.** And `chapter-0438.md:43` ends *a person who leaves one empty for two months is not doing anything a person could be shown doing*, which shares its ground with base `:41`; **that is the volume's register and not a restatement of it, and a repair that cut it would be reducing the voice, which no phase in this repair is permitted to do.**

## Five: the guard caught this pass twice, and one of the two was a check of my own that was wrong

**The added-prose `NONNOUN` guard ran before every write as well as after it, on the proposed text in isolation and tokenised, and it did not fire once on the six revoicings — but the first draft of the `chapter-0434.md` revoicing would have fired it and was caught before anything was written to disk.** The draft read *the nail is the only thing in that room that has ever been put into the wall*, and it carries `that room`, a cell of the closed list of ten, and `that has`, a relative-clause opener on a verb that is not in `NONNOUN` and therefore a sweep bigram no reader would ever see. **Two instances in one sentence, both of them the tic this repair has been chasing since the range behind yours, caught by the guard and not by the lists, which would have shown the aggregate flat.** The landed sentence carries neither.

**The intra-file longest-common-run scan caught this pass once and the fix was a revoicing rather than a decision to leave it.** The `chapter-0435.md` fix produced a six-word overlap with base `:45`, `at the far end of the`, which is the room's own stock phrase and is below nothing: **six words is the floor the scan reports and the range stood at zero pairs at six words before this pass and one after its first attempt, and that is a regression this repair does not accept on a stock phrase either.** The clause was revoiced a second time to *the far end of the boards*, and the scan returned to zero.

**And one instrument of this pass was wrong in the direction of comfort before it was believed, and the standing for it is already in this file.** The twelve-word cross-file index first returned **2,782 hits** on a range whose repaired prose is the manuscript's own. **The cause was this pass's own filename slicing: `path[-8:-3]` on `chapters/volume-09/chapter-0440.md` returns `-0440` and not `0440`, so the exclusion of the range under repair never fired and every one of the ten files was in its own index.** That is item 211's instrument fault in a third costume — the same index, the same shape of mistake, taken on the path instead of on the volume — **and it is the reason the plant below is not optional: the index did not return zero, it returned two thousand seven hundred and eighty-two, and had the range been believed at the value the instrument first gave, seven of the ten chapters would have been rewritten to remove phrases they do not contain.**

## Nine: what the canon held, what is carried unrepaired, and what is left

**The four volume-wide refusals held. No hearing and no arrangement of one appears anywhere in the added prose; no new heading is printed over anything and no new form exists for anything; no House, seat or office is named; no romance is present or implied; and no number that is not on the page is printed.** The movement's own plan held: the sheet with no column is where the volume's oldest wound is, the form that came through a letter slot in Chapter 0389 is not touched here and does not appear in this range's added prose, and a filled-in blank requires nothing of the man of about sixty-one.

**The locks held. The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void anywhere in the added prose. The question on the shelf in `chapter-0436.md` stays a question and carries no full stop, and finding six took the added clause that sat nearest it without touching it. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed and neither is the hand that struck it. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this range pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. # THE THIRD DISPATCH ON CHAPTERS 0441 TO 0449, MEASURED RECORD — A RANGE ALREADY REPAIRED TWICE OVER, SIX DEFECTS TAKEN OUT OF ITS OWN ADDED PROSE, AND THE ORDER OF TWO OPERATIONS WHICH IS THE FINDING

## Zero: the precheck, and the tenth time a prompt in this repair has handed a phase that answer

**This is a repair, not a batch, not a close, not a review, not a second reading and not an outline phase, and it planned no volume: the manuscript is complete at six hundred and twenty chapters, `outline/series.md` says in terms that there is no next volume, and there is no Volume 13.** `chapter-0400.md`, `chapter-0421.md` to `chapter-0440.md`, `chapter-0450.md` and `chapter-0620.md` were read and not opened, and the prose of the repaired ranges behind this one was not used as a base for anything here.

## Two: the finding, and it is about the order of two operations

**This phase ran the `NONNOUN` sweep guard before it wrote and the cross-file lift guard after, and the consequence was that the three paragraphs written to remove three six-word frames were each replaced by fresh runs.** Three at seven words and three at six, all held by one or two chapters in one or two volumes, and **the twelve-word index that had been zero was no longer zero at any of the twelve, seven or six word window sizes.** The three offenders, named so the failure is legible: on the replacement of `chapter-0447.md:17`, `it and he did not move it` at seven words and `and neither of them put anything into` at seven; on the replacement of `chapter-0441.md:75`, `did not look down at it` at six; and on the replacement of `chapter-0448.md:15`, `it for the length of a` at six.

**Item 209 wrote the rule down after three of its own eighteen revoicings created a fresh defect while removing another: a revoicing has to clear the cross-file holder count, the added-prose sweep count and the intra-file run *before* it is written and not once after. This is the first time in this repair that a phase has been handed that rule in its prompt, has built the guard, and has run it on the wrong side of the disk anyway. A guard run after the write is not a guard, it is a report.**

**The fix, and the numbers on it.** A screening pass was built and every candidate was put through it before anything reached the file. It runs the sweep on the added prose, every cross-file window at nine, eight, seven and six words with item 211's non-empty-holder condition, the intra-file longest-common run against every other prose line in the file, the echo against every other added paragraph in the same file, the fifteen prohibited floor materials, and the digit, question-mark, bold-mark and first-person checks. **Fifteen candidates were screened and eleven were rejected; four came back clean and four were written.** The eleven rejections are the useful half, because they are the same frames returning in new clothing: `that step`, `that hour`, `that held` and `that table` each put a sweep form into a sentence that had none, and `the ordinary quiet of a street`, `it and the two of them stood`, `nothing to do about it and`, `it the whole of the time` and `it every working day of that` each reproduced a below-threshold run at six or seven words. **A revoicing that removes a frame tends to install another one in the same clause, and the only instrument that says so is one standing in front of the sentence.**

**Two of this pass's own guards were wrong and both failed in the direction of comfort, and both are recorded because they are the two classes this repair has now hit repeatedly.** The blank-line separation check was written `if i==0 or not c[i-1].strip(): FAIL`, which **fails a paragraph whose line above is blank and passes one whose line above is not**; it reported thirty-six failures on a range where all thirty-six added paragraphs carry a blank line above them, and the corrected check returns zero. That is the third instance of the inversion this repair has recorded. And the guard calibration itself: **the refusal test asked the insert helper to accept anchor 11 on `chapter-0441.md` and the helper refused it, because line 11 is a `---` — and the helper was right and the test was wrong.** Nothing was written by either fault, because both were caught by reading the output. **A guard has to be calibrated against the file it will actually edit and not against a file whose line numbers were assumed: a test that asserts the wrong answer to a correct guard reads as an inverted guard, the repair stops for no reason, and a repair that stops for no reason is how an unfinished repair comes to exist on disk with no record of it.**

## Three: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `2b015ee` and the landed commit is `077076a`. `chapter-0450.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure in this section because it carries the last line of Volume 09 and is not this repair's to move, and it is byte-identical to `2b015ee` at md5 `399b4e32a56681168e5bd2cf2fdae60d` and appears in no diff printed anywhere in this record.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "2b015ee"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def b3(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
    L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))                              # selector THEN stripped
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
```

The columns are cumulative — the ten, then the ten plus the thirteen, then the ten plus the thirteen plus the two — so that each column's cells add to it and to nothing else:**

## Four: an instrument finding about the printed method, and it is against the record above

**The method this repair prints joins nine chapters' token streams with one space, and on this range that join manufactures a sweep bigram no reader would ever see.** `chapter-0441.md`'s method-3 stream ends on the token `that` — the last word of a bold closing sentence — and `chapter-0442.md`'s begins on the token `chapter`, because `b3()` strips date lines from the raw text and does not use `m.prose_lines`, so a chapter's own title line is counted as prose. Joined with a single space the two produce `that chapter`. **Run as printed over the joined string the range reads 202 sweep instances across 74 forms; summed per file it reads 201 across 73, and every record of this range from item 204 onward prints 201 and 73. The figure of record is right and the printed code over-reports it by one, and the two disagree on a range where not one form has moved.** The fix is to sum per file. The transferable half is that **a method which concatenates its inputs has to be checked for a bigram that exists only at a concatenation boundary, and this repair's sweep is precisely a bigram measure, so the two facts are the same fact.**

```python
import re, importlib.util
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "2b015ee"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
```

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`. The method is pasted and not rebuilt, from the section headed *THE PROSE REPAIR OF CHAPTERS 0421 TO 0430, MEASURED RECORD*.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "cb7fce7"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def m3(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(431,441)]
def lists(t, sel=m3):     # the list counts are read off the sweep Counter's own whole-word match,
    sw = sweep(sel(t))     # NOT off str.count, which matches a prefix inside a longer form
    return (sum(sw[x] for x in TEN), sum(sw[x] for x in TEN+ADD),
            sum(sw[x] for x in TEN+ADD+NEW), sum(sw.values()), len(sw), sw)
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record and it does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and they were not added; that is item 173C's standing and a copy that grew by those three words under-reports this sweep. It is pasted and not rebuilt. `to` is not in it either.**

**One instrument was wrong before it was believed, and it is the sixth time in this repair that a clean-looking answer has turned out to be a fault in the direction of comfort.** This pass first computed the three lists as `sum(s.count(form) for form in FORMS)` over the joined token string and got a range total of **53** for the closed list of ten, where the figure of record is **55**. The cause is that `str.count` is a substring match and does not respect a token boundary: it counts `that floor` inside `that flooring`, and `that house` inside `that household`. **The record's per-form cells sum to 55 and the range total read 53, and the two could not be reconciled, which is how it was caught.** The list counts are read off the sweep's own `\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b` match, which is whole-word, and with that corrected every figure reproduces to the digit. **A per-file total and a per-form table that disagree is not a rounding, and the standing is that the list counts come from the sweep Counter and never from `str.count`.**

## Four: the one defect, and it is of a class no instrument in this repository can see

**`chapter-0437.md:29`, an added paragraph this repair wrote itself, said that the front bench of that shed was not made up, and the base of the same chapter says a man is chained to it.**

The line as it stood, quoted plain and without this record's own emphasis, which is the convention a quoted chapter line takes here: the light off the lane came past the open side and reached about the middle of the floor and no further, and he worked in what the light reached and she worked where she worked, and neither of them went behind it. Nothing was carried out of the shed in the hour before she came and nothing was carried in afterwards, and the front bench was not made up at either end of the hour. **The offending clause is not this pass's prose and the date of it is `85cb861`, which is item 220's landed commit; the check of the word against the manuscript was made before this pass's own edit was written, and an earlier draft of this section said it was made before the offending clause itself was written, which misdates it by a dispatch.**

**`chapter-0437.md:3`, base, twenty-six lines above it: *"That building is the same one it was the last time anybody wrote a word about it. The light comes off the lane and off a wall standing a few foot past the open side, and the bench at the front takes a man lying down if he goes on his side. The chain is across the front of it and the chain is on him."*** **An earlier draft of this section called that a flat contradiction of a canon sentence in the same chapter and made it the tenth instance of item 209's class. That classification was wrong and is withdrawn. Base `:3` does not say the bench is made up — it says a man is chained to it and can lie on it — and a chained man on a bare bench is entirely consistent with the bench not being made up, so the added sentence contradicts nothing the chapter states. What it does is apply a bedding term to a bench nine lines after the chapter put a man on that bench, three paragraphs after it did so, and that is a clash of register and an ambiguity, not a contradiction.**

**The word was checked against the whole manuscript, and it is not an ambiguous English word here.** `made up` in the sense of a bed appears **seven** times in Volume 12 — `chapters/volume-12/chapter-0587.md:11`, `0594.md:9`, `0599.md:9`, `0601.md:15`, `0603.md:9`, `0607.md:9` and `0619.md:9`, seven files and one line each, from `grep -rn "made up" chapters/volume-12/ | grep -i bed` — **and in every one of those seven it is the negative that is used, on a bed that is empty.** A further Volume 12 occurrence at `0615.md:43` is the unrelated sense *not a thing anybody made up*, and the eleven other manuscript-wide occurrences are the invented-or-composed sense, so the load-bearing fact is seven for seven and **an earlier draft of this section said eleven, which was the manuscript-wide count and not the bed count.** The same shed's canon puts a chained man on that same bench twice more: `chapter-0412.md:3` *"There is a chain across the front of the front bench and a man on the other side of it"* and `chapter-0421.md:3` *"There is a chain across the front of that bench and the chain is on the man at that bench."* **So the added sentence contradicted its own chapter's opening, and two other chapters of the same volume, in a phrase whose sense this manuscript has fixed eleven times.**

**This is item 209's class exactly — *"a flat contradiction of a canon sentence in the same chapter"* — and it is the tenth time this repair has produced that class. Every instrument in this repository returned clean on it**: the construction lists do not move, `lifts` does not see a contradiction, the intra-file scan shares no run with `:3` beyond four tokens, the twelve-word index cannot see it because **a contradiction is not a repetition**, and no instrument here looks at what a chapter says.

**The fix, and the paragraph's work kept and the sentence changed.** It now reads: *"and **nothing at the front was moved** at either end of the hour."* The clause's work — that the room's fittings were not disturbed across the hour — is unchanged, `at the front` is the chapter's own base noun-phrase from `:3`, and **no figure, no age, no date, no distance, no question mark, no bold marker, no quoted span and no floor material entered the file.** It is word-negative against the line it replaced: **the range is one word shorter than item 220 left it and two words shorter than this pass's own first attempt.**

**And this is the second half of the finding, which is the transferable half: the first correction for this defect was not written, and it was caught by testing the candidate against the indices before it touched the disk.** The first wording tried was *"and nothing at the front of it was moved at either end of the hour"*, which is true and contradicts nothing. **It introduces `at the front of it`, a five-word run held by thirteen chapters across nine volumes, and the five-word `either` re-print bucket moved from 3,953 to 3,954 when it was written.** It was written once, measured, found to have created a defect while removing another, and revoiced before the commit. ## Five: three readings checked and left standing, with their reasons, so a later pass does not take them for oversights

**`chapter-0431.md:95`, "It lay where he had left it for the better part of two hours … and nobody came back for it or asked after it in between."** The base clock of this chapter is the third hour to the sixth for the signing (`:3`), the fourth hour on the date line (`:7`), the odd sheet arriving "about half way through that morning" (`:11`), the fifth hour at `:79`, and the basket down at the seventh hour (`:99`). **The interval is consistent with that clock and is this repair's own figure rather than the base's, which is item 198's class — and the base's own hours are third, fourth, fifth and seventh, so "the better part of two hours" between the fifth and the seventh is a floor and not a ceiling.** The "nobody" clauses are about *saying* and about *asking after*, and `:79` has the man of about sixty-one come back **to the sill** and put his palm flat on it and say the fourth thing to the pot, which is a different act from coming back for the sheet. **Checked and left standing.**

**`chapter-0439.md:25`, "There was never an arrangement about the door and there is not one now, and the door was never the point of it."** Two lines below it, base and in capitals, the same chapter says *"The reason is not that anybody in that house is kind. The reason is that **the arrangement worked for nine years on being unfindable**."* **The two sentences are about two different things and the added one is careful about the difference: the base's arrangement is about her being unfindable, and the added one denies an arrangement *about the door* and says the door was never the point, which is the base's own position.** `:3` puts the door unopened at the top of that stair for twenty years and `:39` gives twenty years as the term of what she has. **Checked and left standing: a distinction and not a contradiction.**

**`chapter-0437.md:57`, "She did not wait for anything and she went out to the lane …",** against base `:55` two lines above it, *"He said nothing to that and she did not wait and nobody thanked her for it."* **This is the plainest form standing one takes and it is the one judgement on this range that could go the other way.** It was left standing for three reasons recorded so the next pass can disagree with them: **the shared run is four tokens, `she did not wait`, under the scan's floor; the volume's own method is anaphoric and repeats a beat inside a sentence on purpose** — `:41` gives *"nobody in that lane has standing to ask it to be void and nobody has asked"* and `:51` gives *"nobody had asked her for it and nobody asked her for anything after"* in base prose; **and the paragraph's work is distinct from `:55`'s**, which is about him not answering and about nobody thanking her, where `:57`'s is about the lane, about the shed not changing and about the man not turning his head. **Checked and left standing.**

**`lifts` names two holders it does not have, and that is this dispatch's second instrument finding: it reports runs it has assembled out of windows that are not adjacent in the chapter it names.** It reports `the far end of the boards did not` at `chapter-0435.md:47` as held by **`chapter-0487.md`**, and `it and not one of the two` at `chapter-0438.md:15` as held by **`chapter-0356.md`**. **Neither holder has the run.** `chapter-0487.md:3` reads *"since before the woman at the far end of the boards came to that floor"* — the three words are there and `did not` is not, and the two are not adjacent. `chapter-0356.md:37` reads *"and not one of the two is going to start"* — `not one of the two` is there and the `it and` in front of it is not. **A literal contiguous whole-word search over all six hundred and twenty chapters on the prose selector returns `chapter-0435.md` alone for the first run and `chapter-0438.md` alone for the second, so neither has a holder outside this range and neither is a lift.** **The mechanism is new, and it is not item 209's case-folding asymmetry, which cannot produce this: a lowercased query loses a match against a key carrying capitals and cannot invent one. `build_lift_index` keys an n-gram on its TEXT and keeps no offset, and the growing intersection in `longest_lift` is taken over chapters and not over positions, so consecutive n-grams of one run can be satisfied from different places in the same chapter.** Measured on the two holders themselves: `chapter-0487.md` holds `far end of the boards` at token offset **55** and `end of the boards did` at token offset **692**, six hundred and thirty-seven tokens apart, and the intersection passes anyway; `chapter-0356.md` holds `it and not one of` at offset **856** and `not one of the two` at offset **785**, seventy-one apart. **The docstring on `longest_lift` claims the answer is always a run that exists whole in one chapter rather than a run stitched out of several, and that claim is false.** This is the mechanism behind item 216's symptom, pinned for the first time, and **it is a false-positive generator in the direction of FINDING a lift, which is the opposite of item 209's and of every other instrument fault recorded in this repair.** **`tools/measure.py` was not edited: it is the instrument every figure in this record was taken with, and changing it inside a record would silently restate every prior range's numbers.** The standing is that a `lifts` hit is a claim and not a finding, and that the cheapest way to rule one is a literal contiguous search of the named holder at the named offset, which is one command and is not `grep` on raw text.

**And one more instrument was wrong before it was believed, in the same direction as the others.** Measuring `and that is the whole of what` on the whole-file text with a literal-space regex returns **144** chapters, against **145** on the prose selector and against the 145 the record gives at three points on this tree. **The 144 is this pass's own error: the run spans a line break in one chapter, so a regex that requires a literal space cannot see it, while tokenising the file as one stream can.** Measured properly, on the prose selector and on the whole-file token stream, the figure is **145 chapters across 12 volumes at both**, and **`there is no form anywhere in this` is 212 chapters across 10 volumes at both.** **The record's 145 stands, the prompt's 144 was already wrong before it was printed, and neither figure was moved by this pass.** That is the second time this sentence has been corrected in this repair and a figure corrected once is not a figure that cannot go stale again in the same repository.

import re, importlib.util
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)

        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]

NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(L for _, L in m.prose_lines(t) if not is_date(L))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `cb7fce7`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)

        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def b3(t):   # the figure of record: the selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def b1(t):   # the selector alone, unstripped
    return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))
def b2(t):   # body_strip as printed in earlier records
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(431,441)]
```

### Four one: `lifts`, and three faults in it, the third of which is new to this repair

**`measure.py` is not edited.** It is shared by every figure in every record in this repository, and a mid-repair change to it would silently move figures asserted elsewhere. **The standing is that each fault is recorded, a corrected harness is used for this range's rulings, and both numbers are printed.** The corrected harness is the same 5-gram seed and the same cap of 24, with **the index built per prose line rather than per chapter and case-folded on both sides** — that is, the query side and the index side are measured the same way, which is the whole of the correction.

**Fault one, item 207's, and it still costs a hit.** `cmd_lifts` lowercases the tokens it queries with and `build_lift_index` stores its keys un-lowercased, so a run carrying a capitalised word cannot match. **On this range the affected line is `chapter-0431.md:15` and the run is `not one word had been said`, six words, held by `chapter-0504.md:65`, which begins `Not one word had been said to either of them`.** The corrected harness reports **36** added lines at six words or over against `measure.py`'s **35**, and the extra one is that line.

**Fault two, item 216's and item 223's, and it is three of the thirty-five.** `build_lift_index` extends one flat token list across a whole chapter, skipping blanks, `---`, headings and the date line **without breaking the token stream at a line boundary**, while `cmd_lifts` queries one line at a time; and `longest_lift` grows a run while the *holder sets* intersect rather than requiring the holder to contain the reported string. **So a run can be reported whose windows are adjacent only in the holder's flattened stream, across a line boundary the selector itself treats as a boundary.** On this range that is exactly three: **`chapter-0435.md:47` at eight words, `the far end of the boards did not`; `chapter-0436.md:71` at seven, `is the whole of it and the`; `chapter-0438.md:15` at seven, `it and not one of the two`.** Checked by asking whether the reported run is contiguous in a single prose line of the named holder, **all thirty-four others are and these three are not, and `grep -c "the far end of the boards did not" chapters/volume-10/chapter-0487.md` returns 0**, so the holder `measure.py` names for the first does not hold it in any form.

**Fault three is new to this repair and it is about the column the instrument prints rather than the count it computes.** `cmd_lifts` reports one holder as `next(iter(held))` over a `set` of paths, and **Python's string hashing is randomised per process, so the named holder is not reproducible across runs on the same tree.** Run on this tree with `PYTHONHASHSEED` at 0, 1, 2 and 3, **`chapter-0439.md:25`'s named holder reads `chapter-0609`, `chapter-0487`, `chapter-0487`, `chapter-0487` on the first and `chapter-0498`, `chapter-0498`, `chapter-0206`, `chapter-0211` for the ten-word register run — four different answers for the same line on the same tree.** **Every holder figure this repair has recorded from `measure.py`'s printed column is therefore a claim about one process, and the transferable standing is that the holder COUNT is deterministic and the holder NAME is not, so a record must print the count and the quoted list and never the instrument's name.** Item 192's standing said to quote the holder list at the four-and-four threshold; this widens it to **every** threshold, because at any threshold the instrument's own name is one arbitrary member of the set.

**Every hit, with its classification and its holder list on the exact token string. Six are register and stand as named survivors; one is above threshold on chapters and below on volumes and is quoted; twenty-six are below threshold and ruled as item 207 ruled them, which is that chasing a seven-word window held by one chapter is the failure item 189 rules out in the other direction; and two are the assembly artefacts of fault two.**

### Four two: the twelve-word cross-file index, zero, and the zero proved three ways

**Built over the range's own added prose only, the range excluded from its own corpus, on `m.TOKEN` tokens, case-folded, per prose line. It reports any twelve-word run in this pass's added prose held by another chapter at fewer than four chapters across fewer than four volumes. It returns zero.**

**It was proved three ways and the standing is that a scan returning zero is a claim and not a fact.** A verbatim **fifteen-word run lifted out of `chapter-0050.md`** — *"three things stood in the way the request of the eighteenth of the ninth month"* — was written into `chapter-0431.md` at line 15 and the index returned **4 hits** instead of 0, **the same run truncated to eleven words returned 0**, and the file was restored with the restoration asserted and `git diff --numstat cb7fce7 -- chapters/volume-09/chapter-0431.md` re-run to confirm the tree. **The plant works, the window is twelve and not eleven, and the zero is real.**

### Four three: the intra-file longest-common-run scan, zero at six words, and the zero proved

**For every line this pass added, and every other prose line in the same file, the longest contiguous run of `m.TOKEN` tokens the two lines share, case-folded, date lines excluded; every pair at six words or over is reported.** **It returns nothing at six words and 24 pairs at exactly five, all of them the room's own stock phrase.**

**This pass's edit took it from one pair at nine words to zero, and the pair it removed is the finding.** `chapter-0439.md:25` held `there is no form anywhere in this empire for` — **nine words — with `chapter-0439.md:15`, a base line in the same chapter.** That is standing one in its plainest form: a re-performance of a base line's act inside the base line's own chapter, and **the scan found it at nine words, which is the only instrument in this repository that can see this class at all.**

**The zero was proved by a second plant, and this one had to be planted from the same file** — the first attempt planted a run taken from another chapter and correctly did not move the intra-file scan, which is what an intra-file scan is for. A verbatim **twelve-word run from a base prose line of `chapter-0431.md` itself** was then written into an added line of the same file and the scan returned **1 pair at twelve words** instead of 0, and the file was restored with the restoration asserted. **Both zeros are planted, both plants work, and both are restored.**

## Five: the finding in the record layer above this one, and it is a holder count item 207 printed on a probe that was not the token window

**Item 207 recorded, of `is the whole of it and the` at `chapter-0436.md:71`: *"11 chapters across 6 volumes on the prose selector, holders `chapter-0098`, `-0168`, `-0183`, `-0184`, `-0192`, `-0245`, `-0248`, `-0353`, `-0461`, `-0588`, `-0619`, quoted rather than counted because the two probes disagree."* It quoted the list, which was the right instinct, and the list is wrong.**

**The corrected count on the exact token string is 2 chapters across 2 volumes — `chapter-0245.md` and `chapter-0353.md` — and the other nine named chapters do not hold it.** They hold `is the whole of it and there`, which is a different seven words: `chapter-0098.md:75` reads *"and that is the whole of it, and there is a girl of seventeen"*, `chapter-0183.md:61` reads *"a district has to know who is in it that is the whole of it and there is no villain in it"*, and the same shape runs through the rest. **`grep -c "is the whole of it and the" chapters/volume-02/chapter-0098.md` returns 0 and the string is on the page, because the page has a comma inside the run at *whole of it, and there*.** That is standing four in its purest form and it is not a hypothetical: **a literal-string probe and a token probe disagree about the same twenty-six characters of the same file, the first says the chapter does not hold the run and the second says it holds a different run, and the first is the obvious way of checking.**

**And this pass was caught by the same fault in its own instrument before it reached a ruling, which is why it is worth printing.** A first probe of the corrected counts reported `either of the two of them` at **29 chapters across 8 volumes** where the answer is **6 across 4**, and it was traced to a character-offset containment test that sliced `seg[j:j+len(run)]` out of a joined token string — **`len(run)` is a character count being used to index a token string, so the slice landed inside the token `there` and returned `is the whole of it and the` as a substring of a string that does not contain it.** That is exactly the fault `measure.py`'s own selftest plant 6 exists for — *"no token begins one character into a word: the failure this plant exists for is a chopped capital, not a count"* — **and it was in an ad-hoc harness written twenty minutes earlier by the same pass.** The transfer is standing four applied to one's own work: **the discipline is to check a surprising number against the page by a second route before acting on it, and this pass's second route was `grep`, which is how the comma was found.**

**So two corrections to the record stand, and neither is re-opened later.** Item 207's holder list for `is the whole of it and the` is **2 chapters across 2 volumes**, not 11 across 6, **and the run is not register**, which is why this pass removed it — not for the lift but because the line it sat in restated its own chapter's opening twice over, section Six. **And the transferable standing is that a token-window count and a literal-string count are different measurements, that this repository's instruments are token measurements, that a figure printed without saying which probe produced it will be quoted by the other probe's convention, and that the comma inside a run is the commonest reason the two disagree.**

## Six: the finding in the prose — nine defects, eight of them found by reading and the last two by a review that read this pass's own corrections, and every instrument blind to every one of them

**All forty added paragraphs were read against the base paragraph immediately above and immediately below each, which is item 192's method and item 184's placement standing, and seven came out. Every one is a class no instrument in this repository can see: a contradiction is not a repetition, a figure is not a shared token, and a restatement of a fact is a shared fact and not a shared string. `lifts`, `reprints` at all four windows, the twelve-word index, the intra-file scan, the `NONNOUN` guard and the prose selector all passed the range while all seven stood. Two more came out afterwards, at section Six two, and **both were introduced by the corrections written here rather than found in the base.**

**One: a duration not on the page, at `chapter-0431.md:95`.** The paragraph read *"It lay where he had left it **for the better part of two hours**"*. **The base gives the third hour, the fourth hour, the fifth hour and the seventh hour and no interval at all**, and `grep -c "two hours" chapters/volume-09/chapter-0431.md` returned 1 — the added line itself, and the only occurrence in the chapter. **Volume 09's fourth refusal is that no number that is not on the page gets printed, and item 202 had already taken three such durations out of this range.** It now reads *"It lay where he had left it **until about the fifth hour**"* — the fifth hour and the *about* are base line 75's, which is landed line 79.

**Two: a base figure attached to the wrong noun, and a tautology in the same sentence, at `chapter-0433.md:15`.** The paragraph read *"The week before this one was entered in **the four places** it always is, and **the four places are the four places**."* **The page's four is four *headings* — base line 41, landed line 45, the clerk's own line, *"a page in front of him with four headings over it"* — and the page's places are *nine*: base line 73, landed line 81, *"The four lines went in the book in the ninth place out of nine."* The added sentence moved the base's four onto the base's noun and made it nine wrong places, and its second clause says nothing at all.** This is item 202's `chapter-0435.md:57` class exactly, a figure carried across from the wrong thing, and the tautology is a second defect in the same twelve words. It now reads *"The week before this one was entered the way the ones before it were entered."*

**Three: a restatement of the chapter's own opening, twice in one paragraph, at `chapter-0436.md:71`.** The paragraph opened *"**About a foot wide is the whole of it**"* — base `:3` already prints *"a window about a foot wide"* — and went on *"**The third chair against the wall is where nobody has sat since she came** and it has not been moved since she came"* — base `:3` already prints *"a third chair against the wall that nobody has sat in since she came."* **Two restatements of the same base line 3, sixty-eight lines earlier in the same chapter, and the sentence repeated *since she came* inside four words of itself.** The paragraph's new work — that the book carries no weather, and that an unmoved chair has never been put in front of anybody — is kept; the two restatements are out.

**Four: a restatement of the base sentence immediately above, at `chapter-0437.md:57`.** The added paragraph opened *"**She did not wait for anything** and she went out to the lane"* and base line 49, landed line 55, two lines above, reads *"He said nothing to that and **she did not wait** and nobody thanked her for it."* **Standing one's first half, in the plainest possible form, eight words against the line directly above.**

**Five: a book count in added prose on the chapter that carries the counting room's carried conflict, at `chapter-0438.md:63`.** The paragraph read *"**She counted sixteen** before he started loading and she counted them again afterwards."* **One fault, and the reason this pass first gave for it was half wrong and is corrected here rather than left.** The standing for this range is *"Write no duration for the Slade-end box, no number of steps, **no book count** and no second figure for the foreman's job"*, **and the counting room's book count is a carried conflict this repair has never settled — `chapter-0145.md:3` puts *about forty books* on shelves made for taller books in the counting room off a dyers' lane in Greyfen, against `chapter-0366.md:5` and this chapter's own base `:5` at sixteen volumes — so a book count may not be added on this chapter at all, whatever the base already prints.** **This pass's first draft of this paragraph also claimed the added count contradicted its own page, on the ground that base `:5` says fifteen of the sixteen are *out on loan*. That is half wrong, and the half that is not wrong is worse: base line 57 already reads *"there is no form anywhere for a person to be entered as the one who counted sixteen and said nothing about the sixteenth"*, so the figure IS on the page and base itself has all sixteen present and counted at the cart.** The claim that there are not sixteen volumes on those shelves to count is therefore not available, and **a record that argues a correct action from a wrong reason is a record that will be quoted for the wrong reason.** The action stands on the standing alone: a repair does not add a book count to a chapter whose book count is a carried conflict, whether or not the base prints one. It now reads *"She counted what went onto the cart before he started and she counted it again when he had finished"*, with the act kept and the numeral gone, **and the reason it is worded that way rather than as *"she had the count of them"* is defect nine.**

**Six: a cadence the base contradicts, at `chapter-0438.md:59`.** The paragraph read *"It goes up on the second day and it goes up on **the second day after that**"* — which read strictly is a two-day interval, against base line 21, landed line 23, *"They have gone up on the second day **every fortnight** since I was seventeen."* **Base line 19, landed line 21, also says *"They go up on the second day"*, so the added sentence's own *"It goes up on the second day"* was a third fault in it: a restatement of a base line six lines above, which is why the whole clause came out rather than being corrected in place.** A sentence that reads two ways and whose second reading contradicts the page is a defect even when the first reading is innocent, and the base already has the word. It now reads *"the second day again **a fortnight** after that."*

**Seven: a nine-word re-performance of the base's own act, ten lines above it, at `chapter-0439.md:25`.** The paragraph carried *"**There is no form anywhere in this empire** for a day of the week to be entered as anything but itself"* and base line 15 — which is landed line 15, no insertion above it — carries *"and there is **no form anywhere in this empire** for taking a said thing back."* **Same chapter, same act, nine words identical — and this is the only pair in the whole range the intra-file scan found, at nine words.** It is standing one in both halves at once: a re-performance of a base line and a restatement of it. It now reads *"A day of the week is the only thing either of them has ever been asked to enter, and it asks nothing of either of them"* — which is Movement Four's own claim, said without the register sentence, **and the register sentence is not reduced, because base line 15 still carries it and `chapter-0439.md` still holds it at line 15: `there is no form anywhere in this empire` measures 212 chapters across 10 volumes with this range included and 207 with it excluded, on the prose selector, before and after this pass's edit.**

**Eight and nine were found after this pass's own record was written, by a review that had no shell and re-derived what it could by reading, and both are defects this pass had introduced at `chapter-0438.md` and left standing. They are the second instance in this repair of a phase auditing its own first draft and finding it wrong, and the third of a review's findings that were right where instruments had been trusted.**

**Eight: a self-inflicted redundancy at `chapter-0438.md:59`.** This pass's own first correction there read *"It goes up on the second day and it goes up on the second day again a fortnight after that"* — which does remove the two-day reading of the original *the second day after that*, **and states its own proposition twice with four words between the two statements, six lines below base line 19 which says *They go up on the second day*.** The old wording was clumsy and the new one was clumsy in a different way. **The clause came out whole rather than being corrected in place**, leaving *"The interval it travels on has never once been shortened or lengthened by anybody, nobody has ever put in a request about it, and nobody has ever asked whether the day could be a different one"* — the contradiction gone, the self-restatement gone, and **base line 21's *every fortnight* left standing as the only place on the page that states the cadence, which is where it belonged.**

**Nine: an ambiguous antecedent and a knowledge claim, both introduced by this pass's own correction at `chapter-0438.md:63`.** This pass's first correction read *"She had **the count of them** before he started loading and she had it again when he had finished"*, and the sentence immediately above it ends *"the stool was not taken out from under **the shelves** … and **the shelves** stood about as high as they have always stood"*, **so the nearest plural antecedent to *them* is the shelves, and a count of shelves is nonsense that a reader resolves only by looking back two sentences.** And *she had the count of them* is a claim about what she **knew** rather than what she did, **which is interiority in a different dress and is the class this record's own prohibited-material scan claims is absent from the added prose.** Both are the standing's own failures and both were introduced by the fix, not found in the base: **the original *She counted sixteen* had no pronoun and was an act.** It now reads *"She counted what went onto the cart before he started and she counted it again when he had finished"*.

**The guard was run on both candidate sentences before either was written, and the sweep is EMPTY on the line being replaced and EMPTY on the line being written in both cases**, so neither revoicing could move any of the four construction lists and no form could rise against another falling. **Nine defects, all revoiced at their own line numbers, with the fact kept and the sentence changed, no base line touched, no insert, no delete, no date line moved and no quoted span changed. Eight were net shorter and one — the `chapter-0439.md:25` re-performance, which had to carry the same claim in words the base does not use — was net longer by five, and the range is 45 words shorter for having had all nine found.**

### Six one: what the canon held, and what this pass wrote nothing about

**The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void: no added paragraph touches it. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question: no full stop is printed on it. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed and neither is the hand that struck it. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this range pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this range, and the walking of all three is on the page as something that has already happened.**

**The four conflicts that bear on this range by name were checked and none is touched and none is settled.** The **stair**, five chapters deep — `chapter-0406.md:3` against `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43`, with `chapter-0399.md:9` against `:17` in Volume 08 — **bears on `chapter-0439.md`, and no added sentence on it says which stair any room is on or whether she has been above the second one; the added paragraphs say *in the house*, *at the front of it*, *behind it* and *in the lane*.** The **corridor bed**, `chapter-0415.md:3` against `chapter-0419.md:3`, **does not reach this range: `chapter-0438.md` carries no corridor and no bed, and the prompt's instruction to read that file twice is discharged by having read it twice.** The **counting room's books**, sixteen against about forty, **bears on `chapter-0438.md` and is the one this pass refused to add to.** The **Slade-end box's duration, the number of steps, and the counting room's sixteen books** — no added paragraph prints any of them.

**One judgment was made against a defect and it is recorded so a later pass does not take it for an oversight: `chapter-0436.md:23` opens by restating base `:19` — *"she is on neither of them"* against *"she is not on the rota and not on the list of clerks"* — and it was left.** The paragraph then does new work in the same sentence, that she came in on neither, and a new clause in the next, that the question of which ought to have had her has never been put to anybody. **A leading restatement inside a paragraph that goes on to add is the volume's own method and this chapter uses it at `:3`, `:13` and `:37`; over-editing is a failure mode and this pass took nine defects and not ten.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, which is `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `2b015ee`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "2b015ee"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def method3_text(t):   # the figure of record: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def b1(t): return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))                     # selector, unstripped
def b2(t): return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
# SWEEP PER FILE AND SUM THE COUNTERS.  Do not concatenate the range into one
# text and sweep once: see section Two.
```

## Four: the two defects, and both were invisible to every instrument here

**One: `chapter-0442.md:23`, an invented pen-pot lid.** The line read *The pot stood where it always stood, close to his right hand, and the lid leaned beside it with a dark ring under the rim.* The corridor is the nine-foot one whose fixture list is **closed at `chapter-0427.md:3`**: *a sill at the top of the steps and a pen pot on the sill and a hook in the wall at the far end of it with a basket hanging on the hook. Two chairs on the landing. A bed against the wall at the near end that is made about half the time.* **A lid is not in that list, and `grep -rn -i pot chapters/ | grep -i lid` returns this one line and nothing else in six hundred and twenty chapters** — every other lid in the manuscript belongs to the box (`chapter-0401.md:91`, `chapter-0443.md:5`, `:49`, `:57`) or to the tin behind the boiler (`chapter-0428.md:15`, `:17`, `chapter-0439.md:43`, `:45`, `chapter-0446.md:63`). This is item 215's class on the same corridor, and standing six's twelfth instance. **The lid became an ink ring on the inside of the canon pot's rim, which is a consequence of a pen going into a pot every morning and not a new object: *the inside of the rim had a ring in it that was not made this morning*.** The nib and the mark are canon — `chapter-0381.md:29` and `:59` give that same man's pen its own groove and `chapter-0396.md:46` has the nib in the ink — and **the groove at `chapter-0442.md:33` was checked and stands on those citations rather than being withdrawn with the lid.**

**Two: `chapter-0443.md:61`, an invented position and an invented emptiness for the volume's own table.** The line read *The table stood alone in the middle of the room.* That room is the one `chapter-0450.md:3` and `:5` fix — *There is a table, a stool, a bed against one wall, and a chair against none*, with the paper standing on that table *against the base of that wall* — and `chapter-0448.md:11` puts the same table's end nearest a window. **So the sentence contradicted the room's canon twice: the table does not stand alone, and it is not in the middle of it.** The sentence went and the paragraph's own beat stayed.

**Nothing saw either of them, and that is the finding rather than a reassurance.** The intra-file scan at six words returned only the survivor item 222 ruled; the twelve-word cross-file index returned **zero** over 1,074 windows; `lifts` passed the lid outright; the added-prose `NONNOUN` guard was empty; and the sweep did not move by one, with the per-form delta empty in both directions on all nine files. **Both were found by reading, and confirmed by a corpus-wide `grep` that is the cheapest instrument in this repository and is not one of the four.**

## Five: the regression this pass caused, and the order of two operations that fixed it

**Revoicing the table sentence as *The room took the sound of a man going out of it* minted a fresh six-word run — `the room took the sound of` — held by `chapter-0366.md` at one chapter in one volume, and `lifts` returned it on the very next run.** That is a lift on the four-and-four test and it is this pass's own.

**The fix is item 173W's on the twenty-eighth range and it is an order of two operations and not a sentence: a candidate line has to clear the cross-file holder count, the added-prose sweep count and the intra-file run BEFORE it reaches the disk.** A screening guard was built, **eight candidates went through it, five were rejected and one was written**; two rejections were sweep bigrams (`that room`, `those in`) and three were six-word frames, one of those frames being *going on doing what it had been doing*, itself lifted from `chapter-0057.md`. The surviving line was then written and `lifts` re-run, and the range went from **4 hits at six words to 3, with 0 at seven and over**.

**A second fault, in this pass's own helper, found by testing the guard the way the finding it stands against would test it — item 202's transfer, applied to this pass's own instrument.** The refusal battery was run on a scratch copy before the first real edit and **the payload *Did he go* was written rather than refused, because the guard tested the character `?` and a question need not carry its mark.** An interrogative test was added and the whole battery re-proved: an anchor that **is** a section rule, an anchor on a blank line, an anchor above the located date line, an anchor *on* the located date line, a question without its mark, a quotation mark, a bold marker, a digit, a sweep bigram, a banned floor material, a section-rule payload and an `It is` opener were each **refused before anything was written**, and one clean payload was allowed. **The character-level gate is necessary and not sufficient, and `?` is a character test standing in for a sentence rule.** The test is word-initial, and a question phrased mid-sentence would still pass it; that limitation is stated rather than papered over.

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file. `BASE` is `185c48e`. `chapter-0500.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure below and is said to be excluded beside each.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "185c48e"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
LIST23 = TEN + ADD; LIST25 = LIST23 + NEW          # 10 + 13 + 2 = 25
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def b3(t):   # THE FIGURE OF RECORD: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = b3(t)
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
files = [f"chapters/volume-10/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(451,500)]
```
