**All twenty-four went out by revoicing an added line with the fact kept and the sentence changed, and every instrument was re-run after every one of them.** Two of the revoicings went wrong in a way that cost a base line, and that is the ninth finding:

**A revoicing that addresses an added line by LINE NUMBER rather than by content eventually addresses a base line, because line numbers move as inserts accumulate.** Two of this pass's revoicing scripts wrote by line number. On the twenty-second round they hit `chapter-0483.md` and `chapter-0499.md` and **overwrote a base line in each — `He gave up the only way he had of knowing a thing that was not written down` in 0483 and `About nine hundred sheets went out of that building that day` in 0499** — and the `git diff --numstat` gate caught it at once, with **two deletions against a standing zero, and the sweep fallen from 1,211 to 1,205.** Both files were restored from `185c48e` and their four added paragraphs re-applied **anchored by content**, and the gate returned to 366 insertions and zero deletions with the sweep back at 1,211. **A revoicing script must locate its line by content, the same rule the insertion helper uses, and a line-numbered revoicing is a deletion waiting for enough inserts.**

**And a sixth instrument fault, in this pass's own helper, found by testing the guard the way the finding it stands against would test it.** Run on a scratch copy of `chapter-0454.md` before the first real chapter was opened, the refusal battery **refused legal anchors below the date line and accepted illegal ones above it** — the guard was written `if after_line > d_at: refuse` where the rule is *legal only at or below*, so the whole class of legal inserts was refused and the whole class of illegal ones was accepted, and the battery reported the run as correct. **It is item 202's inverted guard, and an inverted guard fails silently in the direction that costs the most.** The condition was corrected to `if after_line < d_at: refuse` and the battery re-proved in full: an anchor at line 5 and one at line 3 were refused as above the located date line at 9, an anchor that IS a section rule was refused, an anchor on a blank line was refused, **and the three legal cases were accepted — the date line itself, the last prose line of a section, which must not be refused, and the final line of the file.** The character-level prose guard was then extended after the battery showed two holes in it: **a curly quotation mark and a curly apostrophe were not refused, and both are absent from all six hundred and twenty chapters of the base, so a repair must not introduce one.**

## Six: what the canon held, what this pass added to the world, and what is carried unrepaired

**The locks held and every one of them is checkable on the tree.** No hearing and no arrangement of one, and no new heading over anything and no new form for anything. No House, no seat and no office named. No romance and nothing implying one. **No number that is not on the page got printed. **An earlier draft of this section said the 183 added paragraphs carry no numeral and no number word at all, and that was false, and it is corrected here rather than left, because the sentence was an assertion nobody had run: seventy-three of the 183 carry at least one number word and not one carries a numeral digit.** Every number word in the added prose was then measured against the base of its own file, and **seventy of the seventy-three are on the page in the chapter they were written into** — `the two of them`, `the four flights`, `the eleven things`, `about four hundred`, `the six hours`, `the second of it`, `the four headings`, `the nineteen years`, `about forty-five`, `the twenty minutes` and the rest, every one of them a figure base already carries. **Three are not, and two of the three are idiom and are left, and the third was a canon contradiction and is out.** `chapter-0452.md`'s *did not look down the length of the boards once* is the negative-universal use, which this volume already carries at `chapter-0454.md:47` and `chapter-0468.md:49`, and `chapter-0488.md`'s *the first of it* is canon's own designation for the original sheet, fixed at `chapter-0471.md:37` and `chapter-0462.md:21`. **The third was `chapter-0453.md:21`, and it was a real defect: the added paragraph said the sheet *has been folded once* against base `:17`, which says it came out of *a bundle folded twice*.** A figure that disagrees with the base count four lines above it is item 197's class exactly, and no index here can see it because a contradiction is not a repetition. It is revoiced at its own line number with the fact kept and the sentence changed: the fold count is gone and the paragraph now says the sheet *carries nothing on it anywhere but the strip along the top*, which is base `:19`, **and the range is eleven words shorter for it and the manuscript is at 1,479,205.** **The standing is therefore not stricter than it asks, and the honest form of this line is that seventy-three paragraphs were grepped against `chapters/` rather than none.**** The number in the head of the man of about thirty-four is not printed, not confirmed and not denied; the figure at the end of the cold passage is not printed; the figure on the bill at Lowcross is not printed; and the count of things asked out loud in this matter is printed nowhere in a chapter. No interiority was added — a claim about what a person knows rather than about what a person did is interiority in a different dress, and none of the 183 paragraphs is one. No bold marker and no question mark. **No floor material is named in any added paragraph: `steel`, `brass`, `brick`, `lime`, `plaster`, `glass`, `candle`, `lantern`, `quill`, `pencil`, `match`, `snow`, `slate`, `gravel` and `flagstone` are all in the manuscript and none of them is in the added prose.**

The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question and carries no full stop. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed, and neither is the name of the hand that struck it. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this volume pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in this range**, and the walking of all three is on the page as something that has already happened.

**The count of things asked out loud did not move.** Not one line of speech was added to any of the forty-nine chapters: the quoted spans are span for span identical to the base, 428 across the forty-nine, and `chapter-0499.md` and `chapter-0500.md` carry zero. **No added paragraph contains a question, a question mark, an asking, a request for information, or a sentence reporting what a person wants out of an answer, and the character-level guard refused every draft that tried.**

**No two of the three people the state layer keeps apart are in one room in any chapter of this range, and no chapter states or denies a distance between any two of them.** The full pair list in the outline was checked by reading the range: Marek Kest and Rennick Adley never share a room; the woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor and the clerk of about fifty-three never share one, and `chapter-0489.md` says of the two women who live on one side of one lane that neither has ever said a word to the other about the man who lives between them, which is the base's own arrangement and not a sentence this pass added; the woman of about twenty-six and the woman of about forty with a scuttle never share one; the woman of about twenty-six and the woman who keeps minutes never share one; **the man of about sixty-one and the woman of about twenty-six are never in one room and the four hundred yards is not walked, and the room at the far end of it is not entered**; **the man of about fifty-five with the chain and the man of about sixty-one are never in one room, and this pass added no sentence placing them in one.**

**The canon conflicts carried unrepaired, and none was settled and none was papered over.** Items 177, 180, 181, 182, 184, 185, 186, 189, 192, 194, 196, 197, 199, 201, 202, 203 and 204 hold them and this phase settled none. **The stair conflict is five chapters deep and this range does not touch it: no added sentence in any of the forty-nine says which stair any room is on, and no added sentence says whether the woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor has been above the second stair — `chapter-0469.md` and `chapter-0489.md`, the two chapters that carry her, were written around that entirely, and the added prose in them says *in the passage*, *at the passage window*, *at the foot of a stair* and nowhere about a room's position on a stair.** The bed conflict between `chapter-0415.md:3` and `chapter-0419.md:3` does not reach this range and was checked for and not found. **The counting room's sixteen books against about forty was checked for and no book count is named in any added paragraph.** The others — `chapter-0398.md:31`'s about a year, `chapter-0397.md:3`'s four steps and one step, `chapter-0375.md:5`'s eleven years against `chapter-0356.md`'s nine, and `chapter-0378.md:27`'s neighbour — are carried and none is touched here.

**One finding in the page itself is carried unrepaired by this phase and it is a conflict between the volume's plan of record and its own last chapter, and no phase here may settle it.** `outline/volume-10.md`'s final image puts the second copy **in the inside pocket of a coat on the chair against no wall**, **in that pocket for about a month**, with the first on the table. **`chapter-0500.md:5` and `:7` put the coat on the nail and not on the chair — *The coat is on the nail* and *the coat is not on it any more* — and put both things in the pocket about two years, and `chapter-0486.md:33` agrees with the page and hangs the coat on the nail, and `chapter-0500.md:47` puts both on a nail.** The page and the plan of record disagree about the coat and about how long the second thing has been there, the page says a copy of a copy was never made — `chapter-0500.md:37`, *He has not cut anything, and he has not left anything anywhere for anybody to find* — and the plan's image requires one to exist. **This pass added nothing to either side, invented no fixture, figure or surface in that room or around it, and did not open `chapter-0500.md`; the conflict is carried and named.**

## Seven: what is left, and no phase may imply otherwise

**Two hundred and fifty-five chapters of six hundred and twenty have been through the prose repair, forty-one point one per cent, and this range is forty-nine of them.** Three hundred and sixty-five chapters are unrepaired, fifty-eight point nine per cent, **and they are Volumes 01 to 07 at 350, plus the five volume endings `chapter-0400.md`, `chapter-0450.md`, `chapter-0500.md`, `chapter-0550.md` and `chapter-0620.md`, plus Volume 12's `chapter-0610.md` to `chapter-0619.md` at 10 — so fifteen of the 365 are outside Volumes 01 to 07 and the earlier claim on this line that every unrepaired chapter is in Volumes 01 to 07 was wrong by those fifteen.** **Volume 10 is repaired from 0451 to 0499, forty-nine of its fifty, and `chapter-0500.md` carries the last line of the volume, is byte-identical to `185c48e`, was read and was not opened, and is the fifth of the five exclusions.** The repaired set measured on the tree as it stands is Volume 08 at 0351 to 0399, Volume 09 at 0401 to 0449, **Volume 10 at 0451 to 0499**, Volume 11 at 0501 to 0549 and Volume 12 at 0551 to **0609**, and nothing else: **255 chapters at 431,546 words and a mean of 1,692.3 words a chapter.** **Both figures are corrected here and the correction is item 215's, applied late: Volume 12's repaired set is fifty-nine chapters and not sixty-nine, because `chapter-0610.md` to `chapter-0619.md` carry no prose-repair commit and were never a prompt's target range, and an earlier draft of this section counted them as repaired and so printed 265 and 443,831.** The five per-volume figures re-derive in one line each with `words_in_file`: Volume 08's 85,594, Volume 09's **84,410**, Volume 10's **79,511**, Volume 11's 93,827 and Volume 12's 88,204, and **Volume 09's 84,410 is a one-word correction of the 84,409 this repair has carried since item 227, the word being item 230's own and not this item's.**

**The largest untouched block is Volumes 01 to 07, three hundred and fifty chapters, and that is the bulk of the remainder rather than all of it.** **Volume 12's `chapter-0610.md` to `chapter-0620.md` carry no prose-repair commit and were never the target range of a prompt, and they stand with the prose that `workspace/prose-repair-0002/PROMPT.md` records as found defective; that is eleven chapters, and no phase may settle whether they are repaired.**

**Fifty chapters in one phase is five tens and not one, and whether the remaining three hundred and fifty are taken in that shape is the next phase's own decision to record and not this one's.** **Two hundred and fifty-five chapters are evidence that the work can be done and not evidence that it has been done.**

**And the honest finding, which no amount of state bookkeeping can fix: the manuscript is structurally complete, canonically sound and not publishable as it stands.** Chapter length fell from 4,042 words a chapter in Volume 01 to 1,455 in Volume 12, monotonically across twelve volumes, and the demonstrative-anaphora construction rose with it from 0.5 instances per 1,000 words to 8.7. **Volume 10 stood at a mean of 1,438.8 words, its longest chapter 2,056, its shortest 1,082, and its densest chapter carried 46 sweep instances; it now stands at 1,618.2, and the sweep is exactly where it was at 1,211.** Repairing it added 8,972 words and moved not one of 1,211 constructions, **because a repair that grows the denominator and not the numerator lowers the rate and does not change the tic — and this range carried the highest closed-list count any range in this repair has measured, 352, which is the finding rather than a departure from it.** That is what this repair is repairing, it is a decision about scope, and it belongs to a person.

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file with the heading and the date line in it; for a committed blob the same definition is applied to the text `git show` returns. `BASE` is `2b015ee`.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)

        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L):
    return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(t))
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def b3(t):   # the figure of record: the selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def b1(t):   # the selector alone, unstripped
    return "\n".join(L for _,L in m.prose_lines(t))
def b2(t):   # body_strip as printed in earlier records
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall(re.sub(r"^It is.*$", "", t, flags=re.M)))
def words(t):
    return sum(len(l.rstrip().split()) for l in t.split("\n"))
def base_text(p):
    return subprocess.run(["git","show",f"{BASE}:{p}"],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout
def cur_text(p):
    return open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
files = [f"chapters/volume-09/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(441,450)]
```

## Three: the finding — a paragraph standing inside a quoted span, and eight dispatches read it as clean

**`chapter-0447.md` carried a paragraph of unquoted third-person narration sitting inside a quoted span.** It read *The room held the echo of their voices a moment after they stopped. Both men heard it fade, and neither hurried to fill what came after.* and stood between one speech's closing quotation mark and the next speech's opening one, with a section rule between them. Its base position was **empty**: the base goes from a closing `"` straight to `---`. It was inserted by the first dispatch at `185c48e` and survived four revoicing passes and four audits.

**Why every instrument in this repository read it as clean.** The count of quoted spans is **8 before and 8 after**, because the inserted paragraph sits between a closing mark and an opening mark and does not change how many pairs there are. So the gate this repair has been reading — a span count per file, compared against base — held. **The quote CHARACTERS read 967 at `2b015ee` and 1,105 on the tree, and the gate the record states is span-for-span identity, not span count.** `re.findall(r'"[^"]*"', text)` reads the whole region, paragraph and section rule included, as one span. `lifts`, `reprints`, the twelve-word index, the intra-file scan and the construction guard are all blind to it, because it is a punctuation-placement fault and every one of them measures strings.

**It was also defective on two further grounds, both of standing one.** It performed the beat the base line four lines below it performs — *Then he said the one thing that was about himself* — and it re-performed a silence beat the chapter's own base line 15 already carries: *neither of them said one word for about nine seconds*. **After removal the nine files read 82 quoted spans and 11,393 quote characters, identical to `2b015ee` span for span and character for character**, per file 2,172 / 867 / 774 / 1,133 / 1,622 / 633 / **967** / 1,160 / 2,065.

**The generalisation, and it is the standing a next phase should carry: a paragraph inserted between a closing quotation mark and an opening one is inside a speech as far as the file's own punctuation is concerned, and the span COUNT cannot see it. The character total can, and it is the cheap check: compare `sum(len(s) for s in re.findall(r'"[^"]*"', text))` against base and not only the number of spans.**

## Four: the tic, and it is this repair's own manufacture and no instrument here can see it

**The construction `kept/held its` — the room, the bench, the house or the road holding something, and the people in it not filling it — stood at five instances across five of the nine files in the 1,178 words the range's added prose carried.** Measured against both bases:

| | instances | words | per 1,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| the range's nine added paragraphs, as they stood | **5** | 1,178 | **4.24** |
| the range's own base at `2b015ee` | 1 | 11,263 | 0.09 |
| the other forty chapters of Volume 09 | 1 | 73,203 | 0.01 |

**Forty-seven times its own range's rate and four hundred times the volume's.** `through all of it` stood at **3 in the added prose against 0 in both bases.** Neither is the volume's register and neither was in the base, so removing them is not reducing the voice — **a repair may not reduce the register, and the way to tell the register from a tic is to measure the tic against the base it is supposed to belong to, which is the transfer here and it is the first time this repair has produced one.** Both are now **0 in the added prose**, and the range's totals are back to their base values of 1 and 0.

**A rhetorical construction is not a `that`-bigram, and no instrument in this repository counts one.** `sweep` counts `that|those` plus a non-`NONNOUN` noun; `lifts`, `reprints` and the two indices measure shared token runs; `calendar` and `words` measure counts. **A tic made of a verb and a possessive is invisible to all of them, and it was standing in nine files of the volume's climax for eight dispatches.**

**The guard was built before the first edit and it earned its place.** The added-prose sweep guard — five lines, run on each candidate **before** it reaches disk, comparing the candidate's per-form delta against the paragraph it replaces — **fired three times**: it refused a candidate carrying `that room` and two carrying `that week` and `that room`. The first refusal happened after the write rather than before, which is the finding item 202 records about a helper's ordering, and the file was put right with the range total as the gate. **The insertion helper's refusals were tested on a scratch file before the first chapter was opened, in the direction the finding they stand against would test them**, because an inverted guard fails silently in the direction that costs most. It refuses an anchor above the located date line, an anchor that IS the date line, an anchor on a blank line, and an anchor that IS a section rule; it **accepts** an anchor whose next non-blank is a `---` — the last prose line of a section is legal — and a line that merely **contains** `---` as text, because it matches the line and not a substring. All seven tests passed. The helper also asserts the line count, asserts that no line sits directly under a non-blank line, asserts the located date line is byte-identical and unmoved, and prints the anchor line, the paragraph below the insert and the nearest `---` in either direction on every write.

**One, `lifts`.** ADDED 30 prose lines against a BASELINE of 239, with 3 at six words and over against 206 and **0 at nine and over against 113**, mean 6.33 against 9.88. **Item 225's ruling was applied and cited: breaking a nine-word window on the volume's connective is removing the voice, and this pass broke none.** The three survivors, ruled on holder counts taken **on the exact strings** and on the **prose selector** — `m.prose_lines` does not select a heading, and titles are set in capitals in this manuscript, so a holder counted out of a chapter title is invisible to any count that reads prose:

**The two at exactly four volumes are quoted by holder list rather than by count, as the standing requires:** `on the board by the door and` is held by `chapter-0412.md`, `0421.md`, `0482.md`, `0504.md`, `0521.md`, `0526.md`, `0528.md`, `0585.md`; `at the foot of the stair` by `chapter-0379.md`, `0409.md`, `0424.md`, `0453.md`, `0468.md`, `0492.md`, `0494.md`, `0572.md`. **Four lifts below the threshold were found and revoiced, two of them created by this pass itself, and revoicing one of them minted a fifth, which was also taken out — item 173W on the twenty-seventh range running, and the fix that worked in every case was to remove the frame from the sentence rather than to move the words inside it.**

**The register leaders were measured, not inherited: `there is no form anywhere in this` reads 212 chapters across 10 volumes and `and that is the whole of what` reads 145 across 12.** The 145 has now been confirmed four times in this repair. Neither appears in this pass's added prose.

**Two, the twelve-word cross-file index, with the non-empty-holder clause.** **0 hits at fourteen words, 0 at twelve and 0 at eleven**, and the zero is proved three ways rather than believed. **The clause belongs on the OUTSIDE holder set: `if out and len(out) < 4`, not `if hh and len(hh) < 4`.** A run held by no chapter outside the range is not a lift, and the wrong form of the test returned **568 hits on a range with none in it** — the same failure item 216 records, in the opposite direction, and it is why a scan that returns hundreds of hits on a clean range is as much a finding as one that returns none.

**The plant, taken before the zero was believed.** A fourteen-word run was taken verbatim from `chapter-0050.md`'s prose — *what a man does at the end of a thing that is not an* — and written into `chapter-0441.md` at a legal anchor at or below the located date line. It returned **3 hits held by one chapter in one volume**; **the same twelve words returned exactly 1**; **eleven words returned 0**. The file was restored and the restoration asserted by md5, `ad826ced65ada142761ee71ec5c79406` before and after. **The index was rebuilt from disk after every plant, because a token cache built before a plant was written tests a stale index and reports a zero that is not a zero.**

**Three, the intra-file longest-common-run scan, and it had to be built twice.** `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over case-folded `m.TOKEN` lists, every added line against every other prose line in the same file, added against added included, date lines excluded. **The first version was keyed on line numbers and returned 53- and 110-word runs between unrelated lines, because an insertion shifts every line below it and a current line number does not address the same line in the base blob.** Rewritten to work on text it returned real figures: **two pairs at six words, both restatements of a canon fixture phrase in the same chapter** — `the sill end of the boards` at `chapter-0441.md`, shared with base `:55`, and `on the board by the door` at `chapter-0444.md`, shared with base `:3` — and **both are out.** On the landed tree it returns **nothing at six words and two pairs at five, `the man in the room` and `in his hand and the`, both the room's own stock phrase.** **The six pairs this scan found on the range behind it included ones between two paragraphs of that pass and not against base, and they are the reason the scan exists; a cross-file index cannot see them by construction, because each of them excludes the range under repair from its own corpus.**

**Four, the added-prose construction guard**, which is the fourth index and the one item 202 requires to be built before the first edit. Its figures are in section One and its three refusals are in section Six.

## Eight: what the canon held, and what is carried unrepaired

**The canon held on every point this pass touched, and the volume's final image is untouched.** The room in `chapter-0450.md` has its table, stool, bed against one wall and chair against none, its window on the back of another house, about four feet of bare wall beside it and its one crooked nail with nothing ever hung off it; `chapter-0448.md`'s own base `:13` carries that image and **was not edited, and the revoicing of the paragraph beside it introduced no fixture, no figure and no surface.** The two in their boxes stay in them. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question. The figure at the end of the cold passage was not handed on. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed. The guarantee is not printed in its own words. **The bill at Lowcross is unpaid and no chapter of this pass pays it.** The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph were not asked one question about a number. **A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for.** **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are walked zero times in this range, and all three are on the page as something that has already happened.** No floor material is named in any added paragraph. No hearing, no heading, no form, no House, no seat, no office, no romance, and no number that is not on the page.

**The separations were honoured as rules about mouths and not about geography.** No two of the three people the state layer keeps apart were brought into one room, and no sentence states or denies a distance between any two of them. **The count of things asked out loud in this matter did not move by one, and no added paragraph contains a question, a question mark, an asking or a request for information** — the nine files carry **zero question marks at base and zero now**, and every added paragraph is unquoted third-person narration.

**The conflicts carried in from the ranges behind stand unrepaired and are named here so that no later phase reads this record as settling any of them.** `chapter-0406.md:3` against `chapter-0404.md:23`, `chapter-0409.md:15`, `chapter-0417.md:15` and `chapter-0425.md:43` on which stair the woman who keeps the ground floor has been on: **this pass wrote no sentence about which stair any room is on and none about whether she has been above the second one.** `chapter-0415.md:3` against `chapter-0419.md:3` on a bed at opposite ends of the nine-foot corridor: **`chapter-0442.md` carries that corridor and the sill, and this pass wrote no sentence about that bed in it, nor in the other eight.** `chapter-0398.md:31` against `chapter-0395.md:7` and `:5`; `chapter-0397.md:3` against `:21`, `:53`, `:63` and `:65`; `chapter-0375.md:5` against `chapter-0356.md`; **the counting room's sixteen books against about forty, which this range carries at `chapter-0445.md` — *Sixteen volumes have their places on those shelves* — so this pass wrote no book count and no second figure for it there**; and `chapter-0378.md:27` against `chapter-0397.md:11`. **A repair has no authority to settle a canon conflict it finds and must not paper over one; all seven are carried, named and left standing.**

## Nine: what is left, and why no prompt was created

**Two hundred and fifty-five chapters of six hundred and twenty have been through the prose repair, forty-one point one per cent, and this phase repaired none of them new.** Three hundred and sixty-five are unrepaired, fifty-eight point nine per cent. **The prompt this dispatch was handed put those at 207 and 403 and named Volume 10 as the largest untouched volume in the manuscript; Volume 10's forty-nine were repaired at item 232 and audited at item 233, so both of the prompt's figures are stale by forty-nine chapters and Volume 10 is no longer untouched.** Volume 09 is repaired from 0401 to 0449, forty-nine of its fifty, and **not in full**, and any sentence in the records above that calls it repaired in full is wrong on the same clause as every earlier *in full* claim in this repair. `chapter-0450.md` is one of six exclusions and its ordinal is not asserted, because three different ordinals for that set are standing in this repository and they cannot all be right: measured on the tree there are twelve volume endings and **six belong to a repaired volume — `chapter-0350.md`, `chapter-0400.md`, `chapter-0450.md`, `chapter-0500.md`, `chapter-0550.md`, `chapter-0620.md`** — and the durable form is the list, because a list can be checked against the tree and an ordinal cannot.

**This phase created no prompt, and it is the ninth time this repair has handed a phase an instruction to write one that already exists.** `workspace/prose-repair-0023/PROMPT.md` exists at 37,839 bytes, names Chapters 0451 to 0500, carries `--volume 10` throughout and excludes `chapter-0500.md` in terms; its range was repaired at item 232. `workspace/prose-repair-0024/PROMPT.md` exists at 17,256 bytes and names 0301 to 0350. **Both were checked with `ls -la` and each first line with `head -1`, and not inferred from a commit message.** **A finding for a controller, which no phase here may pay: `workspace/prose-repair-0025/` does not exist, so the frontier has no prompt for the next phase and every prompt directory that does exist names a range already repaired.**

**The honest finding, which no amount of state bookkeeping can fix, and it is sharper on this range than the prompt states it.** The prompt says the ten chapters where a reader is most likely to be told what Volume 09 is worth are the ten where the sentences are shortest and the construction is densest. **On the nine files this pass owns the shortest mean is 1,350.2 and the densest chapter carries 31 sweep instances in 1,906 words, and that is the shape the finding takes in a room.** The manuscript is structurally complete, canonically sound and not publishable as it stands, and this repair is repairing it one range at a time against a defect that spans six volumes and 365 chapters. **Two hundred and fifty-five chapters are evidence that the work can be done and not evidence that it has been done, and fifty-eight of them have had one pass while five have had three or more, which is itself the argument for repairing forward rather than auditing back.** And the ninth dispatch on nine chapters found a paragraph inside a quoted span, a tic at forty-seven times its base rate, an invented window, an invented coat-rail and a wrong man setting a paper on a table — **every one of them invisible to all four instruments, and every one of them standing in the volume's climax since the first pass.**

**Four debts are outstanding and no pass in this repair touched them, and they are owed elsewhere and not here.**

The prompt that ordered this pass named no number at all, on purpose, and it named the range unrepaired for the ninth time.***

## One — THE METHOD, PRINTED WHOLE, AND EVERY FIGURE WITH ITS UNIT

**Line work** uses `tools/measure.py`'s `m.prose_lines(text)`, which drops blank lines, a line that is exactly `---`, a line beginning `#`, and a line matched by `m.DATE_LINE`. Chapter titles in this manuscript are set in capitals after `#`, so **a holder counted out of a chapter title is invisible to any count that reads prose and to `grep -n` against a title line.** The instance standing in the records is `at the other end of the room`, whose sixth holder is `chapter-0515.md:1`.

**Token work** uses `m.TOKEN.findall(text)`, lowercased, and matches contiguous token windows. **Matching by regex over raw text is NOT equivalent and returns zero on a genuine holder**: proved here on `chapter-0593.md:49`, which reads *it did not look at **it again, and** neither of them said one word about the eleven weeks* — the comma defeats a `\s+` regex between `again` and `and`, so a raw-text count returns no holder for a run `lifts` finds at ten words. Every holder count in this section is a token window, and the selector is printed beside it.

**The date line is stripped by `m.DATE_LINE`** before tokens are taken. That is the prompt's method 3, and it is the figure of record. **The demonstratives are `that` AND `those`.** An earlier version of this pass's own method counted only `that` and returned 50 / 69 / 84, and the missing instances were all `those boards` (eleven in the nine files). **The live prompt's per-form survey lists `those boards` 12, so its method is `that` and `those` too.**

**`chapter-0450.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure in this section**, because it carries the last line of Volume 09 and is not this repair's to move. It was read, it was not opened, it is byte-identical to `2b015ee` at md5 `399b4e32a56681168e5bd2cf2fdae60d`, and it appears in no diff this section prints.

## Seven — THE GATES, EVERY ONE RE-RUN ON THE LANDED TREE

**Insert-only.** `git diff --numstat 2b015ee` over the nine files: **60 `insert`, 0 `delete`**, per file `8 0 / 4 0 / 6 0 / 8 0 / 8 0 / 6 0 / 6 0 / 8 0 / 6 0`. **A word-level diff reports 30 inserted lines, 0 deletions and 0 substitutions.**

**Two faults in this pass's own word-level parser are recorded because each returned a clean-looking wrong answer.** Passing an invalid `--word-diff-re` to `git diff` makes git print its usage to the error stream and exit zero, and a parser that reads the empty standard output reports **zero insertions, zero deletions and zero substitutions on a tree with sixty insertions** — a clean pass read off an empty string. And in porcelain output a `~` row is a **separator between line entries, not a substitution**, so counting `line.count('~')` reported **60 substitutions on a tree with none.** The detector finally used counts only genuine `[-old-]{+new+}` pairs, and that detector was then proved against a planted substitution — which it also missed, reporting it as a line deletion instead. **The claim of zero substitutions therefore rests on three agreeing instruments and not on one: `numstat` reports 0 deletions, the strict pair count is 0, and the arithmetic closes to the word in both directions.** Item 234 recorded the first of these two faults; this is the same fault in a second form.

**The arithmetic, run as an addition and as a subtraction because the subtraction is the one that checks:**

```
  base nine files       11,263 words
  added lines' own wc      832 words
  ADDITION    11,263 + 832 = 12,095
  landed nine files    12,095 words          agree: True
  SUBTRACTION 12,095 - 11,263 = 832          equals added: True
```

Each file's own base-plus-added equals its own landed figure, checked per file and not only in the total.

**Date lines.** All ten located by `m.DATE_LINE`, all byte-identical to `2b015ee`, all on the line number they held: **9, 9, 7, 7, 9, 7, 7, 7, 9, 9.** **None is at line 5, so the line-5 check cannot tell an insert above the date line from one below it on any file in this range, and the located check is the standing.** No date line was ever typed out; every one was copied out of the base blob and compared byte for byte on its located line number.

**The insertion helper's refusals were tested on a scratch file before the first chapter was opened, in the direction the finding they stand against would test them, and two of the tests were wrong on the first attempt and are recorded.** It refuses an anchor **above** the located date line, an anchor **on** it, an anchor on a blank line, and an anchor that **is** a section rule, and it **accepts** an anchor whose next non-blank line is a `---`, so the last paragraph of a section is not lost — five such anchors exist in `chapter-0441.md` alone, at lines 21, 35, 51, 61 and 75, and **every one of this pass's twenty-two writes landed on exactly that kind of line.** The first test of the base-line refusal was mis-posed and reported a write where a refusal was required, because the scratch base had been built with the target line already removed from it; it was rebuilt and then refused correctly. A test of the anchor rule that used line 9, 10, 11 and 20 of a file with a rule at 11 tested blank lines and rules rather than prose and proved nothing; it was rebuilt on real prose lines.

**After every write the helper printed the anchor line, the paragraph below the insert, and the nearest `---` in either direction, and asserted the line count, the located date line and its text, a blank line above and below, and that the rewritten line is not a base line.** All twenty-two writes are at the last prose line of a section, which is the case the standing warns costs the last paragraph of most sections if a helper refuses it.

**Item 200 restored five files rather than revoicing them, and this is the same situation and the same instrument.** A revoicing keeps the fact and changes the sentence, which requires the paragraph to hold a fact of its own. **All ten of these held none.** Every one was a restatement of a base line, a re-performance of an act the base already narrates, a restatement of the repair's own added paragraph, or an assertion about a canon fixture that its own chapter contradicts. ## Five — THE ONE FIGURE IN ITEM 235 THAT COULD NOT BE RE-DERIVED, AND WHY THIS PASS'S OWN INSTRUMENT IS THE THING THAT WAS WRONG

**This section was written twice. Its first draft called a scope error and corrected five cells, and every one of those five cells was already right.** It is rewritten here rather than deleted, because the shape of the error is the finding.

**What happened.** Item 235's headline construction table carries a sweep of **319 across 105 forms**, and its per-chapter column reads 54 / 39 / 45 / 29 / 35 / 31 / 25 / 31 / 30. **This pass measured the sweep on `m.prose_lines`, per line, and read 54 / 39 / 45 / 29 / 34 / 30 / 25 / 29 / 30 = 315 across 104 forms.** Three cells disagreed and the total was four out. The obvious reading — and the reading this pass first wrote down — is that item 235 counted one chapter's title line by mistake, because item 235's own section One warns in terms that *a holder counted out of a chapter title is invisible to any count that reads prose*. On that reading the correction was straightforward and this pass was one edit from applying it to a record that reproduces.

**It was the instrument, not the record.** The sweep row is not on `m.prose_lines`. **It is on method 3's body — the raw file with lines matching `DATE_EITHER` or `DATE_THIRD` removed and chapter headings kept — with the `NONNOUN` filter removed**, which is exactly what the row's own label declares: *every `that`/`those` bigram*. Method 3 is the figure of record throughout this repair and its code is printed whole at line 4825. On it:

```
per-chapter column   54  39  45  29  35  31  25  31  30   sum 319
union of forms                                                  104
item 235's row       54  39  45  29  35  31  25  31  30   sum 319 across 105
```

## Two: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists are exactly flat

**`chapter-0500.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure in this section and is said to be excluded beside each.** Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, `sum(len(line.rstrip().split()) for line in handle)` over the whole file. `BASE` is `185c48e`.

```python
import re, importlib.util
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "185c48e"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
LIST23 = TEN + ADD; LIST25 = LIST23 + NEW          # 10 + 13 + 2 = 25
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
def is_date(L): return bool(m.DATE_LINE.match(L))
def b3(t):   # THE FIGURE OF RECORD: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = b3(t)
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
files = [f"chapters/volume-10/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(451,500)]
```

**`NONNOUN` is the set of record, pasted and not rebuilt. It does not contain `too`, `for` or `have`, and it does not contain `to`; a copy grown by any of those four under-reports this sweep.** Every sweep figure runs `sweep` over `b3(t)` **per file** and sums the counters, never over the concatenated range, because a sweep bigram must not straddle a file boundary.

**The locks held.** No hearing and no arrangement of one, no new heading, form, notice, post, commission, warrant or office. No House, no seat and no office named. No romance and nothing implying one. **No number that is not on the page got printed:** no added paragraph carries a numeral digit, seventy-three of the 183 carry at least one number word and every one of them is on the page in the chapter it was written into, item 232 having checked that list and this pass re-running it. **The number in the head of the man of about thirty-four is not printed, not confirmed and not denied; the figure at the end of the cold passage is not printed; the figure on the bill at Lowcross is not printed; the count of things asked out loud is printed nowhere in a chapter.** No interiority was added. ## The finding about this volume, which is the reason the repair is shaped the way it is

**165 is far below the 352 Volume 10 carried, and that is the finding about the volume rather than a target. The demonstrative-anaphora construction is not this volume's defect. This volume's defect is that its base prose repeats itself, and the repetition is so dense that a paragraph written in its own idiom collides with an eight-word run of its own.**

**The case, printed whole.** Volume 07 carries stock sentences that recur across its own chapters: *the door at the top end of the passage has a step worn in front of it*, *a carrier came up the passage with a rack on her hip*, *about nine hundred sheets a year go out of a room with a hand at the foot of every one of them*, *there is no form in this empire that will let a person be said in anything but a room they came into themselves*, *a person can say a thing out loud in a room and nothing that any paper in this empire can hold comes of it*. A paragraph written in that idiom hits an eight-word run of it at a rate that made the first draft of this repair unusable: **of forty candidate paragraphs screened at the outset, thirty-eight were rejected, and the rejections were dominated by this class and not by any canon fault.**

**The consequence for the prose.** The 191 paragraphs are therefore written outside the volume's stock connectives, in shorter sentences, about physical objects the volume's rooms actually have and about what a person's hands and body do. They carry no quotation mark, no bold marker, no question mark, no numeral, no section rule and no heading, because each of those is a gate.

**A second consequence, and it is the one item 221's standing exists for.** `lifts` excludes the range under repair from its own index, the intra-file scan is one file at a time, and the twelve-word index cannot see a run whose only holders are inside the range. **None of them can find a paragraph this pass wrote twice, and the guard built in front of the disk found one.** See the defect table below.

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists exactly flat

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "185c48e"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
LIST23 = TEN + ADD; LIST25 = LIST23 + NEW          # 10 + 13 + 2 = 25
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def b3(t):   # THE FIGURE OF RECORD: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = b3(t)
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
files = [f"chapters/volume-10/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(451,500)]
```

### The date lines, and the instrument fault that governs them

**`m.DATE_LINE` parses 0 of 49 in this range, and all forty-nine positions reproduce at their base line numbers.**

**The fault, printed with the case beside it.** `tools/measure.py:116` defines `DATE_LINE` with the opening clause

```
r"^\s*(?:\*\*)?\s*(?:[Ii][Tt]|[Tt]he date)\s+is\s+the\s+"
```

and Volume 07's date line at `chapter-0301.md:11` is

```
This is the fourth day of the third week of the twelfth month of the year after the year after next, and it is about the fourth hour, ...
```

`[Ii][Tt]` matches `It` and `[Tt]he date` matches `The date`; neither matches `This`, and the alternation is anchored at the start of the line, so **the whole clause fails and the match is False**:

```
DATE_LINE.match(line11) -> False
DATE_LINE lines matched in chapter-0301.md -> []
prose_lines keeps line 11 -> True
```

**`m.prose_lines` therefore keeps the date line in the prose bucket for all fifty files of this volume.** Item 239 named this fault in terms and did not connect it to the prose; **this record connects it, and the connection is three defects on the page.** The prompt's own gate — *"date lines parsed: 49 of 49"*, and *"Locate the date line with `m.DATE_LINE` itself and by nothing else"* — is **unreachable with the instrument it names**, and the prompt's warning that *"a date line found by `startswith("It is ")` is a different function"* is correct as a warning and does not close the gap, because the correct function is not in the instrument at all. `tools/measure.py` is not this phase's to change and was not changed; the fault is named and the case is printed, which is what this repair has done in nine prior passes.

## Zero: the precheck, the base, and the two readings of it

**The prompt's central claim is false and its own rule covers it.** It states in terms that *Volume 10 is untouched in its entirety, and it is the largest single untouched volume in the manuscript*, that *Volume 10 is 71,938 words*, that the manuscript is *1,470,233*, that *two hundred and six chapters* have been through the repair and *three hundred and sixty-five* will be unrepaired, and that the pre-repair figures of `185c48e` are live — and then instructs: *run that `git log` before you write a word; if it returns a `prose-repair` commit, your range has been repaired already — audit it instead of rewriting it, and write the record the first dispatch failed to write.* **This is the nineteenth dispatch on `chapter-0451.md` to `chapter-0499.md` handed a prompt naming the range unrepaired.** Every one of the prompt's global figures is stale by this pass's own range behind it and by the two repairs in front of it.

`git log --oneline -- chapters/volume-10/chapter-045[1-9].md` returns **`52da86e`, `742d599`, `0b70ca4` and `a550a44`** above the batch commits. **The two-sided precheck, both ends read:** `git diff --numstat 185c48e -- chapters/volume-10/` returned **366 insertions and 0 deletions across 49 files** on arrival, where the prompt printed nothing, and it returns **the same 366 and 0** now, item 203's precheck read from the wrong end for the nineteenth time. **`185c48e` is the correct base and the prompt named it.** `git diff --numstat 52da86e -- chapters/` returned nothing on arrival, so the tree was byte-identical to item 241's landed commit. **`chapter-0500.md` is byte-identical to `185c48e` at md5 `2ad68a07e2769a48bd3e3199e7c9d808` on both sides, was read and was not opened, and appears in no diff this item prints.**

**Every command in this record carries `--volume 10`.** The prompt printed `--volume 09` beside this Volume 10 range in the same sentence as its own correction section disowns it, and the flag follows the files and not the sentence.

## One: the construction, method printed whole, and all four lists exactly flat

**Word figures are `tools/measure.py`'s `m.words_in_file`, over the whole file. `BASE` is `185c48e`. `chapter-0500.md` is excluded from every range-wide figure below and is said to be excluded beside each.**

```python
import re, importlib.util, subprocess
from collections import Counter
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", "tools/measure.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
BASE = "185c48e"
TEN  = ["those boards","that lane","that floor","that table","that door",
        "that stair","that room","that passage","that tin","that sheet"]
ADD  = ["that end","that landing","that bench","that sill","that corridor","that case",
        "those stairs","that step","that bay","that ground","that jug","that stone","that board"]
NEW  = ["that building","that house"]
LIST23 = TEN + ADD; LIST25 = LIST23 + NEW          # 10 + 13 + 2 = 25
NONNOUN = set("""is was has had are were be been being am i we he she it they you me my our
their there here then than when where which who whom whose what why how and or but if so as
a an the this these those no not nor do does did done can could will would shall should may
might must one two three four five six seven eight nine ten anybody anything someone something
nobody nothing everyone everything""".split())
DATE_EITHER = re.compile(r"^(This|It) is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
DATE_THIRD  = re.compile(r"^The date is the .* day of the .* week of the .* month of the year after.*$")
def is_date(L): return bool(DATE_EITHER.match(L) or DATE_THIRD.match(L))
def b3(t):   # THE FIGURE OF RECORD: selector, THEN the date line stripped
    return " ".join(m.TOKEN.findall("\n".join(
        L for L in t.split("\n") if not is_date(L))))
def sweep(t):
    c = Counter()
    for mt in re.finditer(r"\b(that|those)\s+([a-z]+)\b", t, flags=re.I):
        if mt.group(2).lower() in NONNOUN: continue
        c[" ".join(mt.group(0).lower().split())] += 1
    return c
def cnt(t, forms):
    b = b3(t)
    return sum(len(re.findall(r"\b"+re.escape(f)+r"\b", b, flags=re.I)) for f in forms)
files = [f"chapters/volume-10/chapter-{n:04d}.md" for n in range(451,500)]
```

## Two: the structural gates, every one re-run on the landed tree

`git diff --numstat 185c48e -- chapters/volume-10/` returns **366 insertions and 0 deletions across 49 files**, and **`chapter-0500.md` is in neither**. **366 is twice the 183 added paragraphs, and the landed diff is twice the paragraph count as the standing requires.** A `difflib.SequenceMatcher` over base and landed line lists returns **zero `delete` and zero `replace` opcodes on every one of the forty-nine**, which is the claim of insert-only resting on an instrument independent of `numstat`. **A word-level diff against `185c48e` reports insertions and 0 deletions**, and **the added lines' own word count, taken on their own, is 8,819 and equals the addition exactly, the subtraction being zero.**

**All fifty date lines are byte-identical to `185c48e` and stand on the line numbers they held**, located by `m.DATE_LINE` and never typed out: **11, 7, 11, 9, 7, 9, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 7, 7, 7, 9, 7, 7, 9, 9, 7, 9, 7, 7, 9, 9, 11, 7, 9, 7, 7, 9, 9, 7, 7, 7, 11, 9, 9, 7, 7, 7, 9 and 9**, with `chapter-0500.md` at 9. **Fifty of fifty agree**, checked by comparing the located line at the tree against the same line at the base and not by count.

**Section-break counts, bold-marker counts, question-mark counts, title lines, trailing newlines and quoted spans are all identical to base, span for span and character for character: section rules 230 over the fifty, bold markers 594, question marks 0, quote characters 859, quoted spans 428 on the forty-nine owned files with no file's span *sequence* differing, title lines identical and a trailing newline on all fifty, and `chapter-0500.md` at zero spans and zero quote characters.** **183 inserted prose paragraphs and zero of them standing without a blank line ahead of them.**

The gate table: `selftest` **PASS**; `calendar --volume 10` **50 files read, 50 date lines parsed, none unparsed, 12 month-boundary restarts and no break inside a month**; `words --volume 10` **80,757** *(the whole volume of fifty, of which `chapter-0500.md` contributes 1,399 and the forty-nine owned files 79,358)*; `words` **1,488,233 in 620 files**; `reprints --window 20 / 12 / 8 / 5 --volume 10` `either` prose **0 / 448 / 1,463 / 3,842**.

## Three: the four indices, all four run, every hit ruled in writing

**Index one, `lifts`, and a fault in it that this pass found and that is new to this repair.** `python3 tools/measure.py lifts --volume 10 --first 451 --last 500 --base 185c48e --min 6 --show 20` reports **ADDED 183 prose lines, 164 at six words and over, 2 at nine and over, mean 6.77** against **BASELINE 1079 / 935 / 534, mean 9.68**; the baseline reproduces the prompt's floor to the digit at every window.

**`m.longest_lift` grows a run by intersecting the holder sets of two overlapping five-grams, which does not establish that any one chapter holds the concatenated run, and its docstring claims in terms that it does.** The docstring reads: *the answer is always a run that exists whole in one chapter rather than a run stitched out of several.* It does not deliver that. `build_lift_index` indexes five-grams over a chapter's **concatenated** token stream, so a chapter can hold `A B C D E` in one paragraph and `B C D E F` in another and satisfy the intersection without holding `A B C D E F` anywhere. **Three hits on this range were wrong in the instrument's own favour and one against it, and all three were found by quoting the string back, which is standing four.** `chapter-0490.md:55` was reported as a 10-word lift of `chapter-0356.md` on the string `it and not one of the two is going to`, **which is held by no chapter in the index at all**; the verified shared run is 9 words, `and not one of the two is going to`. `chapter-0457.md:39` was reported as a 9-word lift of `chapter-0561.md` on `there for about as long as it takes to`, **which no chapter holds**; the verified run is 8 words, `for about as long as it takes to`, and `chapter-0561.md:63` reads *left it there for about as long as it takes a lid to stop rocking* and its `:40` reads *in about as long as it takes to put a coin into an apron*, so the instrument's string is a splice of one line and the other. **`chapter-0484.md:27` went the other way and was under-reported at 11 where the true run is 12**, `she put her hands flat on the table on either side of`, held by `chapter-0182.md:107` and by nothing else. **A corrected instrument that re-verifies the grown run against the named holder's own token stream gives ADDED 0 lines at nine words against BASELINE 572, where the instrument gives 2 against 534 — so the added prose of this range was always well below the floor of the other five hundred and seventy chapters, and further below it than the instrument reported, and the correction raises the baseline and not the added figure.** `tools/measure.py` was **not** edited; it is not a file this phase may touch, and the corrected figures here come from this pass's own harness.

**Index two, the twelve-word cross-file index, rebuilt from disk after every plant.** It reported **two** distinct twelve-word runs in the added prose shared with any other chapter on arrival: `put her hands flat on the table on either side of` held by `chapter-0182.md` alone, and a second with no outside holder. **Both are now zero**, and the range's added prose shares **no twelve-word run with any chapter in six hundred and twenty**. Proved by plant before it was believed, per the standing.

**Index three, an index of the range against itself, which `lifts` cannot see by construction because it excludes the range.** It reported **one** run on arrival: `nobody has put a hand on the lid of it since the`, held by `chapter-0490.md:5` — which is the same added line this pass found to be a canon contradiction. **It is now zero.**

**Index four, the intra-file longest-common-run scan over `difflib.SequenceMatcher` on case-folded `TOKEN` lists, date lines excluded.** **It reported nineteen added-against-base pairs at six words or over on arrival and thirteen now**, every one of the nineteen read and ruled in writing below. **Its first version compared added lines against base lines only and was blind to a run one added paragraph shares with another, and its own plant proved it:** a fragment copied from added line `:21` into added line `:53` of `chapter-0461.md` returned 0 pairs. **The scan was extended to compare every added line against every other prose line in the same file, and the same plant then returned 2 pairs and the file was restored and the restoration proved by `git diff --numstat HEAD` returning nothing.** On the extended scan the range carried **two** added-against-added pairs, both in `chapter-0478.md` and both the same six words, `into the middle of the room`, at `:21` and `:39`. **Both are now zero.**

**Every one of the nineteen intra-file pairs, ruled.** Six are stock base noun phrases carrying a different claim and stand: `chapter-0451.md:79` and `chapter-0481.md:39` on *the near end of the boards*; `chapter-0454.md:55` on *the two at the back of*; `chapter-0477.md:49` on *at the end of the sill*; `chapter-0493.md:35` on *the man at the front bench*, where the base names him that way four times and the added sentence's claim, that he kept his head where he keeps it, is in none of the four; `chapter-0497.md:63` on *the far end of those two joined tables*; `chapter-0497.md:31` on *down in the middle of the*, where the base's middle is a book and the added line's is the floor. **Thirteen were defects and are out**, and they are the thirteen listed in section Four.

**The six-word floor has no discriminating power on this manuscript and the record says so rather than quoting a number as if it meant something.** At six words the corrected scan returns **147** single-holder coincidences on this range's added prose, and they are the volume's own connective tissue: *and the light off the lane*, *the boards at the near end*, *and he did not put it down*, *for the whole of the hour and*. **At nine words and above, which is the band the instrument's own reporting treats as meaningful and the band every lift ruling in this repair has been made at, the range's added prose is now clean.**

**One lift is named a survivor rather than revoiced.** `chapter-0457.md:39` holds the eight-word run *for about as long as it takes to*, whose verified outside holders are `chapter-0557.md` and `chapter-0561.md`, one chapter and one volume. **The same eight words are in the base of Volume 10**, which is the discriminator that settles it: it is this volume's own register and not a sentence lifted from elsewhere, and the standing's four-and-four test is applied to the register and not to a phrase the volume already uses.

## Four: every defect found, and the two that are the reason this dispatch exists

**Twenty-seven lines were revoiced across eighteen files, all of the range's own added prose, no base line touched, no insert, no delete, no date line moved and no quoted span changed.**

### Two canon contradictions, which no instrument in this repository can see

**`chapter-0455.md:37` put the rack coming down a stair with a man on it.** The added paragraph read *the rack came down the far side of the lock with him on it*. Base `:19` has *the rack went on up the flags with him on it*; base `:41`, four lines below the added line, has *He went up past her on the fourth pass without stopping and without turning round, and the rack came down the other side*; and base `:3` makes *the rack came past her with nothing on it* load-bearing across all eight walks of the morning. **A rack that descends with him on it cannot be the rack that ascends with him on it, and cannot be the rack that comes down the other side while he goes up past her.** The longest shared token run with the base line it collides with is under six words, `reprints` found nothing, the sweep did not move, and a contradiction shares no run with the line it contradicts. Found by reading.

**`chapter-0468.md:45` denied the chapter's central event.** The added paragraph read *Nobody has put a hand on the lid of it since the two years began*. Base `:3` says *nobody at the loading end of it has opened it once in that time*, base `:15` has the man of about forty-five *put his hand flat on the lid and took it off again in about two seconds* on the second day of this week, and the chapter's whole movement is two men making a box chargeable **because** a hand went on its lid. **The added line said no hand had been on it in two years, two lines after his speech saying he has not moved it and neither have you.** The same line carried a second fault: it shared a twelve-word run with `chapter-0490.md:5` that `lifts` cannot see because it excludes the range from its own index, and it restated base `:39`'s *the lane outside was doing whatever the lane does at the hour* four lines above. One revoicing cleared all three.

### Three faults of this pass's own, recorded because two of them had already reached the disk

**This pass's own first revoicing introduced two fresh lifts, which is item 221's standing caught for the tenth time in this repair.** `chapter-0478.md:21` was given a ten-word run held by `chapter-0351.md` and `chapter-0480.md:31` an eleven-word run held by `chapter-0379.md`, both where the pre-existing line had shared nothing at that length. **Both were caught by the cross-file index after they landed, not before, and both were revoiced a second time.** **The third fault was an invented figure and it is the one that would have been hardest to see: `chapter-0494.md:49` was rewritten to say *the four things in front of it are four things whichever way round a person counts them*, and the shelf in that chapter holds the day-book and the page — base `:43` — while the *four* on the page is four headings in a book and four entries made in a house.** A count was imported from one noun onto another, which is the class item 227 named, and it was caught by grepping the base for what the shelf holds rather than by any run test. **A twelfth revoicing removed a claim that he had not turned his head once, which base `:19` of the same chapter contradicts three lines earlier, where he looked back down at her.** Twenty-seven lines in all, five of them rewritten twice.

## Five: the locks, each checkable, each with its citation

**Every lock holds.** No hearing and no arrangement of one and no new heading, form, notice, post, commission, warrant or office, and no new form for a disagreement at the foot of a sheet. No House, no seat, no office and no person from the antagonist ladder named beyond what the closed page already carries. No romance and nothing implying one. **No number added, and the numbers this pass removed are the substance of two of its findings: an invented count of four on a shelf, and a set of hours claimed for a chapter whose clock the base fixes.** The count of things asked out loud does not move, and **none of the twenty-seven replacement lines contains a question, a question mark, an asking, a request for information, or a sentence reporting what a person wants out of an answer.** No floor material in any added line — the screen refused `brick` on a scratch test before any chapter was opened. No bold marker and no quotation character in any added line. **The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not handed on and does not get a heading. The name at the end of a struck line is not printed. The guarantee is not printed in its own words and no child is named in it. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid, nobody is liable, and no chapter of this volume pays it. The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are not asked one question about a number. The girl of seventeen and the reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for. The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are walked zero times in this range.** **The room with the rail is not described at all, and no added line describes a copy in the same words twice and no added line describes a line cut into a printed strip in the same words in two chapters.** **No two of the three people the state layer keeps apart are in one room in any chapter of this volume, and no chapter states or denies a distance between any two of them.** **The woman who did nine minutes of work on a box stays dead.**

**Five patterns were run against the twenty-seven replacement lines and every one that fired was a denial:** the `that`-bigram screen fired nine times and all nine lines were rewritten before they reached the disk; the floor-material screen, the question-mark screen, the bold screen and the quotation screen each fired zero times on the lines as finally written.

1. **`chapter-0465.md:39`, a stray closing quotation character in the base**, one character, making the file's quote count odd and every quote-pairing instrument on it wrong from that line on. Carried forward from item 241. Base text, and the 0-deletion gate forbids a repair to edit it.
2. **67 of the 620 files carry an odd total quote count**, of which one is in this range. Volume 03 alone carries twenty-eight. No instrument here watches for it.
3. **`chapter-0482.md`'s added paragraph says the bright place before the lamp is the one she walks to, where base `:51` says she goes to *that doorway* and base `:49` and `:55` say *the frame*.** Item 241 carried the question of whether the frame and the doorway are one thing and this pass does not settle it: the revoicing names neither, so the question stands exactly as it stood.
4. **`m.longest_lift` grows a run by intersecting overlapping five-gram holder sets and its docstring's claim that the answer is always a run that exists whole in one chapter is false.** Three hits on this range were wrong. `tools/measure.py` was not edited and every earlier `lifts` figure recorded in this repair is an upper bound on that account.
5. **The six-word lift floor has no discriminating power on this manuscript.** 147 single-holder coincidences on this range's added prose, all of them the volume's own stock connectives.
6. **Item 232's prose figure of 428 quoted spans against its own table's 429**, corrected forward at item 241 and left standing there.

## Three: the guards built before the disk, and the fourteen defects they found

**Two guards had to be built, because the standing instruments cannot see this class by construction.** `lifts` excludes the range under repair from its own index, the intra-file scan is one file at a time, and the twelve-word index cannot see a run whose only holders are inside the range — **none of the three can find a paragraph the repair wrote twice, and none of the three can see a contradiction.** Two guards were therefore built and both were run **before** any candidate reached the disk.

1. **A screening guard** that takes a candidate line and rejects it if it carries a run of **eight words or over** held anywhere in the base prose of the whole manuscript, or a run of eight or over held by any other added line, or a date-line n-gram of eight or over, or a sweep bigram, or any of the twenty-five construction forms, or a figure token absent from the base of its own file, or an Arabic numeral, or a question mark, or a bold marker, or a quotation mark, or a neighbour-restatement overlap at or above 0.55.
2. **A number-word scan** over the added prose checking every figure token against the base of its own file and against the base of the whole volume, because the last repair's claim that its added paragraphs carried no numeral and no number word was a claim and had to be run.

**The screening guard rejected twenty-four candidates across four rounds before this pass wrote a single line, and every rejection was a real defect in a candidate and not a false positive.** The rejections were: **eleven eight-or-nine-word runs held by base prose elsewhere in the manuscript** — *going to be the one who rules one* (9w), *a party and a party is a person* (8w), *and there is nobody in the room to* (8w), *about four hundred and thirty miles of river* (8w), *fifteen of them were put there by somebody* (8w), *on a day he is not paid for* (8w), *in this empire has a place to put* (8w), *the eleven books have been on that shelf* (8w), *a column and a column wants a heading* (8w), *the fourth thing on the board is a* (8w), *and there has never been a column on* (8w); **three sweep bigrams** — *those rooms*, *those fifteen*, *that shelf*; **one figure token absent from its own file's base** — *second* at `chapter-0345.md:15`; and **two clause endings that collided with base**. **This is item 221's standing observed for the eleventh time in this repair, and it is the reason the guard runs before the disk and not after: every one of those twenty-four would have become a defect on the page.**

**The fourteen defects taken out, in a table with which instrument found each and why the standing instrument could not.**

Base `:3` fixes the window as *a window about two feet wide that has had no pane in it for about four years*, base `:59` and `:65` fix it as out for about four years, and eight chapters fix it at about four years; base `:9` and `:47` fix his nineteen years at the foot of a sheet. **Since before he came is at least nineteen years, so the line cannot be true and the base is not in doubt.** | reading, against a grep of every *pane* line in the volume's base | **a contradiction shares no run with the line it contradicts.** The longest shared token run with base `:3` is **zero**, so `reprints`, the twelve-word index and `lifts` all return nothing and always will |

**All fourteen were revoiced in place, 1 for 1, so no line number in the manuscript moved.** Each replacement was screened by the guard above *before* it was written, and the landed result is verified in the next section.

**Three faults of this pass's own, recorded because each returned a wrong answer before it was corrected.**

- **A number-word scan split hyphenated compounds into their numeric parts** and so reported `thirty-four` and `fifty-five` as absent from files that carry both as single `m.TOKEN` tokens. It returned **five apparent canon defects** at `chapter-0324.md:15`, `chapter-0325.md:33`, `chapter-0346.md:15`, `chapter-0346.md:57` and `chapter-0348.md:31`. **All five were this pass's bug and not defects**, and on the corrected scan the range returns **0 figure tokens absent from the base of their own file and 0 absent from the base of the whole volume**. The lesson is item 244's: a hyphenated compound is one token and testing its halves tests two words that need not exist.
- **A restatement guard scored only the nearer neighbour paragraph** and therefore returned **1.00** for `chapter-0318.md:73`, whose base neighbour above is the three-word line *Nobody thanked her.*, while the paragraph it does re-perform is the long one **below** it. The guard was extended to score both neighbours, and on that reading the range's count at or above 0.55 falls from 24 to 22.
- **The extractor that reads the repair's own added lines was reading them from `HEAD` rather than from the working tree**, so the number scan, the fixture scan, the lock scan and the restatement guard all reported on **stale text** after the fourteen edits had landed. It was corrected, the added lines re-extracted from the tree, and all four re-run; the figures in this record are from the corrected runs and the stale figures were not printed anywhere.

### Four of the sweep's 1,211 instances are artefacts of tokenisation at a sentence boundary

The sweep is counted on the `m.TOKEN` output, which drops punctuation, and **that is why it exceeds the raw-text reading by exactly four.** The four are a demonstrative ending a sentence followed by a word beginning the next: `that. His hand` at `chapter-0463.md`, `that. About nine hundred` at `chapter-0483.md`, `that. Put that man` at `chapter-0493.md`, `that. Ruling one` at `chapter-0494.md`, which tokenise to `that his`, `that about`, `that put` and `that ruling`. **`that his` is not an anaphora construction at all**, and the form count of 201 is 200 plus it. This does not move the flatness, which is before-equals-now on every reading tried, and it is printed because a figure with an undisclosed method behind it is how this repository got a set of numbers that reproduced under none.
