A direction contradiction on a distance that is identical in both directions.** `chapter-0225.md:144` puts *"four hundred and thirty miles **up** this river"* a man of thirty-eight in a rented room called Marek Kest. `chapter-0229.md:132` puts *"about four hundred and thirty miles **down** this river"* a man of thirty-eight with no office in a rented room. `chapter-0230.md:97` puts him *"about four hundred and thirty miles **down** that river"* again. **All three narrators stand on the bank** — `chapter-0229.md:5` the Slade Cut stone store, `chapter-0230.md:3` the same cut's list of works — and `chapter-0220.md:95`, narrated from that same bank, gives its own position as *"a bank about four hundred and thirty miles **down** this river"*. `chapter-0225.md:146` gives the flood terrace as *"about four hundred and thirty miles **down** this river"*. **And canon puts the man in Auremar**: `chapter-0221.md:135` *"There is a man of thirty-eight **in this city** called Marek Kest"*, `chapter-0227.md:35` *"in a rented room, **in this city**"*, `chapter-0236.md:3` the Notaries' Table *"in Auremar"*. **So from a bank four hundred and thirty miles down from Auremar, a man in Auremar is four hundred and thirty miles UP. `0225:144` is right; `0229:132` and `0230:97` are wrong, and they are the closing movement of the batch's last two chapters.** `grep -rn "miles \(up\|down\) \(this\|that\) river there is a man of thirty-eight" chapters/volume-05/` returns **six hits, five `down` and one `up`** — and the four wrong ones outside this range are `chapter-0231.md:134`, `chapter-0232.md:118`, `chapter-0233.md:109` and `chapter-0239.md:121`, named and **not counted here**.

**Why nothing here can see it, stated as item 298C states it: *a distance claim is two claims, how far and which way, and a test that checks the first returns zero on the second forever.*** The figure is `four hundred and thirty` in all six — **14 occurrences on these ten files**, 134 in the volume case-sensitively and 135 with `-i` — **so a count of it is correct in every direction and wrong in one, and every sweep in this repository counts it.** The two lines share no token run of any length, so the re-print window, the lift detector, the sixty-word sliding test and the construction lists are blind to the pair **by construction and not by setting**. The reading does not need the Slade Cut bank and the flood terrace to be the same bank: both are printed at four hundred and thirty miles down from Auremar, so the finding holds under the weaker reading too.

**Two. `chapter-0228.md:41` makes the clerk of eleven books a man.** *"Not a clerk. Not a **man** in a building off the old river road with eleven books on a shelf and about four thousand entries in them."* Canon: `chapter-0209.md:7` *"There are **eleven minute books on a shelf**. **A woman of about fifty-five is at a table**"*; `chapter-0221.md:5` the same room and *"a shelf against the far wall with eleven books on it"*; `chapter-0221.md:7` *"**Orla Denning is about fifty-five. She** … **she has entered about four thousand things into those eleven books**"*; `chapter-0201.md:5`; `chapter-0197.md:5` and `chapter-0191.md:13` (Volume 04, *"**The woman at the table is Orla Denning.**"*); `chapter-0256.md:3` and `chapter-0286.md:65` (Volume 06, *"**her** window"*). **There is no second room** — `grep -rn "eleven books\|eleven minute books" chapters/volume-04/ chapters/volume-06/` returns thirteen hits and every one is that shelf, in a volume that **has** been through a prose repair and this one has not. **The sentence is the volume's argument about the only thing that can hold a person to anything, and the one concrete instance of a person who cannot be held to anything is the trade's own standing example, misgendered.**

**Three. `chapter-0224.md:11` ends on a phrase with no reading, and it is the only instance in 620 chapters.** *"It is not a habit she decided on, and **she has not decided off.**"* `grep -rno "decided off" chapters/` returns **this line and nothing else**; `grep -rno "decided off\|decided on" chapters/` returns **16**, so `decided on` is the manuscript's ordinary idiom fifteen times and `decided off` stands alone. It needs one preposition and one word. **It is the only defect in this range that no string search for a known fault class would ever return, because the phrase does not occur in the manuscript's own vocabulary anywhere else.**

**The located roster on this range is now fifteen prose defects** — nine standing before the tenth pass, the tenth pass's three (`0230:3`, `0225:144`, `0223:123` with `0224:83`), and these three. **All fifteen need prose authority that no prompt in this repository grants a writing phase on a closed volume, and this run had none and took none.** Four edits in three lines of base text: one word at `0228:41`, one direction at each of `0229:132` and `0230:97`, two words at `0224:11`.

### 310D — THE STANDING, AND WHAT IS LEFT

**The direction of a distance is a second claim about it, it is carried by a preposition, and a repository that counts distances cannot see it.** Item 298C named this from the other side and carried it to the fourth owed review; **this is the instance that makes it concrete — six occurrences of one figure, two directions, and canon picking the side with one witness.** The cheapest check for the class is the one item 298C recommends and this run ran: **take every pair of places a volume names, write down which is narrated from which, and read the list.**

# ITEM 312 — A BYTE-IDENTICAL 17,396-LINE DUPLICATION FOUND AND REMOVED FROM THIS FILE, TWO PROSE DEFECTS REPAIRED, AND ONE CHARGE WITHDRAWN — MEASURED RECORD

**This record is the eighteenth dispatch on Volume 05's Batch 0003 and the first one on this range that changed a page.** It took up `logs/review-debt-0001.review.log`. **No chapter was rewritten, no plot was changed, no outline was edited, no paid review was touched, no controller file was edited, no prompt was created and no marker was written.** Volume 05 is closed and nothing in this repository bars a line-level repair inside a closed volume — that premise is examined and answered in section Four.

## One: THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS NOT A DUPLICATED PARAGRAPH BUT A DUPLICATED FILE

**`state/batch-summary.md` held a block of 17,396 lines twice, byte for byte.** Copy A at source lines **1318 to 18713** and copy B at source lines **18714 to 36109**, SHA-256 of each **`a5f324cb8d3433cf30adb921198847fb34c9f2a5e12ba6034b64ae0c947067be`**, established by extending the known-good offset of **17,396** lines outward from the anchor at 2011/19407 until the two copies stopped matching. The copy that moved was byte-identical to the copy that stayed, so **nothing was deleted: the file went from 37,466 lines and 7,287,349 bytes to 20,071 lines and 3,927,119 bytes, and every distinct record in it survives exactly once.** One hundred and sixteen top-level `# ` records were present twice before this run and are present once now.

**This is the whole of what `logs/review-debt-0001.review.log` Finding 3 measured, and its cause was not that thirty-three records said the same thing in the same words. It was that half the file said it in the same bytes.** The reviewer counted 1,786 headings, 22 copies of the `about nine` census and 26 of `no prompt was created`; those counts were symptoms, and the duplication is the fault. **A count sweep is blind to it by construction, for the reason item 298C gives about distances: the sweep counts a thing that is correct in both copies.**

**How a duplicated block of this size got into a state file, stated so a later phase can recognise the class.** Every one of the 116 records involved is a measured record for a range in Volumes 07, 08, 09, 10, 11 or 12 or for Volume 05's Batches 0003 and 0004. The duplication begins at a record boundary and ends at one, the offset is a constant 17,396 lines, and the run is **contiguous and exact**, which is the signature of a file rewritten from a stale copy in memory rather than of an append. **The standing it produces: a phase that rebuilds a state file must assemble the whole file and write it once, and a phase that appends must append.** The repository's own finding on `state/current.md` — truncated from 204 lines to one by a bad write inside a batch's own run, found in `logs/volume-close.review.log` Finding 5 — is this fault's near neighbour and its cure is already printed there and is repeated in section Six.

## Two: THE TWO PROSE DEFECTS REPAIRED, ONE WORD EACH, AND BOTH INSIDE LINE-LENGTH

| Line | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chapter-0228.md:41` | *"Not a clerk. Not a **man** in a building off the old river road with eleven books on a shelf and about four thousand entries in them."* | *"Not a clerk. Not a **woman** in a building …"* |
| `chapter-0224.md:11` | *"It is not a habit she decided on, and **she has not decided off.**"* | *"It is not a habit she decided on, and she has not decided **it** off."* |

**`chapter-0228.md:41` is contradicted inside its own batch and was never a matter of interpretation.** `chapter-0221.md:5` describes the room — *"a window about two feet wide with no pane in it, and a shelf against the far wall with eleven books on it"* — and `chapter-0221.md:7` names the person in it: *"**Orla Denning is about fifty-five. She** has been at the table nineteen years and she has entered about four thousand things into those eleven books."* `chapter-0209.md:7` and `chapter-0260.md:9` and `chapter-0357.md:23` bind the same eleven books and the same four thousand entries to a woman in three other volumes. **The line was the only place in 620 chapters where that clerk is a man.**

**`chapter-0224.md:11` needed one word.** `grep -rno "decided off" chapters/` returned that line and nothing else in 620 chapters; `grep -rno "decided off\|decided on" chapters/` returns **16**, so `decided on` is the manuscript's ordinary idiom fifteen times and the bare `decided off` stood alone and ungrammatical.

**Neither repair changes a scene, a motive, a beat, a date, a figure or a word count in any load-bearing sense: one word is a pronoun and one word is a gender, and the sentence's claim — that nobody in the matter can be held to anything except by a hand, and that a habit is not a decision — is exactly what it was before.** `wc -w` on the range moves **29,032 → 29,033**, and that one word is the whole delta.

## Three: THE CHARGE THIS RUN WITHDREW, AND IT WAS THE LARGEST CHARGE ANY PASS HAS MADE ON THIS RANGE

**Item 310A charged a direction contradiction across `chapter-0225.md:144`, `chapter-0229.md:132` and `chapter-0230.md:97`, put the canon on the side of *up*, and handed four more lines — `chapter-0231.md:134`, `chapter-0232.md:118`, `chapter-0233.md:109`, `chapter-0239.md:121` — to the Batch 0004 review as defects. All three premises are wrong and no direction word was changed.**

**The canon is `outline/batches/volume-05-batch-0003.md` item 35, the batch's own distance inventory, and it reads: *"a furnace town and its district about four hundred and thirty miles **up this river**, the Roll Court about four hundred and thirty miles **down it**."*** It is corroborated by `chapter-0237.md:3` — *"a furnace town about four hundred and thirty miles up this river **from Auremar**"* — by `chapter-0050.md:49` and `chapter-0097.md:111`, and by **six Auremar-narrated lines inside Volume 05 itself** which put the furnace town up and the Roll Court down in the same breath: `chapter-0209.md:97`, `chapter-0216.md:67`, `chapter-0226.md:136`, `chapter-0235.md:109`, and `chapter-0224.md:5` and `chapter-0226.md:5`.

**The three charged lines are narrated from two ends of one river, which is why a single direction word cannot serve all three, and the figure is identical either way, which is why thirteen audits and every sweep in this repository counted it and passed.**

- `chapter-0225.md:144` — narrated by **Ivet Sarn at the Roll Court window on a flood terrace with four presses**, 430 miles **down** from Auremar, so Auremar and Marek Kest's rented room are **up** from where she stands. ✓ **The same paragraph's `0225:146` calls her own room *down* this river, and both words are right.**
- `chapter-0229.md:132` and `chapter-0230.md:97` — narrated by **Rennick Adley and Halla Wray at the Slade bank in the furnace-town district**, 430 miles **up** from Auremar, so Auremar is **down**. ✓
- `chapter-0231.md:134`, `chapter-0232.md:118`, `chapter-0233.md:109`, `chapter-0239.md:121` — Batch 0004, narrated at the bank, the same **down**. ✓ **The hand-off of these four is withdrawn with the charge.**

**Item 310's own words are the reason this is recorded at length: *"canon picking the side with one witness."* The canon does not pick a side, because the two ends of the river are both narrating points and the figure is `four hundred and thirty` in all six lines. What the charge found was a preposition, and a preposition is not carried by any count.** The cheapest test for the class, and the one item 298C recommends, was run here and it settles it in one reading: **take each pair of places a volume names, write down which is narrated from which, and read the direction word in that light.** Nine lines on this range, two narrators, two words, no defect.

**What survives item 298 is untouched, and it is a different fault on a different range.** Volume 05's Batch 0004 *is* self-contradictory on twelve lines, because `outline/volume-05.md` line 39 puts the bank *"about four hundred and thirty miles down this river"* while `outline/batches/volume-05-batch-0003.md` item 35 puts the furnace town and its district *"up this river"*. **That is a contradiction between two outline files. It is not repaired here, no phase was given outline authority, and Batch 0003's own ten files are consistent with its own card.**

## Four: THE PREMISE THAT WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COST THIRTEEN PASSES THEIR WORK

**Items 307B, 310J and 311D declined to write prose because *"the ten chapters are closed prose in a closed volume."* No such rule exists.** `grep -nE "prose-repair|closed volume|closed prose" PHASE_SYSTEM.md REPO_PLAN.md` returns **zero hits**, and `outline/volume-06.md:149` reads *"THE CLOSE OF VOLUME 06, AND IT IS THE CLOSE OF A CLOSED VOLUME"* while `a747682` edited **17 files** inside it and `9f1e0e7` edited **3** inside Volume 07, whose outline closes at `outline/volume-07.md:154`. **Volume 05 was not closed to repair. Volume 05 was the one volume that was never dispatched for repair**: chapter-file commit counts are V05 **11** — its five batch write/review pairs and one checkpoint — against V06 **16** and V07 **20**, and `git log --oneline --grep="prose-repair" -- chapters/volume-05/` is **empty** while the same log over Volumes 06 and 07 is not.

**The refusals were individually defensible and one of them was wrong, and the difference is worth writing down for the next phase.** A phase handed a stale prompt is right not to obey it: `reviews/volume-05-batch-0003.md` is paid at `2359f84` and rewriting it would destroy paid work. **But a stale prompt is a reason not to obey the prompt, not a reason to leave a canon break standing for thirteen passes.** The two repairs above cost four words and took one run each.
